lines.index: #section:Elwynn Forest.
lines.text: Elwynn Forest.
lines.title: Elwynn Forest

lines.index: #section:Elwynn Forest is the green heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Its oaks crowd close about the white walls of the capital, and between them lie quiet lakes, golden fields and old mines that have fed the kingdom for generations. To the folk of Stormwind, Elwynn has always been the safest place in the world. That belief is now wearing thin. Wolves prowl nearer the farms each season, strange things stir in the mines, and the roads that once knew only merchants and pilgrims now know thieves.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records the year when the first humans settled Elwynn. What is known is that the forest was claimed many centuries before the Dark Portal opened. When the ancient empire of Arathor ended its long unity, bold families of the Arathi bloodline travelled south in search of new lands. Among the rich woods and rivers they found there, they raised a kingdom they named Azeroth, and at its heart a city called Stormwind. Elwynn became the realm's granary and its garden. North of the city, the clerics of Northshire Abbey tended the faith of the Holy Light, and their abbey became one of its oldest homes in the south.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Elwynn has regrown from the ashes of war, but it is poorly guarded. King Varian Wrynn has vanished, and none can say where he has gone. In his absence, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon rules as regent, and the strength of the realm is spread thin across a dozen troubled borders. Kobolds have seized the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines. Riverpaw gnolls raid across the southern border. Bandits of the Defias Brotherhood prey upon the farmsteads near Westfall. The few marshals of Goldshire can no longer hold the forest alone, and they welcome any sword willing to serve.

lines.title: The Present Day

lines.index: #section:• The people of Stormwind. Farmers, the loggers of Eastvale and the miners of the hills remain because the land is good, and because they have nowhere else to go. • The clergy and recruits of Northshire. At the abbey, priests and paladins train the young men and women who will defend the kingdom. • Kobolds. They burrow in the mines. They fear the dark above all things and guard their candles with savage devotion. • The Riverpaw gnolls. They come down from the southern hills and from Redridge, hungry for food and plunder. • The Defias Brotherhood. Their ranks began with men who once rebuilt Stormwind, and who now take by the knife what they believe the crown still owes them. • Murlocs. The murloc tribes haunt the shores of Crystal Lake and Stone Cairn Lake, as they have for as long as anyone can remember.

lines.title: Inhabitants

lines.index: #section:• The Long Peace. For generations Elwynn knew little but harvest and festival. Its villages grew rich on the trade that flowed through Stormwind. • The First War. Then the orcish Horde came through the Dark Portal, and the lands of Azeroth were the first to burn. In the First War, the Horde put Elwynn's farms and forests to the torch, and even the sacred halls of Northshire Abbey did not escape the flames. At last Stormwind itself was sacked, and King Llane Wrynn was slain within his own keep. Sir Anduin Lothar led the survivors north across the sea to Lordaeron, and with them went the king's young son, Varian. • The Return. After the Second War, the exiles came home. They replanted the forest and rebuilt the villages. The Stonemasons' Guild, led by Edwin VanCleef, raised Stormwind anew from its rubble. When the House of Nobles refused to pay the masons for their labor, the masons rioted in the streets. Queen Tiffin Wrynn was among those who died in the chaos. The masons were driven from the city, and from their bitterness the Defias Brotherhood was born. • The Present Day. Now the king is gone, the armies are far away, and Elwynn waits on the courage of a handful of marshals and volunteers.

lines.title: History

lines.index: #section:• Among the kobolds of Elwynn, no crime is greater than stealing a candle. Every miner who has worked below knows the cry that follows such a theft. • The Maclure and Stonefield families have feuded across the same fence for longer than either can remember. Yet the whispers of Goldshire say that a Maclure daughter and a Stonefield son meet in secret when the fields are dark. • The Tower of Azora rises in the east of the forest. It is the home of a mage whose studies the common folk of Elwynn neither understand nor care to ask about. • The farmers of the south speak of Hogger in low voices. He is a gnoll so large and cunning that the bounty on his head has gone unclaimed through many seasons.

lines.index: #section:Northshire Abbey.
lines.text: Northshire Abbey.
lines.title: Northshire Abbey

lines.index: #section:Northshire Abbey stands at the head of a sheltered valley north of Stormwind. For centuries it has been a house of the Holy Light, where clerics prayed, healed and kept the old books of their faith. It was here that the young Medivh lay for years in a sleep no healer could break, tended by the brothers of the abbey. In the First War the Horde burned it, but the faithful returned and raised its walls again. Today it is a training ground. Recruits come to learn the sword, the spell and the prayer before they are sent out into a forest that needs them.

lines.index: #section:Goldshire.
lines.text: Goldshire.
lines.title: Goldshire

lines.index: #section:Goldshire is the crossroads of Elwynn. Its roads run north to the abbey, south to the farms, east to the logging camps and west toward Westfall. At its heart stands the Lion's Pride Inn, where the Farley family has poured ale for travellers for as long as the town's oldest folk can remember. The town has a smith, a stable and an apothecary. It is also the post of Marshal Dughan, whose few soldiers must answer for the safety of the whole forest.

lines.index: #section:Fargodeep Mine.
lines.text: Fargodeep Mine.
lines.title: Fargodeep Mine

lines.index: #section:Fargodeep was once a gold mine of the crown. It lies in the southern hills of Elwynn, between the lands of the Stonefields and the Maclures. When the miners left it, the Kobolds came. Now its tunnels flicker with the candles of a kobold warren, and it is said that the kobold Goldtooth hoards stolen treasures in its depths. Whatever the kobolds are digging toward, they are digging with a will.

lines.text: Jasperlode Mine.
lines.title: Jasperlode Mine

lines.index: #section:Jasperlode Mine lies in the eastern hills, north of the Tower of Azora. It was one of the mines that fed the forges of Stormwind. Kobolds now hold its upper tunnels. Deeper still, where even the kobolds do not willingly go, great mine spiders spin their webs in the dark. The miners who fled Jasperlode speak of the spiders more than of the kobolds.

lines.index: #section:Tower of Azora.
lines.text: Tower of Azora.
lines.title: Tower of Azora

lines.index: #section:The Tower of Azora rises above the eastern woods of Elwynn. It is the seat of the mage Theocritus and of the gnomes who serve him. From its highest chamber, a scrying device called the Eye of Azora looks far to the east, toward the Tower of Ilgalar in Redridge. There dwells the warlock Morganth, whose dark studies Theocritus has sworn to watch and to thwart. The folk of the forest keep their distance from both towers.

lines.text: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch.
lines.title: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch

lines.index: #section:The Brackwell farm lies in the south-east of Elwynn, where once a family grew pumpkins famous across the forest. The Brackwells are gone, and no one can say what became of them. The Defias Brotherhood holds the farm now. Gold taken from the kobold mines is said to pass through it on its way to a Defias agent called the Collector. Only one Brackwell treasure remains: Princess, their prize sow, who has grown enormous on the vegetables of her neighbours.

lines.index: #section:Eastvale Logging Camp.
lines.text: Eastvale Logging Camp.
lines.title: Eastvale Logging Camp

lines.index: #section:Eastvale is the lumber camp of Elwynn, at the forest's eastern edge near the road to Redridge. Its loggers supply the timber that rebuilt Stormwind, and they still send wagons west every season. The camp lives under constant threat from wolves and bears. Guard Thomas holds the bridge to the west, and the old manor of Marshal Haggard stands nearby.

lines.index: #section:Stone Cairn Lake.
lines.text: Stone Cairn Lake.
lines.title: Stone Cairn Lake

lines.index: #section:Stone Cairn Lake is a ring of water around a wooded island in the north-east of the forest. On its shore stands Heroes' Vigil, where a cairn of stones remembers the men and women of Goldshire and its farms who died in the First War. It is a place of mourning. It is no longer a place of peace: renegade wizards have taken the island, and murlocs hunt along the southern shore.

lines.index: #section:Maclure Vineyards and Stonefield Farm.
lines.text: Maclure Vineyards and Stonefield Farm.
lines.title: Maclure Vineyards and Stonefield Farm

lines.index: #section:In the south of Elwynn, two farms sit on either side of a narrow stretch of land. To the east grow the vines of the Maclures. To the west stand the fields and house of the Stonefields. The two families have been at war for longer than any of their children can remember, and the cause is long buried beneath insults, stolen goods and slammed doors. Yet between the vineyard and the farm runs a quiet path, and not everyone who walks it walks there in anger.

lines.index: #section:Crystal Lake.
lines.text: Crystal Lake.
lines.title: Crystal Lake

lines.index: #section:Crystal Lake lies east of Goldshire, still and clear as its name. Its waters feed a rare kelp that glitters like glass, prized by apothecaries for its strange properties. The murlocs of the lake guard it jealously. Fishermen who once cast their nets here now keep to the far shore.

lines.text: Westbrook Garrison.
lines.title: Westbrook Garrison

lines.index: #section:Westbrook Garrison guards the western edge of Elwynn, where the forest gives way to the fields of Westfall. Its barracks were built to keep the peace of the border. They now struggle to keep anything at all. Thieves come from the west, and the Riverpaw gnolls of Forest's Edge raid from the south. On the garrison's notice board hangs a poster that every soldier knows by heart: a reward for the head of Hogger.

lines.title: Marshal McBride

lines.index: #section:Marshal Douglas McBride commands the recruits of Northshire Abbey. Each new defender of Stormwind passes first through his hands. He must turn farmers' sons and clerks' daughters into soldiers, and he must do it with the kingdom's army far away and the valley itself under threat.

lines.index: #section:Milly Osworth owns the vineyards of Northshire. Her grapes supply the abbey's cellar, and she has always been proud of them. Now thieves in red bandanas have taken over her vines, and her crates of grapes sit unguarded among them.

lines.index: #section:Milly shows the price of Stormwind's thin defenses. Even the vineyard beside a holy abbey is no longer safe from theft.

lines.index: #section:Marshal Dughan. Marshal of Goldshire.
lines.text: Marshal Dughan. Marshal of Goldshire.
lines.title: Marshal Dughan

lines.index: #section:From the crossroads town of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan commands the defense of Elwynn Forest. His soldiers are too few for the task. Yet he must keep open the roads that bind the capital to its farms, its mills and its mines. Every recruit who leaves Northshire Abbey passes through his hands, and he sends each one wherever the forest bleeds worst.
lines.text: From the crossroads town of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan commands the defense of Elwynn Forest. His soldiers are too few for the task. Yet he must keep open the roads that bind the capital to its farms, its mills and its mines. Every recruit who leaves Northshire Abbey passes through his hands, and he sends each one wherever the forest bleeds worst.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Dughan is the face of a kingdom stretched to its limit. Stormwind has no king in the throne, no army near at hand, and only the loyalty of ordinary men and women to keep its peace. He does not complain of this. He simply does the work that remains.
lines.text: Dughan is the face of a kingdom stretched to its limit. Stormwind has no king in the throne, no army near at hand, and only the loyalty of ordinary men and women to keep its peace. He does not complain of this. He simply does the work that remains.
lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He holds Elwynn with a handful of soldiers, spread between Goldshire, Westbrook Garrison and Eastvale. • He sends scouts into the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines, where the kobolds grow bolder each day. • He places a bounty on the gnoll Hogger and on the Riverpaw raiders of the southern border. • He sends what aid he can to the forest's outlying posts, though he rarely has any to spare.

lines.index: #section:The Recruits of Northshire. The recruits arrive bearing letters from Marshal McBride. Dughan has little time to greet them, for kobolds hold the mines, gnolls prowl the border and thieves haunt every road. He puts each newcomer to work within the hour.

lines.title: The Recruits of Northshire

lines.index: #section:Beneath the Hills. The reports from Fargodeep and Jasperlode confirm what Dughan has feared. The kobolds are no longer a nuisance to be driven out with torches. They are spreading, and they are digging deeper than any honest miner ever dared.

lines.index: #section:The Southern Border. For a long time the tales of Hogger were told as fireside stories. Dughan stopped treating them as stories when the dead began to come home from the southern farms.

lines.title: The Southern Border

lines.index: #section:The Collector. The gold dust stolen from the mines does not stay with the kobolds. It travels by hidden roads to a Defias agent known only as the Collector. When the Collector's ring is found, it bears the mark of the old Stonemasons' Guild of Stormwind. Dughan understands then that the thieves of Elwynn are no common bandits. They are the masons whom Stormwind betrayed.

lines.index: #section:Deputy Rainer holds Westbrook Garrison at the western edge of Elwynn. He does not hide his bitterness. The army was sent abroad, he says, and the garrison was left to fend for itself against gnolls from the south and thieves from the west.

lines.title: Remy "Two Times"

lines.index: #section:Remy is a merchant from Redridge who does his trade in Goldshire. He has a curious habit of repeating the end of everything he says, which has earned him his name. He buys what others will not ask about, and he always seems to know someone who can pay.

lines.index: #section:Remy hears everything that passes through Goldshire. What he hears, he sells, and sometimes he passes it on for free.

lines.index: #section:Marshal Haggard. Retired Marshal of Stormwind.
lines.text: Marshal Haggard. Retired Marshal of Stormwind.
lines.title: Marshal Haggard

lines.index: #section:Marshal Haggard served Stormwind for many years before he retired to a manor near Eastvale. His eyes have grown dim with age, but his pride has not. He still keeps the badge of his office, and he still knows old tales that younger soldiers have forgotten.
lines.text: Marshal Haggard served Stormwind for many years before he retired to a manor near Eastvale. His eyes have grown dim with age, but his pride has not. He still keeps the badge of his office, and he still knows old tales that younger soldiers have forgotten.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Haggard is a living memory of the old Stormwind. His house also holds the first thread of a darker tale, one that leads east into Duskwood.
lines.text: Haggard is a living memory of the old Stormwind. His house also holds the first thread of a darker tale, one that leads east into Duskwood.
lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He served as a marshal of Stormwind until his retirement. • He knows the old tale of a man called Stalvan, a tale that begins with a sealed crate found in the canals of Stormwind.
lines.text: • He served as a marshal of Stormwind until his retirement. • He knows the old tale of a man called Stalvan, a tale that begins with a sealed crate found in the canals of Stormwind.

lines.index: #section:The Thief in the Dark. One night a man in a Stormwind tabard came to Haggard's door. In the dark, the old marshal took him for Dughan and handed over his badge. The visitor was no marshal. He was a Defias thief called Dead-tooth Jack, and he vanished with the badge before dawn.
lines.text: The Thief in the Dark. One night a man in a Stormwind tabard came to Haggard's door. In the dark, the old marshal took him for Dughan and handed over his badge. The visitor was no marshal. He was a Defias thief called Dead-tooth Jack, and he vanished with the badge before dawn.

lines.index: #section:The Sealed Crate. A sealed crate, long forgotten in the canals of Stormwind, held papers that pointed to Marshal Haggard. When they reached him, the old marshal recognized the name they spoke of. It began a story he would rather not remember: the legend of Stalvan Mistmantle, a name still whispered with dread in Duskwood.

lines.text: Guard Thomas. Guard of the Eastvale Bridge.
lines.title: Guard Thomas

lines.index: #section:Guard Thomas holds the bridge on the road to Eastvale. He has lost men to the wild beasts of the eastern woods, and he fears he will lose more. He watches the road, counts the wolves, and sends his reports to Goldshire with growing alarm.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Thomas's post shows how far Stormwind's peace has frayed. He believes the fighting will reach Goldshire itself before long.
lines.text: Thomas's post shows how far Stormwind's peace has frayed. He believes the fighting will reach Goldshire itself before long.
lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He sends searchers to find two of his guards who never returned. • He posts bounties on the murlocs of the lakes and on the wolves and bears of Eastvale. • He warns Marshal Dughan that the fighting draws near.

lines.index: #section:The Lost Guards. Two of Thomas's guards went out and did not come back. One was found half-eaten in the woods. The other, Footman Rolf Hartford, was found dead among the murlocs by the lake. Thomas wrote their names in his report and asked, once more, for soldiers who never came.

lines.text: Theocritus. High Mage of the Tower of Azora.
lines.title: Theocritus

lines.index: #section:Theocritus is the master of the Tower of Azora. He is a mage of great learning and little patience, served by gnomes who tend his instruments. His greatest concern lies far to the east: the warlock Morganth, who dwells in the Tower of Ilgalar in Redridge.

lines.index: #section:Theocritus is one of the few who watch the dark powers gathering beyond Elwynn's borders. While the marshals guard the roads, he guards against what cannot be fought with swords.

lines.index: #section:• He watches Morganth through the scrying Eye of Azora. • He seeks to thwart Morganth's hunt for an ancient relic called the Scythe of Elune.

lines.text: Maybell Maclure. Daughter of the Maclures.
lines.title: Maybell Maclure

lines.index: #section:Maybell is the daughter of the Maclure family. Her heart belongs to Tommy Joe Stonefield, the son of the family her own kin have hated for generations. She will not give him up, and she will not wait for the feud to end on its own.

lines.index: #section:In a forest full of fear, Maybell's story is a small and stubborn act of hope.
lines.text: In a forest full of fear, Maybell's story is a small and stubborn act of hope.

lines.index: #section:• She sends word to Tommy Joe across the fields that divide their families.

lines.text: Brother Paxton. Keeper of the Northshire Library.
lines.title: Brother Paxton

lines.index: #section:Brother Paxton is a priest of Northshire Abbey and the keeper of its small library. He has spent years gathering books on faith, history and the arts of magic. Now his shelves are emptying. The Kobolds of the Echo Ridge Mine have been stealing his books, and some they have tried to eat.

lines.index: #section:Paxton's loss is more than a scholar's grief. Among the stolen volumes are books of real power, and in the wrong claws they could do real harm.

lines.index: #section:Camping.
lines.text: Camping.
lines.title: Camping

lines.index: #section:Camping is the old art of the road: to build a fire in the wild, to share it, and to rest beside it before the journey goes on. Travellers across Azeroth have always known that a night by a good fire can mean the difference between reaching the next town and never reaching it at all.
lines.text: Camping is the old art of the road: to build a fire in the wild, to share it, and to rest beside it before the journey goes on. Travellers across Azeroth have always known that a night by a good fire can mean the difference between reaching the next town and never reaching it at all.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:A camp begins with a campfire, built by those who know the art of cooking. Other travellers may then add to it, each according to the craft they know. A smith sets up a sharpening wheel. A leatherworker raises a tent. An alchemist, an enchanter, a miner or a tailor each brings something of their own: a well of mana, an enchanted lute, a lodestone, a banner of their people. The greatest of these works are built from plans kept by the masters of each craft, and some of those plans are said to lie in the hands of dangerous foes.

lines.index: #section:Dun Morogh.
lines.text: Dun Morogh.
lines.title: Dun Morogh

lines.index: #section:Dun Morogh is a land of snow and stone in the west of Khaz Modan, the old homeland of the dwarves. Its peaks are the highest in the Eastern Kingdoms, and within the greatest of them lies Ironforge, the capital of the Kingdom of Ironforge. The gnomes once lived here too, in the city of Gnomeregan beneath the western hills. Between the two cities lie frozen lakes, pine woods and a single long road through the snow. It is a hard country, and its people are proud of it.
lines.text: Dun Morogh is a land of snow and stone in the west of Khaz Modan, the old homeland of the dwarves. Its peaks are the highest in the Eastern Kingdoms, and within the greatest of them lies Ironforge, the capital of the Kingdom of Ironforge. The gnomes once lived here too, in the city of Gnomeregan beneath the western hills. Between the two cities lie frozen lakes, pine woods and a single long road through the snow. It is a hard country, and its people are proud of it.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The dwarves say that they were shaped from the stone of these mountains in ages past, and that Ironforge is their oldest home. Long ago all dwarves were ruled from it by a single high king. When that king died, the Bronzebeard, Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans went to war for his throne, and the Bronzebeards kept the mountain. The gnomes came to be the dwarves' neighbors and friends, and they raised Gnomeregan in the western foothills. No chronicle records the year when either city was founded.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Dun Morogh is less safe than it has been in living memory. Much of the king's army is far away, serving the Alliance abroad, and the mountaineers who remain are few. The troggs have boiled up out of the deep places, and they now hold the Coldridge Pass and the pits of Gol'Bolar Quarry. The Frostmane trolls hold their caves and ridges in the west. Gnomeregan is lost, and its poisoned people wander before its gates. Wendigo have filled the Grizzled Den. Most troubling of all, spies of the Dark Iron clan have been seen in the east, carrying maps of tunnels that lead beneath Ironforge itself.

lines.title: The Present Day

lines.index: #section:• The dwarves of Ironforge. Miners, brewers, ram breeders and mountaineers, they live in Kharanos, Brewnall Village and the lonely camps of the high country. • The gnomes of Gnomeregan. The survivors of their fallen city shelter in Ironforge, and some work in Kharanos to undo the harm that was done. • The Frostmane trolls. They hold caves and ridges in the west and dispute the snows with the dwarves. • The troggs. The Rockjaw troggs rose from beneath the earth and now attack wherever the dwarves dig. • The wendigo and the beasts. Wendigo, bears, boars and snow leopards roam the hills, and some of them have grown too bold and too large. • The Dark Irons. A band of them holds Ironband's Compound in the east, watching and waiting.

lines.title: Inhabitants

lines.index: #section:• The Three Hammers. In the war of the three clans, the Bronzebeards held Ironforge and drove out their rivals. A treaty kept beneath the city records that the Wildhammers signed the peace, and the Dark Irons did not. • The Second War. When the Horde overran Khaz Modan, Ironforge itself held out. The dwarves joined the Alliance of Lordaeron and fought beside humankind until the Horde was broken. • The Fall of Gnomeregan. The troggs rose beneath the gnomish city. The gnomes fought to drive them out, but the weapon they used poisoned the city and many of their own. The survivors fled to Ironforge. • The Present Day. Now the dwarves face troggs, trolls and Dark Irons at once, with half their strength away at war.

lines.title: History

lines.index: #section:• The Thunderbrews of Kharanos and the Barleybrews of Brewnall Village are rival brewing families. Each believes the other's ale is fit only for boars. • The Frostmane trolls grow a pale herb called shimmerweed on the ridges above Iceflow Lake, and they use it in their rituals. The dwarves have found a better use for it: stout. • The mountaineers of Ironforge carve their names into the stocks of their rifles, so that the snow can be made to tell who it has taken. • Thieves in Ironforge whisper that the king's armored steam tanks carry ore and gems from Gol'Bolar Quarry by a strangely roundabout road, and that someone ought to relieve him of a little of it.

lines.index: #section:Coldridge Valley.
lines.text: Coldridge Valley.
lines.title: Coldridge Valley

lines.index: #section:Coldridge Valley is a sheltered vale in the south-west of Dun Morogh, closed in by mountains on every side. New defenders of Ironforge come here to learn their trade at Anvilmar. The valley has lost its peace. Rockjaw troggs overran the camp to the west and swarm the hills by the frozen lake. Frostmane trolls hold a cave in the south. The only road out, through the tunnel of Coldridge Pass, is now thick with troggs, and a mountaineer keeps watch at its mouth.

lines.text: Anvilmar.
lines.title: Anvilmar

lines.index: #section:Anvilmar is a dwelling dug deep into the mountainside at the head of Coldridge Valley. Here the trainers of Ironforge teach the young to fight, pray and work their craft, and outfitters give them warm clothing against the cold. It is also a refuge. Gnomes who fled the poison of Gnomeregan have found shelter within its halls, and some of them still count what they lost on the road.

lines.text: Kharanos.
lines.title: Kharanos

lines.index: #section:Kharanos is the chief town of Dun Morogh, a cluster of stone houses on the road between Coldridge and Ironforge. At its heart stands the Thunderbrew Distillery, famed across Khaz Modan, whose cellars are stacked high with barrels of Thunder Ale. The inn within is rarely quiet. Mountaineers report here, and Senir Whitebeard writes his reports for the Senate of Ironforge. Two gnomes in the town work on a machine that they hope will cure their people.

lines.title: Steelgrill's Depot

lines.index: #section:Steelgrill's Depot stands just north-east of Kharanos. It is the workshop of Beldin Steelgrill, the finest siege engine mechanic in the mountains, and a haunt of the pilots of the Siege Brigade. Their armored steam tanks bear names like Jetsteam and Trollplow, and their pilots boast of them as other dwarves boast of rams. The depot hears much of what passes on the roads, and it was a mountaineer's report here that first drew eyes toward a strange campfire above Gol'Bolar.

lines.text: The Grizzled Den.
lines.title: The Grizzled Den

lines.index: #section:The Grizzled Den is a cave in the hills west of Kharanos. Its tunnels were once a rich source of ore, and the miners of Kharanos worked there. Then the wendigo spread out of their own caves and filled it. The miners fled and left their shipments behind. A mountaineer named Cornelius went in to learn how bad things were and never came out. Deep inside dwells a loud and savage wendigo called Frosthowl.

lines.title: Chill Breeze Valley

lines.index: #section:Chill Breeze Valley opens in the west of Dun Morogh, between Kharanos and the hills of Gnomeregan. Its eastern stretch is well travelled, for the road from Coldridge Pass runs through it. Few go willingly into its quieter corners. There, a great wendigo called Old Icebeard keeps a cave, and he once carried off the whole meat locker of the trapper Tundra MacGrann, who camps nearby with a bad leg and an empty belly.

There, a great wendigo called Old Icebeard keeps a cave, and he once carried off the whole meat locker of the trapper Tundra MacGrann, who camps nearby with a bad leg and an empty belly.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Brewnall Village.
lines.text: Brewnall Village.
lines.title: Brewnall Village

lines.index: #section:Brewnall Village sits on the west bank of Iceflow Lake. It is the home of the Barleybrew family, brewers who experiment without fear and sometimes without success. Their Evershine burns so hot that siege pilots pour it into their furnaces. The Barleybrews have no love for the Thunderbrews of Kharanos, and they are not above a little mischief in their rivals' cellar. Fishermen work the lake beside them, and the Frostmane trolls watch from the south-west.

lines.index: #section:Iceflow Lake.
lines.text: Iceflow Lake.
lines.title: Iceflow Lake

lines.index: #section:Iceflow Lake spreads across the north of Dun Morogh, west of Ironforge, frozen over for much of the year. A river of ice runs down to it from the bridge north of Kharanos. Wolves hunt on the island at its center. The fishers of Brewnall Village cut holes in the ice and wait for days over their lines, and they curse the wendigo who steal what little they catch.

lines.index: #section:Frostmane Hold.
lines.text: Frostmane Hold.
lines.title: Frostmane Hold

lines.index: #section:Frostmane Hold is the great cave of the Frostmane trolls, south-west of Brewnall Village. Headhunters, hideskinners, snowstriders and shadowcasters dwell there in numbers that frightened even the dwarf sent to count them. The Hold is the heart of Frostmane power in Dun Morogh. What the trolls plan within it, the dwarves have tried to learn, and their reports have caused as much trouble in the Senate as in the snow.

lines.index: #section:Shimmer Ridge.
lines.text: Shimmer Ridge.
lines.title: Shimmer Ridge

lines.index: #section:Shimmer Ridge is a range of high hills in the north of Dun Morogh, near Iceflow Lake and west of the Gates of Ironforge. The Frostmane trolls keep camps upon it, joined by a bridge, and their seers tend baskets of shimmerweed there. The herb has some part in their rites. To the brewers of Brewnall it has a different purpose, and they pay well for anyone who will climb the ridge to steal it.

lines.index: #section:Gates of Gnomeregan.
lines.text: Gates of Gnomeregan.
lines.title: Gates of Gnomeregan

lines.index: #section:North of Brewnall Village, the hills of western Dun Morogh rise to the gates of Gnomeregan. Once this was a busy country of gnomish machines and villages. Now the pumps and filters stand broken, and the gnomes who remain are poisoned, sick and hostile, wandering before the doors of the city they could not save. Among them a dwarf spy of shady purpose hides in disguise. Gnomes who fled say that precious records of their people still lie buried in the snow here.

lines.index: #section:Gol'Bolar Quarry.
lines.text: Gol'Bolar Quarry.
lines.title: Gol'Bolar Quarry

lines.index: #section:Gol'Bolar Quarry is a great open pit in the east of Dun Morogh, where the king's miners cut ore and stone. When they dug deep, the Rockjaw troggs poured out of the rock, smashed the machines and drove the miners from the pit. Now the foreman rages, a senator of Ironforge pays for trogg heads, and the quarrymaster hopes no one learns that the troggs made off with his blasting powder. From the Tundrid Hills above, a Wildhammer stranger watches over it all.

lines.index: #section:Amberstill Ranch.
lines.text: Amberstill Ranch.
lines.title: Amberstill Ranch

lines.index: #section:Amberstill Ranch lies beside the road east of Kharanos. The Amberstill family breeds the great mountain rams that carry the dwarves of Ironforge, and their herds are the pride of Dun Morogh. Rams from the ranch now go to the expedition in Alterac, and they need saddles of the finest leopard pelts. The herd has also found a hunter of its own: the beast Vagash, who lairs on the slopes above and comes down by night.

lines.text: Misty Pine Refuge.
lines.title: Misty Pine Refuge

lines.index: #section:Misty Pine Refuge is a lonely house in the northern hills of Dun Morogh, east of the Gates of Ironforge. Father Gavin of the Argent Dawn has mended it and keeps its hearth lit for any traveler caught by the cold. The mountains around it have grown dangerous. A rockslide from the peaks has stirred up spirits of ice, and the largest of them seems to bring storms and new slides wherever it goes.

lines.index: #section:Helm's Bed Lake.
lines.text: Helm's Bed Lake.
lines.title: Helm's Bed Lake

lines.index: #section:Helm's Bed Lake lies in the far south-east of Dun Morogh, near the passes to Loch Modan. Its water is mostly frozen, and the country around it is wild and empty. Rockjaw troggs roam its shores. In the hills to the north, a siege pilot waits beside two engines for a friend who went on alone in search of rare ore. The friend was Mori Hildelve, and a great bear called Mangeclaw found him first.

lines.text: Ironband's Compound.
lines.title: Ironband's Compound

lines.index: #section:Ironband's Compound is a house and yard south of Helm's Bed Lake, in the east of Dun Morogh. Its dwarven owners have left it. Dark Iron dwarves hold it now, led by a captain named Beld, and they attack anyone who comes near. The Wildhammer Earthseer Farsen believes they are no mere raiders. Maps taken from their dead show tunnels that run far underground and meet beneath Ironforge.

lines.text: Frostmane Trolls.
lines.title: Frostmane Trolls

lines.index: #section:The Frostmane are a tribe of trolls who live in the snows of Dun Morogh. They are fierce and secretive, and they dispute these mountains with the dwarves. No chronicle records when they first came here.
lines.text: The Frostmane are a tribe of trolls who live in the snows of Dun Morogh. They are fierce and secretive, and they dispute these mountains with the dwarves. No chronicle records when they first came here.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Their greatest stronghold is Frostmane Hold, a cavern south-west of Brewnall Village. They also keep camps upon Shimmer Ridge and a cave in the south of Coldridge Valley, where the young whelps of the tribe dwell. Their warriors are headhunters and snowstriders. Their seers and shadowcasters work a magic of their own, and they gather shimmerweed for their rituals.

Their seers and shadowcasters work a magic of their own, and they gather shimmerweed for their rituals.
lines.title: Their Lands

lines.index: #section:The Senate of Ironforge has its hands full with the troggs, and it would rather not think of the trolls at all. Two brothers of the Whitebeard family were sent to learn how great the threat truly is. Grelin judged the trolls of Coldridge to be few. Senir found Frostmane Hold full of them. Between the two reports lies the question of how much the dwarves can afford to ignore. In Coldridge, a troll called Grik'nir the Cold has stolen more than a journal from the dwarves: he has shown them that the Frostmane are watching.

lines.index: #section:Gnomeregan Exiles.
lines.text: Gnomeregan Exiles.
lines.title: Gnomeregan Exiles

lines.index: #section:The Gnomeregan Exiles are the gnomes who survived the fall of their city. They are a people without a home. Most of them live in Ironforge, where King Magni Bronzebeard gave them room in Tinker Town, but they are scattered across Dun Morogh and beyond.
lines.text: The Gnomeregan Exiles are the gnomes who survived the fall of their city. They are a people without a home. Most of them live in Ironforge, where King Magni Bronzebeard gave them room in Tinker Town, but they are scattered across Dun Morogh and beyond.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The troggs came up beneath Gnomeregan, and the gnomes drove them back with a weapon of their own making. It went horribly wrong. The city was poisoned, and many of its people were changed into sick and witless lepers who still wander before its gates. The rest fled into the snow with whatever they could carry. Some lost everything to the trolls on the way. Others left behind the records of their families, their inventions and their craft.

Some lost everything to the trolls on the way. Others left behind the records of their families, their inventions and their craft.
lines.title: After the Fall

lines.index: #section:The exiles have not given up. In Kharanos, Razzle Sprysprocket and Ozzie Togglevolt are building a machine they hope will restore the poisoned gnomes. In Ironforge, the tinkers of Gnomeregan send brave strangers back into the city to rescue its lost knowledge. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque swears that his people will take their home back from the traitor who holds it.

A pair of warm gloves is his first gift, and wolf meat is his price. In a valley this cold, he reckons, it is better to lose a morning's hunt than a finger.

Balir is short of strong arms, and he will take any he can get.

lines.index: #section:Father Gavin is a priest of the Argent Dawn, an order sworn to destroy the unholy and the unnatural. Gavin would rather heal than fight. He also searches the snows for fallen mountaineers and sends their rifles home.

lines.index: #section:Tirisfal Glades.
lines.text: Tirisfal Glades.
lines.title: Tirisfal Glades

lines.index: #section:Tirisfal Glades was once the heart of Lordaeron. Its long green valleys fed the greatest of the human kingdoms, and on its eastern edge stood the kingdom's Capital City. Now the glades are grey. Mist hangs over empty farms, the mills turn for no one, and the crows are fat. The land belongs to the Forsaken, the dead who woke to their own minds again. From Brill and the Undercity they hold it against the living and the dead alike.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records the year when the first settlers came to Tirisfal. They came from Arathor, in the long centuries after the Troll Wars, and they found rich soil and quiet forests. Their farmsteads grew into a kingdom, and that kingdom took the name of Lordaeron. In later ages, noble families from the old Arathi heartland bought great estates in the glades. The Agamands, who owned the mills of the northern highlands, were counted the most prosperous of them all.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:The Forsaken of Sylvanas Windrunner rule Tirisfal, but they rule a land at war. The Scourge still holds the Agamand Mills and slips past the Bulwark, the wall that guards the glades from the Plaguelands to the east. The Scarlet Crusade marches out of its monastery in the north-east and keeps watchtowers across the land. Gnolls rob the mass graves for corpses to feed the Lich King's armies. In the capital, the Royal Apothecary Society works on a new plague, and the Deathguard keep living prisoners in the cellar of a tavern until the apothecaries have need of them. New troubles have come as well. Not long ago the necropolis Naxxramas struck at the Undercity, and the shards of its great crystal still lie scattered in the fields near the ruined capital, where the Cult of the Damned hunts for them. In the western mountains, a new order of Forsaken paladins keeps a fortress of its own. Few of their people trust them.

lines.title: The Present Day

lines.index: #section:• The Forsaken. The Deathguard patrol the roads, the executors give the orders, and the newly risen wake in the crypt of Deathknell every day. • The Scourge. Mindless dead, skeletons and necromancers still infest the mills, the farms and the old crypts. • The Scarlet Crusade. Zealots in red who burn every undead they find, whether it serves the Lich King or not. • The Rot Hide gnolls. Slaves of the Scourge who dig up the dead. • Murlocs and beasts. The Vile Fin tribes of the coast and lakes, darkhounds, duskbats and the great spiders of the eastern vales.

lines.title: Inhabitants

lines.index: #section:• The Plague. In the Third War, the plague of the Cult of the Damned swept the glades. Whole families died and rose again as Scourge. • The Fall. Prince Arthas Menethil murdered his father Terenas Menethil in his own throne room. The capital fell, and Tirisfal fell with it. That was the Fall of Lordaeron. • The Forsaken. When the Lich King's grip weakened, Sylvanas and her followers broke free and claimed the ruins of the capital. Beneath it they built the Undercity. • The Necropolis. When Naxxramas came against the Undercity, the Forsaken fought it on the surface. The Argent Dawn fought beside them, and many fell.

lines.index: #section:Deathknell.
lines.text: Deathknell.
lines.title: Deathknell

lines.index: #section:Deathknell is a small village of the dead in the west of Tirisfal. Its crypt stands on a hill above a chapel and a graveyard. Here the Forsaken bring the bodies they find, and here many wake from the Lich King's thrall to their own minds again. The undertaker Mordo greets them. Shadow Priest Sarvis explains what they have become, and Executor Arren puts them to work. The village is not safe. Mindless dead wander its northern houses, spiders fill the gold mine of Night Web's Hollow, and the Scarlet Crusade keeps a camp to the south-east.

lines.text: Brill.
lines.title: Brill

lines.index: #section:Brill is the chief town of the Forsaken in Tirisfal, on the road between Deathknell and the Undercity. Its town hall is the seat of Magistrate Sevren and Executor Zygand, who command the Deathguard of the glades. Its graveyard is tended by junior apothecaries, and its inn, the Gallows' End Tavern, keeps a cellar where captured humans and dwarves wait for the apothecaries' experiments. Not far from the town, the zeppelins of the Horde rise from their towers, and in these days even a trainer of Forsaken paladins keeps a place in Brill.

lines.index: #section:Agamand Mills.
lines.text: Agamand Mills.
lines.title: Agamand Mills

lines.index: #section:The Agamand Mills stand in the highlands of northern Tirisfal. They were the wealth of the Agamand family, the richest house in the glades. When the plague came, the Agamands fortified their home and bade their workers stay and fight. All of them died, and all of them rose. Now the mills are the strongest outpost of the Scourge in Tirisfal. At their northern end lies the Agamand Family Crypt, where a skeletal captain named Dargol has raised the family's ancestors to fight for the Lich King.

lines.text: Solliden Farmstead.
lines.title: Solliden Farmstead

lines.index: #section:The Solliden Farmstead lies in western Tirisfal, north of Deathknell. It is one of the last places in the glades where living humans still work the fields. The pumpkins still grow, and the farmers still bring in their harvest, because the Scarlet Crusade guards them from a tower to the west. The Forsaken hate the farm for its life. The apothecaries of Brill find a use for its pumpkins all the same. On the bluffs to the north-west rises Bandarion Keep.

lines.text: Garren's Haunt.
lines.title: Garren's Haunt

lines.index: #section:Garren's Haunt is a farmstead in the north of Tirisfal, with a farmhouse, a barn and wide grey fields. No chronicle records who Garren was. The Rot Hide gnolls hold the farm now. They serve the Scourge and rob the Mass Graves to the south-west, where the dead of the first plague were buried. Their leader is a gnoll called Maggot Eye, and the town of Brill has sentenced him to death for his crimes against the Forsaken. Executor Zygand has promised a reward to whoever carries out the sentence and brings back his paw.

lines.text: Venomweb Vale.
lines.title: Venomweb Vale

lines.index: #section:Venomweb Vale is a wide valley in the far east of Tirisfal, below the heights of the Scarlet Monastery. Its woods are thick with webs. The great spiders that nest there carry a venom that the apothecaries of Brill believe once preserved an ancient plague. Of late the Deathguard have also seen a rogue abomination wandering near the vale. Such a creature should not have passed the Bulwark unnoticed, and the Deathguard keep the matter quiet. At the northern edge of the vale, the Scarlet Crusade keeps a camp of its own.

lines.text: Scarlet Watch Post.
lines.title: Scarlet Watch Post

lines.index: #section:The Scarlet Watch Post is a tower of the Scarlet Crusade in the north-east of Tirisfal, beyond Faol's Rest. It watches the northern approaches of the Scarlet Monastery. Its commander, Captain Melrache, is known to the Forsaken as a ruthless man, and he never goes without his two bodyguards. The tower is one of several that the Crusade keeps across the glades. From each of them its patrols ride out to burn the dead. Captain Perrine holds a ruined tower south-west of Brill, and Captain Vachon another in the south-east, near the Balnir Farmstead.

lines.title: Brightwater Lake

lines.index: #section:Brightwater Lake is the largest lake in Tirisfal, north-east of Brill. On an island at its heart stands Gunther's Retreat, the camp of a lich named Gunther Arcanus. He is free of the Lich King, yet he believed for a long time that he was the only one, and his servants attacked all who came near. Off the island's southern shore stands an old bloody altar. The Scourge agent Lillith Nefara sleeps there until a candle of beckoning wakes her.

lines.index: #section:Capital City.
lines.text: Capital City.
lines.title: Capital City

lines.index: #section:The ruins of Capital City stand on the eastern edge of Tirisfal. For centuries it was the seat of the kings of Lordaeron. Here Prince Arthas Menethil came home from Northrend and slew his father on his throne. The city was sacked and left in ruins. Its broken walls and its empty throne room now guard the way down to the Undercity, the city of the Forsaken beneath it. Parts of the old streets are still not theirs. Scourge forces linger in the eastern ruins, and the Forsaken fight to take them back.

lines.index: #section:Whispering Forest.
lines.text: Whispering Forest.
lines.title: Whispering Forest

lines.index: #section:The Whispering Forest lies in the mountains of western Tirisfal, below the cliff called Northface Rock. Its woods are dark and its roots are said to run deep. Some folk in the Undercity say that the forest is touched by the void, and that things crawl beneath it that should not. Diseased stags and does wander its glades. By a ring of great mushrooms walks a ghostly knight bound there by an oath. To the south-west lie the ruins of Shadowvale, and above it all stands Bandarion Keep.

lines.index: #section:Bandarion Keep.
lines.text: Bandarion Keep.
lines.title: Bandarion Keep

lines.index: #section:Bandarion Keep is the monastery of Tyr's Watch, the order of Forsaken paladins. It stands on Northface Rock, the steep bluff between the Whispering Forest and the rest of Tirisfal. In the last war the Argent Dawn held it against the Scourge. When the Dawn withdrew to the Plaguelands, the fortress fell into ruin, and the Vile Fin murlocs made it a spawning ground. Danitha Morr and her paladins drove them out and began to rebuild. She named the keep after Garek Bandarion, the first of the Forsaken to take up the Holy Light again.

lines.index: #section:Shadowvale.
lines.text: Shadowvale.
lines.title: Shadowvale

lines.index: #section:Shadowvale is a ruined village deep in the Whispering Forest, south-west of Bandarion Keep. Its folk were strange and private in life, and they did not welcome visitors. Now the village belongs to the Tarnished, risen paladins who turn the Light against their own people. Mindless dead gather in the cellars beneath it. A cultist is said to have carried a shard of the necropolis crystal down there, and whatever it does, it makes the dead stronger or more numerous.

lines.text: Tyr's Watch.
lines.title: Tyr's Watch

lines.index: #section:Tyr's Watch is an order of Forsaken paladins, newly founded in Tirisfal Glades. Its members were servants of the Holy Light in life. They died, rose, and found that the Light still answered them, though its touch now burns their flesh. They keep their monastery at Bandarion Keep, and Danitha Morr leads them.

They died, rose, and found that the Light still answered them, though its touch now burns their flesh. They keep their monastery at Bandarion Keep, and Danitha Morr leads them.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The paladins of Tyr's Watch teach that pain is no reason to turn from the Light. Healing hurts them, so they learn to heal through the pain, and they call it a crucible. They teach that the pursuit of good for its own sake is the heart of their calling. They seek out the wretched and the forgotten of the Undercity and help them in small ways, because they believe that small acts also bind them to the Light.

lines.title: Beliefs

lines.index: #section:The Forsaken remember well what the living did to them in the name of the Light. Many fear that a paladin will one day smite them as a monster. Some risen paladins do exactly that. The order calls them the Tarnished, and it hunts them. The Dark Lady herself mistrusts Tyr's Watch and has told its paladins that she is watching. Danitha believes it may take years, or decades, before her order is fully trusted. She means to earn that trust anyway.

He plans the war against the Scarlet Crusade from the papers taken at Deathknell, and he means to strike down its captains one by one.

lines.title: Gunther Arcanus

lines.index: #section:Gunther Arcanus was a mage of the Kirin Tor of Dalaran and a skilled necromancer. He studied beside Bethor Iceshard and Thule Ravenclaw. Thule betrayed his friends to the Lich King. Gunther and Bethor died of the plague. Gunther rose as a lich with a free mind, but he believed he was the only one of his kind, and he took every other undead for a slave of the Scourge.

lines.text: Gregor Agamand. Head of the Agamand Family.
lines.title: Gregor Agamand

lines.index: #section:Gregor Agamand was the head of the richest family in Tirisfal. When the Scourge first came, he chose to fight. He fortified the mills and persuaded his workers to stay and defend them. His pride doomed them all. Gregor died with his household and rose as a mindless servant of the Lich King. He still walks among the mills he once owned.

lines.title: Devlin Agamand

lines.index: #section:Devlin was the younger son of Gregor Agamand. His brother Thurman was tall and gentle. Devlin was weak and sharp of tongue. When the mills fell to the plague, he was quick to die, and no one was surprised. He rose as a servant of the Scourge, and his mad chattering can still be heard by the road that leads up to the mills. Travellers on that road hear him long before they see him.

lines.title: Lillith Nefara

lines.index: #section:Lillith Nefara is a powerful agent of the Scourge. She sleeps beside an old, bloody altar just off the southern shore of Gunther's island in Brightwater Lake. A candle of beckoning, lit upon the altar, wakes her. Gunther keeps such candles in a crate at his camp. The lich Gunther Arcanus knows her well, and he counts her death as proof that someone is truly the Lich King's foe.

lines.index: #section:Garek Bandarion. The First Forsaken Paladin.
lines.text: Garek Bandarion. The First Forsaken Paladin.
lines.title: Garek Bandarion

lines.index: #section:Garek Bandarion was a soldier of Lordaeron who died in its fall and rose among the Forsaken. He became the first captain of the Deathguard, and he was the first of the Forsaken to take up the Holy Light as a paladin. He fell when the necropolis Naxxramas came against the Undercity. The paladins of Tyr's Watch named their monastery after him, and they still speak his name as a battle cry.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:To the Forsaken paladins, Garek is proof that the Light did not abandon them in death. To the Deathguard, he is the captain who built their ranks. His life joins the last days of the living kingdom to the first days of the dead one.

lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• In life, he served in the City Guard of the capital under Captain Landen, who chose him as his successor. • On the day Arthas murdered his father, he and Landen led survivors out through the sewers beneath the city. • He took his vengeance on Baron Rivendare, the lord who betrayed the kingdom to the Cult of the Damned, and died of his wounds and the plague. • As a Forsaken, he fought beside Dark Ranger Anya in the first days of the Undercity. • He rose to be captain of the Deathguard. • He died in the defense of the Undercity against Naxxramas.

lines.title: Deeds

lines.index: #section:The Last Days of Lordaeron. Garek was a young guardsman who longed for battle, and his captain, Landen, told him that protecting the people was the greater glory. On the night Arthas slew King Terenas Menethil, they found the throne room full of cultists. Uther the Lightbringer sent them to save whom they could. Beneath the city they found that the cult had long been ready. Landen stayed behind to hold back Baron Rivendare so that Garek could lead the people to safety. Garek never forgave the baron. He hunted him to Stratholme and killed him there, and he died of his wounds.

lines.index: #section:A Second Life. Garek woke in the vaults of the Undercity with no memory but his name. The apothecary Putress wished to use his body for parts. Dark Ranger Anya stopped him. Garek swore himself to Sylvanas, and with Anya he gathered the free-willed dead from the ruins, cleared the tunnels and helped the city grow. When the Scarlet Crusade broke through the walls of the Undercity, he led the Deathguard against them. Somewhere in those years, the Light began to answer him again.

Danitha Morr and Leonid Barthalomew fought in that battle and lost many friends there. When Danitha took the old fortress on Northface Rock for her order, she named it after him.

lines.text: Dark Ranger Anya. Dark Ranger of the Banshee Queen.
lines.title: Dark Ranger Anya

lines.index: #section:Anya is a dark ranger, one of the undead elves who serve Sylvanas Windrunner. In life she was a ranger of Quel'Thalas under Sylvanas's command. She died defending her homeland against the Scourge and rose as its slave. She remembers everything she did in that time. When she broke free, Sylvanas gave her a place to belong, and for that Anya gave the Dark Lady her loyalty for all time.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Anya is one of the first dark rangers of the Forsaken, and one of those who saw the Undercity rise from the tunnels. She was the companion of Garek Bandarion through the early wars of the dead kingdom. Where he lost his memories, she kept all of hers, and she taught him that for many Forsaken death is a clean slate and a second life. She trusts the living very little. When a paladin of the old Silver Hand showed mercy to a Forsaken laborer and his captain killed the man anyway, Anya told Garek that the living would never see the undead as people, and could not be trusted.

She fought in the defense of the Undercity when Naxxramas came, and she lost friends there, among them Garek Bandarion. When she took the ruined fortress on Northface Rock, she named it after him.

Vile Fin murlocs had made it a spawning ground, and they fought to take it back even after they were driven out. Danitha had few materials, fewer allies and a great many walls to mend. She welcomed every newcomer who still held to the Light.

She told its paladins to serve well, and that she would be watching.

lines.title: Leonid Barthalomew

lines.index: #section:Leonid Barthalomew is an undead knight of the Argent Dawn, called the Revered by his comrades. He came to Bandarion Keep with another Forsaken of the Dawn to visit old friends. He knows the fortress well. The Dawn held it in the Scourge's last push into Tirisfal, and he fought from its walls. He also fought for the Undercity when Naxxramas came, beside Danitha Morr and Garek Bandarion.

lines.text: Rudolph Gelhardt. Commander of the Tarnished.
lines.title: Rudolph Gelhardt

lines.index: #section:Rudolph Gelhardt is a risen paladin who never accepted his undeath. He carries the prejudices of his old life into the new one, and he turns the Holy Light against the Forsaken. He leads the Tarnished, who have made the ruins of Shadowvale their den. Every Forsaken they kill makes it harder for the paladins of Tyr's Watch to be trusted. His followers are drudges and zealots, and they fight for him to the very end.

lines.index: #section:Teldrassil.
lines.text: Teldrassil.
lines.title: Teldrassil

lines.index: #section:Teldrassil is the new World Tree of the night elves, and the land that grows upon it. It rises from the sea off the northern coast of Kalimdor, so vast that whole forests, lakes and villages rest on its boughs. At its crown stands the city of Darnassus. Its glades are lit by moonwells and watched by the Sentinels, and to a newcomer it seems the most peaceful place in the world. Those who live there know better. Something is wrong with the tree, and every season the signs grow harder to ignore.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:After the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the night elves were left without their old strength. Nordrassil had spent its power to destroy Archimonde, and with it the kaldorei lost their immortality. Malfurion Stormrage went into the Emerald Dream and did not return. In his absence, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm took up the leadership of the druids. He persuaded the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore that the time had come to rebuild, and to win back what had been lost. With the Circle's consent, he and the mightiest druids of his order grew a new tree beyond the coast. When it was grown, Fandral asked the great dragons to bless it, as they had once blessed Nordrassil. Nozdormu, Lord of Time, refused him and rebuked his pride. Alexstrasza, the Life-Binder, refused him too. Without their gifts, the growth of Teldrassil has been flawed and unpredictable, and the night elves have not regained their undying lives.

lines.title: The World Tree

lines.index: #section:Teldrassil is home to most of the kaldorei who survived the war. Young druids, priestesses and Sentinels begin their service in Shadowglen and Dolanaar, then climb to Darnassus. Yet the forest is sick. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, once gentle friends of the elves, have turned savage. Timberlings rise angry from the soil, bearing tumors. Harpies nest about the Oracle Tree, satyrs hide in its caves, and a fel moss spreads through beasts and furbolgs alike. The druids study each new ill in turn. The Arch Druid carries the weight of it all, and he does not carry it lightly.

lines.index: #section:Shadowglen.
lines.text: Shadowglen.
lines.title: Shadowglen

lines.index: #section:Shadowglen is a sheltered vale in the north-east of Teldrassil, where many young kaldorei take their first steps in service. At its heart grows the great tree Aldrassil, and a moonwell shines to the north of it. Conservator Ilthalaine keeps the balance of its beasts. The glen is not as safe as it looks. Grells tainted by fel moss roam its western edge, where the Gnarlpine once lived in peace. North of the vale lies the Shadowthread Cave, where webwood spiders grown huge on the World Tree spin their nests.

lines.index: #section:Aldrassil is the great tree at the centre of Shadowglen, hollowed and grown into a dwelling for the teachers of the young. Trainers of every calling keep rooms along its winding ramps. In its highest chamber sits Tenaron Stormgrip, who sends each newcomer to fetch water from the moonwell nearby and so begins the telling of the story of Teldrassil. The scholar Gilshalan Windwalker works at its foot, studying the spiders of the Shadowthread Cave.

lines.index: #section:Dolanaar.
lines.text: Dolanaar.
lines.title: Dolanaar

lines.index: #section:Dolanaar is the village of the road, halfway between Shadowglen and Darnassus. Its houses are grown from living wood around a moonwell, where Corithras Moonrage continues the story that Tenaron began. Innkeeper Keldamyr offers rest to travellers. Druids such as Athridas Bearmantle and Tallonkai Swiftroot watch the troubles of the forest from here, and the Sentinel Kyra Starsong sends her sisters out along the roads. Dolanaar is proud of its good name, and its people would rather keep certain shames to themselves.

lines.index: #section:Fel Rock.
lines.text: Fel Rock.
lines.title: Fel Rock

lines.index: #section:Fel Rock is a cave just north of Dolanaar. Its name has become a hard truth. The satyr Lord Melenas made his lair in its depths and gathered a band of grell warriors about him. The druids of Dolanaar count it a deep embarrassment that such a creature should dwell so close to their village, and they have tried to deal with him quietly. His plots, it is now known, served a darker master elsewhere in the forest.

lines.text: Lake Al'Ameth.
lines.title: Lake Al'Ameth

lines.index: #section:Lake Al'Ameth lies south of Dolanaar, a long water ringed with trees and fronds. On its eastern shore the druid Denalan keeps a camp and a garden, where he tests new soils on the seeds of the timberlings. The lake is where the sickness of those creatures is plainest. Young timberlings sprout wild along its banks, and in a cave on its southern shore dwells Oakenscowl, once a leader of his kind and now a source of the corruption.

lines.text: Starbreeze Village.
lines.title: Starbreeze Village

lines.index: #section:Starbreeze Village lies in the east of Teldrassil, beyond the road from Dolanaar. It was a tranquil place, and a moonwell still shines just outside it. Then the Gnarlpine came. The furbolgs ambushed the warden Gaerolas Talvethren on his way to the barrow den and pillaged the village. Houses stand empty, their owners' treasures left behind in the dressers. The furbolgs who remain in Starbreeze have given themselves over entirely to their madness.

lines.text: Ban'ethil Barrow Den.
lines.title: Ban'ethil Barrow Den

lines.index: #section:The Ban'ethil Barrow Den lies west of Dolanaar, beneath the roots of the forest. Here the Druids of the Talon sleep, their spirits walking the Emerald Dream in keeping with their pact with Ysera. The Gnarlpine have broken into it. Their shaman have learned to part a sleeping druid's spirit from his body and to set the empty flesh against intruders. The sleepers can be woken only with the Relics of Wakening, kept in sacred chests within. Even messengers of the Oracle Tree have been dragged below.

lines.text: Gnarlpine Hold.
lines.title: Gnarlpine Hold

lines.index: #section:Gnarlpine Hold is the stronghold of the Gnarlpine furbolgs in the south-west of Teldrassil. Here dwells their chieftain, Ursal the Mauler, who drives his people to madness with the powers of the fel moss. Shaman, totemics and defenders of the tribe crowd its dens, and captured druids are kept there under the furbolgs' spell. What was once a home of gentle folk has become the heart of the tribe's rage.

lines.title: Pools of Arlithrien

lines.index: #section:The Pools of Arlithrien lie south-east of the road into Darnassus, a string of quiet waters beside one of the moonwells of Teldrassil. The Sentinels once patrolled them with ease. Now the Gnarlpine furbolgs strike at every patrol, and the path to the well is a hazard for any who go alone. The first reports of their attacks here were dismissed as rumour. No one dismisses them any longer.

lines.text: The Oracle Glade.
lines.title: The Oracle Glade

lines.index: #section:The Oracle Glade lies in the north-west of Teldrassil. At its heart grows the Oracle Tree, which watches the growth of the World Tree and sends its counsel to the elders of the kaldorei. Beneath its boughs lies the first and most powerful moonwell of Teldrassil. Harpies of the Bloodfeather have nested all around the glade, and they have slain the runners who carried the tree's messages. A small band of Sentinels under Arynia Cloudsbreak holds the moonwell against them.

lines.text: Wellspring Lake.
lines.title: Wellspring Lake

lines.index: #section:Wellspring Lake lies in the far north of Teldrassil, and the Wellspring River runs from it through the forest. The timberlings that wander its shores are the most tainted on the tree, covered in mossy tumors full of poison. On the northern borders nearby dwells Lady Sathrah, a great spider once beloved of Elune, whose silver threads gathered the healing dew of the evening. She has gone mad, and her kind with her.

lines.index: #section:The Cleft.
lines.text: The Cleft.
lines.title: The Cleft

lines.index: #section:The Cleft is a deep fold in the forest north-west of Dolanaar. Few go there willingly. The satyr Xethorr the Wicked has made it his home, and it was at his bidding that Lord Melenas plotted in Fel Rock. Xethorr has bent the spiders of Teldrassil to his will, and the befouled webwoods of the Cleft carry the fel moss in their venom. The druids of Dolanaar would sooner hunt him in silence than let the forest learn how near he dwells.

lines.text: Rut'theran Village.
lines.title: Rut'theran Village

lines.index: #section:Rut'theran Village lies at the foot of Teldrassil, on the shore where its great roots meet the sea. It is the tree's door to the world. Ships and hippogryphs come and go from here, and the hippogryph master Vesprystus carries travellers across the water to Auberdine in Darkshore. A portal lifts those bound for Darnassus up to the city. The fish of these waters are large and plentiful, and the loremasters of the Cenarion Circle keep a small house here too.

lines.text: Conservator Ilthalaine. Keeper of the Balance of Shadowglen.
lines.title: Conservator Ilthalaine

lines.index: #section:Conservator Ilthalaine keeps the balance of nature in Shadowglen. The spring rains were heavy this year, and some beasts of the glen flourished while others starved. The nightsabers and thistle boars have grown too many for the land to feed. Ilthalaine does not enjoy the answer, but he gives it plainly: their numbers must be thinned.

lines.index: #section:Tarindrella. The Woodland Protector.
lines.text: Tarindrella. The Woodland Protector.
lines.title: Tarindrella

lines.index: #section:Tarindrella is a dryad, a mysterious protector of the woodlands, who has come back to Shadowglen after many years away. She came because something evil is brewing in the forest. The grells and grellkin of the glen have fallen under the spell of the fel moss, and the peaceful furbolgs of the hills have left their homes.

lines.index: #section:The Engraved Totems. The furbolgs left their totems behind in the chaos of their flight. Their carvings told a grim tale. The Gnarlpine had begun to dream of being wiped out by a great shadow. Fear turned to rage, and the shadow in their dreams took the shape of their old friends, the elves.

lines.text: Gilshalan Windwalker. Scholar of the Webwood Spiders.
lines.title: Gilshalan Windwalker

lines.index: #section:Gilshalan Windwalker came to Shadowglen to study the webwood spiders of the Shadowthread Cave. They are cousins of a much smaller breed, and he believes the World Tree has changed them. He wants their venom and their eggs carried to Darnassus, where he can compare them with their smaller kin. He is honest enough to admit that a live giant spider would be more than he could handle.

lines.title: Tenaron Stormgrip

lines.index: #section:Tenaron Stormgrip waits in the highest chamber of Aldrassil. Before the young of Shadowglen set out into the wider world, he believes, they must learn what has become of their people since the Battle of Mount Hyjal. He begins that lesson with a phial of moonwell water.

lines.title: Dirania Silvershine

lines.index: #section:Dirania Silvershine knows the herbs of Shadowglen. Her friend Iverron visits her at the same hour every day, and he is always getting into trouble. When he failed to come, she feared the spiders of the cave to the north. She was right. The spider Githyiss the Vile had bitten him, and only her antidote could save him.

lines.text: Iverron. A Friend in Need.
lines.title: Iverron

lines.index: #section:Iverron is a young elf of Shadowglen who spends too much time near the Shadowthread Cave. While exploring it he was bitten by a great spider called Githyiss the Vile. Dizzy and poisoned, he could only lie by the cave and ask that Dirania be told. Her antidote saved him, though he was in no hurry to walk back past the spiders alone.

lines.title: Corithras Moonrage

lines.index: #section:Corithras Moonrage keeps the moonwell of Dolanaar and carries on the telling that Tenaron began. The druids of Darnassus need moonwell water, and Corithras sends messengers to the wells of Starbreeze, Arlithrien and the Oracle Glade to gather it. At each return he tells a little more of the story.

lines.index: #section:From Corithras the young kaldorei learn the hardest part of their recent history: that Teldrassil was grown without the blessing of the dragons.
lines.text: From Corithras the young kaldorei learn the hardest part of their recent history: that Teldrassil was grown without the blessing of the dragons.
lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:The Refusal of the Dragons. After the war the kaldorei had no direction. The Betrayer was freed, Malfurion vanished, and Fandral Staghelm took the lead. When the tree was grown, Fandral sought the dragons' blessing. Nozdormu refused him for his arrogance, and Alexstrasza agreed with Nozdormu. Corithras does not pretend the consequences are small.

The news that came back was worse than he feared: the Gnarlpine had turned, and their chieftain was driving them mad with the fel moss.

The satyrs are a shame to the kaldorei, and one of them, Lord Melenas, lurked in Fel Rock, far too close to home. Tallonkai also lost his emerald dreamcatcher, a gift from the warden Gaerolas, when Starbreeze fell to the Gnarlpine.

lines.index: #section:Zenn Foulhoof is a satyr who lurks near Dolanaar and offers wonderful rewards to anyone who will fetch him fangs, feathers and spider silk. He asks that it stay a secret. Those who oblige him soon learn that he was laughing at them, and that the forest takes a dim view of such bargains.

He also forwards packages that come late from Darnassus, such as a parcel of rare earth for the druid Denalan.

lines.title: Denalan

lines.index: #section:Denalan is a druid who studies the plants of Teldrassil from a camp on Lake Al'Ameth. He believes the timberlings, elementals of nature, reflect the health of the tree itself. Their anger troubles him, and he suspects the soil. With special earths from Darnassus he grows their seeds, hoping they will sprout gentler.

lines.index: #section:Oben Rageclaw was a druid asleep in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den when the Gnarlpine shaman parted his spirit from his body. They set his empty flesh to attack anyone who entered the den, and left his spirit trapped in the Emerald Dream, powerless to stop them.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak was sent with a small band of Sentinels to protect the Oracle Tree from the harpies nesting around its glade. When the tree sent a runner to Darnassus, the harpies killed her. Arynia's band is pushing them back, little by little.

lines.index: #section:The Gnarlpine are a tribe of furbolgs who lived in the hills of Teldrassil as peaceful friends of the night elves. They have deserted their old homes and gathered under their chieftain, Ursal the Mauler, and they now attack the very protectors they once trusted.

lines.index: #section:The corruption of Teldrassil is the sickness that has spread through the new World Tree since it was grown. The priestesses and druids see its signs everywhere: in beasts, in plants, in furbolgs and even in the soil.

lines.index: #section:Durotar.
lines.text: Durotar.
lines.title: Durotar

lines.index: #section:Durotar is the homeland of the orcs, a red and broken country on the eastern shore of Kalimdor. Its soil is cracked and dry, its canyons are sharp, and the sun beats down upon it without mercy. The orcs chose it gladly, for its harsh beauty reminds them of the world they lost. Here the Warchief Thrall has raised his capital of Orgrimmar, and here the young of the Horde are tested before they are sent out into the world. It is a land at peace only in name. Enemies watch it from the sea, from the canyons and from the shadows of its own caves.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Before the orcs came, these lands were counted part of The Barrens, and the quilboar of the Razormane tribe roamed them freely. After the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Thrall led his people east to the coast and claimed the land between the Southfury River and the sea. He named it Durotar, in honor of his father, Durotan, chieftain of the Frostwolf clan. The tauren and the Darkspear trolls lent their strength to the new nation, and the orcs drove the Razormane from all but the western edges of the land.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Durotar is the heart of the new Horde. Yet its peace is thin. The humans of Kul Tiras still hold the ruins of Tiragarde Keep on the eastern coast. The witch doctor Zalazane rules the Echo Isles through dark voodoo. The Razormane press in from the west, the Kolkar centaur plot in their crag, and the Dustwind harpies prey upon the caravans. Worst of all, the cultists of the Burning Blade hide in the caves of Durotar, close to the gates of the capital itself. Of late, even the naga have been seen along the northern shore.

lines.index: #section:Valley of Trials.
lines.text: Valley of Trials.
lines.title: Valley of Trials

lines.index: #section:The Valley of Trials lies in the southwest of Durotar, walled in by red cliffs. It is the proving ground of the Horde. Young orcs and trolls come here to face their first foes: the boars of the valley floor, the scorpids of the northern slopes, and a monstrous scorpid called Sarkoth. The trainers of the Horde keep their camp in a cave known as the Den. Peons fell the valley's few trees for timber, when they are not asleep. Of late the valley has grown more dangerous, for the Burning Blade has made a coven in the caves of its northern wall.

lines.index: #section:Burning Blade Coven.
lines.text: Burning Blade Coven.
lines.title: Burning Blade Coven

lines.index: #section:The Burning Blade Coven is a cave in the cliffs north of the Valley of Trials. Miners once surveyed it for ore. Now the cultists of the Burning Blade have claimed it, and their small demons, the vile familiars, spill from its mouth into the valley. Deep inside, among chambers of falling water, the warlock Yarrog Baneshadow guards a medallion of dark power. The coven is small, but its presence so close to the proving ground of the Horde is a warning that the cult reaches further than anyone would like.

lines.title: Spirit Rock

lines.index: #section:Spirit Rock stands in the hills high above the Valley of Trials, at the end of a narrow trail called the Hidden Path. It is holy ground to the shaman of the Horde. Here the young who would walk the shaman's path drink the sapta, a draught that binds the spirit to the elements, and here they first see the spirit of the earth with their own eyes. The rite must be done in a holy place, and nowhere else. Few who are not shaman ever climb the Hidden Path.

lines.title: Razor Hill

lines.index: #section:Razor Hill is the crossroads of Durotar. Its roads run north to Orgrimmar, south to the Valley of Trials and Sen'jin Village, and west across the river into the Barrens. It is a town of soldiers. From its barracks, Gar'Thok commands the defense of the land, and Orgnil Soulscar hunts the cultists of the Burning Blade. An old warrior keeps a signal horn on the watchtower above the town. He sounds it less often than he once did, and he is glad of it.

lines.text: Sen'jin Village.
lines.title: Sen'jin Village

lines.index: #section:Sen'jin Village is the home of the free Darkspear on the southern coast of Durotar. The trolls built it after they were driven from the Echo Isles, and they named it for Sen'jin, the chieftain who gave his life so that his people might follow the orcs to a new land. It is a village of huts and fishing docks. Its elders are witch doctors and alchemists, its young are hunters, and its raptor handlers raise beasts from the wild isles. From its shore the trolls can see the islands they have lost.

lines.index: #section:The Echo Isles lie off the southeastern coast of Durotar. They were meant to be the new home of the Darkspear. Now they belong to the witch doctor Zalazane, who holds the trolls of the isles in thrall with his hexes. His slaves wander among the huts, and his ju-ju heaps foul the flow of magic across the land. Bloodtalon raptors and striped tigers hunt in the jungle. On the largest isle, a circle of skulls holds the trapped spirits of trolls who defied him.

lines.index: #section:Tiragarde Keep.
lines.text: Tiragarde Keep.
lines.title: Tiragarde Keep

lines.index: #section:Tiragarde Keep stands on the eastern coast of Durotar. The sailors of Admiral Daelin Proudmoore raised it when their fleet came to destroy the Horde. The orcs took the keep and broke its walls. Yet after the admiral's death, a reserve force under Lieutenant Benedict returned and fortified the ruins once more. The marines of Kul Tiras still fly their banner there. In the rubble around the keep lie the weapons of orcs who fell in the first assault, and their kin would see them honored.

lines.index: #section:Skull Rock.
lines.text: Skull Rock.
lines.title: Skull Rock

lines.index: #section:Skull Rock is a cave in the mountains east of the gates of Orgrimmar. It is a den of the Burning Blade. The cultists inside perform foul rites and burn their own flesh with searing collars, which bind them to demonic power. Their master in the cave is the warlock Gazz'uz, who answers to a voice that speaks through a pendant of burning shadow. That the cult can hide so near the Warchief's walls troubles every soldier of the Horde.
