lines.index: #section:Drygulch Ravine.
lines.text: Drygulch Ravine.
lines.title: Drygulch Ravine

lines.index: #section:Razorwind Canyon cuts through the hills between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar, and through a cave on its eastern side lies the hidden gorge of Drygulch Ravine. Both belong to the Dustwind harpies. They swoop down upon the goblin caravans of the road, carry off their goods, and hoard them in their nests on the cliffs. The strongest of the flock guard their eggs in the ravine. Some of the harpies' witches have begun to toy with a strange storm magic.

lines.index: #section:Thunder Ridge.
lines.text: Thunder Ridge.
lines.title: Thunder Ridge

lines.index: #section:Thunder Ridge is a wooded gorge in the northwest of Durotar, south of Orgrimmar. It takes its name from the thunder lizards that roam it, great beasts whose bodies hold a charge of lightning. The goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm has made a camp there with cultists of the Burning Blade, and they spread chaos among the trees. The orcs hunt the lizards for their hides, which line the roofs of the growing capital. The mightiest of them is called Halikor, and his hoof is a trophy worth boasting of.

lines.index: #section:Kolkar Crag.
lines.text: Kolkar Crag.
lines.title: Kolkar Crag

lines.index: #section:Kolkar Crag is a rocky gorge in the south of Durotar, west of Sen'jin Village. The Kolkar centaur have made it their camp. They raid by night, and their warlord, Kolkanis, has drawn up plans to strike at the orcs and trolls of the land. A troll scout of the Horde once crept into the crag and read those plans with his own eyes. Others who have tried to scout the crag alone have not always come out again.

lines.index: #section:Razormane Grounds.
lines.text: Razormane Grounds.
lines.title: Razormane Grounds

lines.index: #section:The Razormane Grounds lie in the west of Durotar, where the land falls toward the Southfury River. Here the quilboar of the Razormane tribe keep their bramble camps. They held much of Durotar before the orcs came, and they have never accepted its loss. Bones picked clean litter the ground around their thorns. Their geomancers call upon the earth, and their battleguard defend the camps with a fury born of wounded pride. The orcs of Razor Hill have sworn to drive them out of Durotar, and after that, perhaps out of Kalimdor.

lines.index: #section:Darkspear Islands.
lines.text: Darkspear Islands.
lines.title: Darkspear Islands

lines.index: #section:The Darkspear Islands lie off the coast of Durotar, battered by the storms of the open sea. The trolls hold them sacred, for their spirits are strong there, and the Darkspear gather on them for their ceremonies. Now the Alliance seeks a foothold on the islands, close to the shores of the orcish homeland. The Darkspear and their allies of the Horde will not let them stay. Among ruins, a camp, an old tower and a cove of shipwrecks, the two sides fight for control of the isles and of a sacred relic of the tribe.

lines.text: Kaltunk. Greeter of Recruits.
lines.title: Kaltunk

lines.index: #section:Kaltunk meets the young orcs and trolls who come of age in the Valley of Trials. He looks each one over with a critical eye and a broad grin. He knows that every recruit dreams of strangling a dragon on the first day, and he takes pleasure in telling them to start with something smaller. Then he laughs, and points them to the Den.

She fears it is only the herald of a greater evil.

lines.text: Hana'zua. Wounded Hunter of the Darkspear.
lines.title: Hana'zua

lines.index: #section:Hana'zua is a young troll who went hunting scorpids in the Valley of Trials and found one far larger than the rest. He struck the beast a heavy blow upon its claw, but its stinger cut deep into his chest. He lies wounded on the plateau, too weak to walk back to the Den, and more troubled by his honor than by his wound. If he must die, he wants at least to know that his foe died first.

lines.index: #section:Gar'Thok commands Razor Hill and the defense of central Durotar. He served the Horde when the orcs first came to Kalimdor, and he saw the sailors of Kul Tiras fall upon his outpost and slaughter his men. He trusts no human. He means to drive the Razormane from their last camps and the Kul Tirans from the ruins of Tiragarde Keep.

lines.text: Master Gadrin. Elder Witch Doctor of the Darkspear.
lines.title: Master Gadrin

lines.index: #section:Master Gadrin is the eldest witch doctor of Sen'jin Village and an elder of the Darkspear. With the young Zalazane, he once trained the priests and mages of the tribe. Then Zalazane went mad with power and drove him from the Echo Isles. Now Gadrin works to end the traitor's reign and to free the spirits he has enslaved. Among them is Gadrin's own brother, Minshina, who calls to him in dreams.

lines.title: Master Vornal

lines.index: #section:Master Vornal is an old troll of Sen'jin Village whose eyes are failing. He leans more and more on alchemy to work the magic that once came easily to him. He has never taken an apprentice, for he has never found one worthy. He also grieves for the idols of the loa that his people left behind when they fled the Echo Isles.

lines.index: #section:Zalazane. Witch Doctor of the Echo Isles.
lines.text: Zalazane. Witch Doctor of the Echo Isles.
lines.title: Zalazane

lines.index: #section:Zalazane was once a witch doctor of the Darkspear, a gifted pupil who helped Master Gadrin train the priests and mages of the tribe. The powers he called up drove him mad. He cursed the Echo Isles, enslaved many of his own people with his hexes, and drove the rest across the water to the mainland. Now he rules the isles as their master, and he sends his hexed servants across the water to spread his curse.

lines.title: Margoz

lines.index: #section:Margoz is a shaman of the Horde whose counsel is valued in Razor Hill. From his lonely camp in the north of Durotar, he studies the corruption of the Burning Blade. He wants to know how the cultists bind themselves to demons, and he has learned that the secret lies in the searing collars they wear. He urges all who serve the Horde to stay on the pure path.

lines.title: Rezlak

lines.index: #section:Rezlak is one of the goblins of Gazlowe, the master of Ratchet, sent to help the orcs build in Durotar. His work would go well, he says, if only his caravans arrived. The Dustwind harpies keep stealing them. Rezlak quotes his boss's sayings at every turn, and he means to follow one of them: if you want something done well, do it yourself, and pay someone to help.

lines.index: #section:Daelin Proudmoore. Grand Admiral of Kul Tiras.
lines.text: Daelin Proudmoore. Grand Admiral of Kul Tiras.
lines.title: Daelin Proudmoore

lines.index: #section:Daelin Proudmoore was the Lord Admiral of Kul Tiras and the father of Jaina Proudmoore. In the Second War his fleets ruled the seas for the Alliance, and he became one of the great heroes of humankind. He never forgave the orcs for that war. When he learned that they had settled on the shores of Kalimdor, he came with an armada to destroy them, and he died in the attempt.

When he learned that they had settled on the shores of Kalimdor, he came with an armada to destroy them, and he died in the attempt.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Daelin's war was the first great threat to the young nation of Durotar. His death drew a line between father and daughter, and between two ways of seeing the orcs: as a people who could change, or as monsters who never would. His men still hold Tiragarde Keep in his name.

lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:Kul Tiras was a kingdom of sailors, and the house of Proudmoore led its fleets. When the Horde marched north after the First War, Daelin brought his navy into the Alliance of Lordaeron. His ships fought the orcish fleets on the open sea and carried the armies of the Alliance from shore to shore. Kul Tiras paid dearly in ships and men. Daelin remembered that price for the rest of his life.

lines.title: The Admiral of the Alliance

lines.index: #section:After the Third War, his daughter Jaina led the survivors of Lordaeron west to Kalimdor and built the city of Theramore. There she made peace with Thrall. Daelin would not accept it. He sailed to Kalimdor with a great fleet, raised Tiragarde Keep on the coast of Durotar, and made war on the orcs and on the trolls of the Echo Isles. The Horde answered. Its warriors broke the keep, and at last they carried the fight to the walls of Theramore itself. Jaina stood aside. In the fighting, the admiral was slain.

The orcs of Razor Hill read in it a simple warning: the admiral was dead, but his war was not.

lines.index: #section:Mulgore.
lines.text: Mulgore.
lines.title: Mulgore

lines.index: #section:Mulgore is the homeland of the tauren, a wide country of golden grass and gentle hills walled in by mountains on every side. Kodo herds graze its plains, and clear wells and lakes water the land. Over it all stand the great mesas of Thunder Bluff, the tauren capital, where the High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof keeps his lodge. To the tauren this is the gift of the Earth Mother, a peaceful land after centuries of wandering. Yet quilboar, gnolls, harpies and goblins press in from every edge, and the young of the tribes must prove themselves against them.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:For countless generations the tauren were nomads who followed the herds across the plains of Kalimdor. The centaur hunted them without mercy, drove them from their old lands and scattered their tribes. Cairne of the Bloodhoof set himself to gather his people and lead them to a land where they could live in safety.

lines.index: #section:The centaur were driven out, but Mulgore is not at rest. The Bristleback quilboar war on the young tauren of Red Cloud Mesa and defile the burial ground of Red Rocks. Palemane gnolls hunt the wildlife to ruin and answer every word of peace with blades. Windfury harpies nest on the ridges. The goblins of the Venture Company have poisoned the sacred wells and dug a mine into the eastern cliffs, and dwarves dig for old secrets in the west. In these days a band of Galak centaur has been seen again inside the borders, and a Longwalker sent to watch the east did not come home. In the north-west, the shamans of the Earthen Ring have raised a camp where a strange people arrives from the sky: Skyborne elves of the Windshapers, come down from Skywall to seek new allies.

lines.index: #section:• The Long March. Near the shores of the Great Sea, the young warchief Thrall came upon Cairne's people under centaur attack. The orcs escorted the tauren caravans across The Barrens to Mulgore, and in return Cairne showed Thrall the way to the Oracle of Stonetalon. • The Third War. Cairne pledged his people to the Horde, and tauren warriors fought beside the orcs at the Battle of Mount Hyjal. • The Claiming of Mulgore. With the help of the Horde, the tauren broke the centaur's hold on the plains and made Mulgore a permanent home for all their tribes. On the mesas they raised Thunder Bluff.

lines.index: #section:Red Cloud Mesa.
lines.text: Red Cloud Mesa.
lines.title: Red Cloud Mesa

lines.index: #section:Red Cloud Mesa is the high tableland in the south of Mulgore, where young tauren take their first steps as hunters. Plainstriders and mountain cougars roam its grass, and the elders say that its people pride themselves on keen hunting above all else. A well lies south-east of the camp, where the Greatmother of the Hawkwinds draws water. In the hills to the south the seer Graytongue keeps his abode, and above the far south-eastern slopes stands a shrine to An'she and Mu'sha. East of the mesa opens Brambleblade Ravine, from which the Bristleback quilboar come by night to ambush hunters and steal from the camp.

lines.index: #section:Camp Narache.
lines.text: Camp Narache.
lines.title: Camp Narache

lines.index: #section:Camp Narache is the camp of Chief Hawkwind on Red Cloud Mesa. It is a place of tents, totems and cookfires, and it is where the young of the tribe begin the Rites of the Earthmother. The chief teaches that every member of the tribe has a place in the balance of living things, and that the elders take note even of humble work. His son Grull tests the young hunters. The camp lives under threat, for the Bristleback warchief has drawn up plans to lay siege to it. Those who prove themselves here follow the road north to Bloodhoof Village.

lines.index: #section:Brambleblade Ravine.
lines.text: Brambleblade Ravine.
lines.title: Brambleblade Ravine

lines.index: #section:Brambleblade Ravine cuts into the hills east of Red Cloud Mesa. It is choked with thorns, and in it the Bristleback quilboar have built a rough village. From here their raiders creep onto the mesa to ambush the hunting parties of Camp Narache. The quilboar train battleboars in the ravine and teach them to be vicious. Their chief, Sharptusk Thornmantle, keeps his hut at the ravine's heart, and the tauren of Narache say that his war on them has cost many lives since they came to this land.

lines.index: #section:Bloodhoof Village lies in the heart of Mulgore, on the road between Red Cloud Mesa and Thunder Bluff. It is the village of Cairne's own tribe, and his son Baine leads it as chief. Around its great fire gather the tribe's teachers: the shaman Mull Thunderhorn, who cleanses the poisoned wells, the spiritual leader Zarlman Two-Moons, the warrior Ruul Eagletalon and the hunters Harken Windtotem and Skorn Whitecloud. Its inn welcomes travellers. From Bloodhoof the young tauren go out to the wells, the mine and the gnoll camps, and those who pass the Rite of Vision set out from here toward the city.

lines.index: #section:Water Wells of Mulgore.
lines.text: Water Wells of Mulgore.
lines.title: Water Wells of Mulgore

lines.index: #section:Three sacred wells water the plains of Mulgore, each named for a tauren clan. The Winterhoof Water Well lies south-east of Bloodhoof Village, the Thunderhorn Water Well to its north, and the Wildmane Water Well north of Thunder Bluff. The wells give life to the tauren and to the beasts they depend on. The goblins of the Venture Company and their servants have fouled all three. To cleanse them, the shaman Mull Thunderhorn makes a totem for each from what the land itself offers, and a ritual must then be performed at the well, often under the eyes of goblin guards.

lines.index: #section:The Venture Co. Mine.
lines.text: The Venture Co. Mine.
lines.title: The Venture Co. Mine

lines.index: #section:The Venture Co. Mine is cut into the eastern cliffs of Mulgore, north-east of Stonebull Lake. Here the goblins of the Venture Company dig ore and minerals from tauren land without leave. Their supervisor, Fizsprocket, kept plans for driving the tauren out of Mulgore altogether, so that the company could plunder the plains at will. His notes speak also of shredders, great machines that can fell a forest in days, and of the company's plans to spread further across the land.

lines.index: #section:Ravaged Caravan.
lines.text: Ravaged Caravan.
lines.title: Ravaged Caravan

lines.index: #section:The Ravaged Caravan lies on the northern shore of Stonebull Lake. It was a Venture Company train travelling under guard, and the tauren, who had lost two of their own to the goblins in an earlier fight, fell upon it and burned it. They left the supply crates behind, thinking the fire had spoiled them. It had not. The crates held ore taken from Mulgore and a sheaf of papers that revealed the size of the company's mining in the tauren lands.

lines.index: #section:Palemane Rock.
lines.text: Palemane Rock.
lines.title: Palemane Rock

lines.index: #section:Palemane Rock is a cave in the western hills of Mulgore, the lair of the Palemane gnolls. From here the gnolls go out to poach the herds, skin their kills and tan the hides, taking far more than the land can give. The tauren tried to speak with them and were met with scorn. In these days the High Chieftain sent a Longwalker, Perith Stormhoof, to try once more. The gnolls answered with violence, and Perith was held inside the rock, fearing that he would become their feast.

lines.index: #section:Bael'dun Digsite.
lines.text: Bael'dun Digsite.
lines.title: Bael'dun Digsite

lines.index: #section:The Bael'dun Digsite lies in the west of Mulgore, north-west of Bloodhoof Village. Dwarves have raised a camp here and are digging into the earth, with diggers to break the ground and appraisers to judge what they find. They believe that secrets lie buried in Mulgore. Chief Baine Bloodhoof does not doubt it. He holds only that tearing open and fouling the earth is the wrong way to learn its secrets, and he has asked that the dwarves' digging tools be taken and smashed.

lines.index: #section:Red Rocks.
lines.text: Red Rocks.
lines.title: Red Rocks

lines.index: #section:Red Rocks is the sacred burial ground of the tauren, in the north-east of Mulgore beyond Thunder Bluff. Only the most valiant are laid to rest here: the warriors who helped found and defend the city, and those who gave their lives for their tribes and chieftains. Ancestral spirits dwell among the stones, and it is here that young tauren who have drunk the Water of the Seers come to receive the blessing of their forebears. The old Lorekeeper Raintotem watches over the graves. Bristleback raiders have lately come onto the holy ground to ravage it.

lines.index: #section:Windfury Ridge.
lines.text: Windfury Ridge.
lines.title: Windfury Ridge

lines.index: #section:Windfury Ridge is the high northern rim of Mulgore, where the plains climb toward the mountains. It is the stronghold of the Windfury harpies. Their matriarchs and sorceresses roost among the crags, and their witches call on the wind. The tauren count the harpies among the natural enemies of Mulgore, yet they also prize the azure and bronze feathers of the northern flocks for the headdresses worn before the High Chieftain. The harpy Sister Hatelash is said to lead the flocks of the north-west.

lines.index: #section:The Golden Plains.
lines.text: The Golden Plains.
lines.title: The Golden Plains

lines.index: #section:The Golden Plains spread east of Thunder Bluff, a sea of tall grass between the city and the eastern cliffs. Flatland cougars hunt here, and the old strider Mazzranache is said to roam the same country. Now and then a great white wolf called Ghost Howl crosses these plains, its hide still scarred from battle with demons. The goblins of the Venture Company cut their roads across the grass between their mine and the wells. In these days one of their shredders has been seen on the plains, a machine the tauren will not suffer to fell a single tree of Mulgore.

lines.index: #section:Camp Gev'rek.
lines.text: Camp Gev'rek.
lines.title: Camp Gev'rek

lines.index: #section:Camp Gev'rek stands on Skywatcher Plateau in the north-west of Mulgore. It is a gathering of the Earthen Ring: tauren shamans, a troll, even one of the Grimtotem, led by Muln Earthfury and the elder farseer Nuara Tremorhoof. Here the skycutter ships of the Windshapers come down from Zephras Isle, bringing Skyborne elves to a world they have never seen. Alaana Stormwalker greets each new arrival. Beside the camp a goblin trader, a priestess of An'she and handlers of the Skyborne galestriders have set up their stalls.

He sets the first of the Rites of the Earthmother before the young, and he sends those who pass on to Baine Bloodhoof.

lines.index: #section:Greatmother Hawkwind is the mother of Chief Hawkwind. Each morning she walks to the well south-east of Camp Narache to fetch water for the tribe. One morning she was gone so long that her son began to worry. Her legs have lost the strength they once had, but she will not give up her duties. She simply takes a little longer than she used to.

He is patient with those who would share the land, and stern with those who will not. He has seen many of the conflicts that wound the world, and he hopes the young of his tribe will see fewer.

The swoops fly anywhere in Mulgore, he says, but only sharp eyes will spot them and only quick hooves will catch them.

lines.index: #section:Mull Thunderhorn is a shaman of Bloodhoof Village. When the goblins and their servants poisoned the sacred wells of Mulgore, he would not let it stand. For each well he makes a cleansing totem from what the land offers, the paws, talons, claws and teeth of its beasts, so that a ritual can wash the poison away.

lines.index: #section:Mull is the healer of Mulgore's waters. His work restores life to the wells on which the tauren and the wild beasts alike depend.

lines.title: Morin Cloudstalker

lines.index: #section:Morin Cloudstalker walks the road east of Bloodhoof Village and watches the goblins of the Venture Company. It was his band that burned their caravan on the shore of Stonebull Lake. He thinks the company greedy and grown too fast, and he will not allow its work on tauren land.

lines.text: Zarlman Two-Moons. Spiritual Leader of Bloodhoof.
lines.title: Zarlman Two-Moons

lines.index: #section:Zarlman Two-Moons is the spiritual leader of Bloodhoof Village. He guides the young through the Rite of Vision. From well stones gathered at Mulgore's wells and ambercorn fallen beneath its great trees, he brews the Water of the Seers. Drunk before the tribal fire, it calls forth a vision that the young must follow.

The vision that rises from the fire at Bloodhoof leads them across the plains to him, and he always seems to know they are coming. He sends them on to the ancestral spirits of Red Rocks for the Rite of Wisdom.

lines.text: Ruul Eagletalon. Warrior and Teacher.
lines.title: Ruul Eagletalon

lines.index: #section:Ruul Eagletalon calls himself a warrior and a teacher. He watches for the moment when a young tauren is ready to go further than the plains of home. He holds that a tauren must prepare for trials before venturing much further than home. Those who wish to test their strength he sends against the Windfury harpies, whom he counts among the natural enemies of Mulgore.

lines.text: Skorn Whitecloud. Hunter of Bloodhoof.
lines.title: Skorn Whitecloud

lines.index: #section:Skorn Whitecloud is an old hunter of Bloodhoof Village. He once felt the same lust to wander that he sees in the young, and he holds that hunting is a tauren's greatest honor. Those who would walk the hunter's path he sends to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff, bearing the claws of the flatland prowlers of Mulgore, tough and cunning prey fit for a young hunter.

lines.text: Lorekeeper Raintotem. Keeper of Red Rocks.
lines.title: Lorekeeper Raintotem

lines.index: #section:Lorekeeper Raintotem watches over Red Rocks, the sacred burial ground of the tauren. He knows the names of the valiant who lie there, the founders and defenders of Thunder Bluff. To be buried at Red Rocks is the greatest honor the tribes can give. He is old now and past his prime, and when Bristleback raiders came to ravage the graves, he could not drive them off himself.

lines.text: Brave Wildrunner. Brave of Bloodhoof.
lines.title: Brave Wildrunner

lines.index: #section:Brave Wildrunner guards Bloodhoof Village. When the Longwalker Malah Longwind did not return from the eastern border after three days, it fell to him to learn what had happened. His duty kept him at the village, so he sent another in his place. The news that came back was the worst he could have heard. Malah had been found dead near the eastern edge of Mulgore, with centaur arrows in her back and her report still clenched in her hand.

lines.text: Perith Stormhoof. Longwalker of the High Chieftain.
lines.title: Perith Stormhoof

lines.index: #section:Perith Stormhoof is a Longwalker, one of the trusted scouts of the High Chieftain. Cairne sent him to Palemane Rock to speak with the gnolls who had settled there. The gnolls met his words with violence and held him in their cave. The rest of his errand he keeps secret, as all Longwalkers must.

lines.text: Alaana Stormwalker. Windshaper of Camp Gev'rek.
lines.title: Alaana Stormwalker

lines.index: #section:Alaana Stormwalker is a Skyborne of the Windshapers who came down to Mulgore before most of her people. She waits at Camp Gev'rek to receive each skycutter from Zephras Isle. She welcomes the newcomers gladly, warns them that the world below is as dangerous as it is wondrous, and tells them that their new allies are the key to their people's survival.

lines.text: Muln Earthfury. Elder of the Earthen Ring.
lines.title: Muln Earthfury

lines.index: #section:Muln Earthfury is a tauren shaman and a leader of the Earthen Ring, the council that keeps the balance of the Elements. In these days his duty to the spirits took him beyond the world itself, to Skywall, the realm of the air. There he answered the call of the Windshapers, and when he returned he brought them with him.

In these days his duty to the spirits took him beyond the world itself, to Skywall, the realm of the air. There he answered the call of the Windshapers, and when he returned he brought them with him.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Muln is the bridge between the Skyborne and Azeroth. Through him the Windshapers found the Earthen Ring, and through the Ring they found the Horde. The elves who come down to Mulgore are his guests, and they know the world at first through his camp and his counsel.

lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He answered the plea of the Windshaper leader Ayessa Dawnsinger, whose home was failing. • He went with shamans of the Earthen Ring to Zephras Isle to aid the Skyborne. • He faced one of the great lords of the wind and told it that the Ring had no quarrel with it. • He warned the Windshapers of the elemental lords, and of good reason to fear Al'Akir. • He opened a road of skycutter ships between Zephras Isle and Mulgore. • He keeps the camp on Skywatcher Plateau where the newcomers arrive.

lines.index: #section:Little is written of Muln's life before these days. The chronicles of this age do not record when he rose to lead the Ring, or how Ayessa first reached him across the planes.

lines.title: Unrecorded

lines.index: #section:Help from Below. The Windshapers had sent for help, and it was slow to come. When Muln and the shamans of the Earthen Ring arrived at last, the battle against the cult of the High Priestess Lorthuna was already raging. He asked Ayessa's pardon for coming late. When the Lord of the East Wind came upon them, Muln spoke for the Ring: they had no quarrel with him, and asked only to be left in peace. When the battle was over, he returned at once to Azeroth.

lines.index: #section:The Warning. Muln told Ayessa much of the elemental lords. What he told her left her afraid. The wards that had hidden Zephras Isle were gone, and nothing stood between the island and Al'Akir in his own domain. The High Elder of the Skyborne took a longer view: to an elemental lord, years or even decades might pass before he turned his eyes their way.

lines.text: Mazzranache. The Red-Eyed Strider.
lines.title: Mazzranache

lines.index: #section:Mazzranache is a strider of the plains of Mulgore, spoken of in the tales of the Bloodhoof hunters. He has demonic red eyes, razor talons and a venomous bite. Maur Raincaller's grandfather fought him long ago, and now Maur bears the mark of his bite himself. He roams the plains east of Thunder Bluff and is not easily found.

lines.title: Ghost Howl

lines.index: #section:Ghost Howl is a great white wolf who wanders the plains of Mulgore. His ragged hide bears a terrible wound. It is said that he took it in battle against the Burning Legion, and it has marked him ever since. He is seen now beneath the bluffs of Thunder Bluff, now on the eastern plains, now far in the north.

lines.text: Herak the Pillager. Raider of the Galak.
lines.title: Herak the Pillager

lines.index: #section:Herak the Pillager leads a small raiding party of Galak centaur that has crept into Mulgore from the east. His riders killed the Longwalker Malah Longwind with arrows in the back and raised a camp inside the tauren borders. Herak claims the plains for the Galak and swears vengeance on the tauren. His riders meant to rest before they struck at Bloodhoof Village, and to send to the Barrens for more.

lines.text: Bristleback Quilboar.
lines.title: Bristleback Quilboar

lines.index: #section:The Bristlebacks are the tribe of quilboar who live in Mulgore. They were there before the tauren settled the plains, and they have been at war with them ever since. From their thorny village in Brambleblade Ravine they strike at Red Cloud Mesa, and their raiders reach as far north as the burial ground of Red Rocks.

lines.index: #section:The Bristlebacks fight from ambush. Their warriors lie in wait for tauren hunting parties and steal into Camp Narache by dark. Their shamans fight beside them. lines.text: Palemane Gnolls.
lines.title: Palemane Gnolls

lines.index: #section:The Palemane are a tribe of gnolls who have settled in Mulgore. They lair in the cave of Palemane Rock in the western hills and keep camps south of Bloodhoof Village. They are poachers, skinners and tanners, and they slay the wildlife of the plains without restraint.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The tauren tried to share the land with them. Again and again they sought to speak with the gnolls, and each time they were met with disrespect. Chief Baine Bloodhoof at last judged that words were no longer the answer. Even so, the High Chieftain made one more attempt in these days, and sent his Longwalker Perith Stormhoof to them. The gnolls seized him and held him in their cave.

lines.title: Windfury Harpies

lines.index: #section:The Windfury are the harpies of Mulgore. Their flocks nest on the mountain edges of the south-east, away from the roads, and above all on Windfury Ridge in the far north. The tauren count them among the natural enemies of their land.
lines.text: The Windfury are the harpies of Mulgore. Their flocks nest on the mountain edges of the south-east, away from the roads, and above all on Windfury Ridge in the far north. The tauren count them among the natural enemies of their land.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The Windfury flocks are ruled by matriarchs, and their witches and sorceresses command the wind. They prey on whatever walks below their roosts. Their plumage is prized by the tauren: the azure and bronze feathers of the northern flocks are used for the headdresses that young tauren wear when they stand before the High Chieftain.

lines.text: Longwalkers.
lines.title: Longwalkers

lines.index: #section:The Longwalkers are the most trusted scouts of the tauren. They answer to the High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof alone, and they carry his most secret errands. A Longwalker can be known by a headband and a feathered staff. Even the chief of Bloodhoof Village, Cairne's own son, may only ask for their help.

lines.index: #section:Secrecy is the first law of the Longwalkers. They travel alone, they do not speak of their missions, and when one is saved from danger he goes on alone rather than tell anyone where he is going. When a Longwalker does not return from a watch, the braves of the nearest village must go and learn why.

lines.index: #section:The Rites of the Earthmother are the trials by which a young tauren earns the respect of the elders of Thunder Bluff. There are three: the Rite of Strength, the Rite of Vision and the Rite of Wisdom. Together they lead from the first camp on Red Cloud Mesa to the lodge of the High Chieftain.

lines.index: #section:• The Rite of Strength. Drunk before the tribal fire, it calls up a vision of the plains that leads the drinker to the seer Wiserunner. • The Rite of Wisdom. At Red Rocks, the ancestral spirits give their blessing to those who have drunk the Water of the Seers.

lines.index: #section:Westfall.
lines.text: Westfall.
lines.title: Westfall

lines.index: #section:Westfall is a land of wide golden plains between Elwynn Forest and the Great Sea. For generations its farms filled the granaries of the Kingdom of Stormwind, and the folk of the capital called it their breadbasket. Now the fields lie untended. Windmills turn over empty barns, strange machines walk the furrows, and men in red masks rule the roads. Most of the farmers have gone. Those who remain have learned that no army is coming, and that they must defend their homes themselves.

Windmills turn over empty barns, strange machines walk the furrows, and men in red masks rule the roads. Most of the farmers have gone. Those who remain have learned that no army is coming, and that they must defend their homes themselves.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records the year when the first farmers ploughed the plains west of Stormwind. What is known is that the land was rich in more than grain. Beneath its hills lay mines and quarries that fed the forges of the capital, and the greatest of them, beneath the village of Moonbrook, was once the richest gold works in all the human lands. The coast gave fish to the villages and danger to the ships, and a lighthouse was raised on the southern rocks to guide sailors past them.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Westfall belongs to the Defias Brotherhood in all but name. The Brotherhood holds Moonbrook, the mines and the southern hills. It drove the farmers from their homes, sometimes by threat and sometimes by fire, and it now works the land for its own ends. Riverpaw gnolls and kobolds labour in the mines at its command. Stormwind has sent no soldiers. Its army is marshalled far away, and the regent's court has answered the pleas of Westfall with silence. On Sentinel Hill, a veteran named Gryan Stoutmantle has raised the People's Militia from farmers who refused to leave. They are few, but they are the only law in Westfall.

lines.title: The Present Day

lines.index: #section:• The farmers of Westfall. A handful of families, such as the Saldeans, hold their land against every danger. Others, like the Furlbrows, have packed what they could and turned toward the city. • The People's Militia. Former farmers and returned soldiers under Gryan Stoutmantle, sworn to defend the plains in the name of the Holy Light. • The Defias Brotherhood. Thieves, smugglers and pillagers in red bandanas. The colour and cloth of the bandana mark a member's rank. • The Riverpaw gnolls. They raid the fields and dig in the Gold Coast Quarry on behalf of the Brotherhood. • Murlocs. The murloc tribes swarm along the whole length of the coast. • The harvest golems. Machines built to tend the crops now drive off anyone who comes near them.

lines.title: Inhabitants

lines.index: #section:• The Years of Plenty. Westfall's grain and gold made it one of the pillars of the kingdom. • The First War. When the Horde razed Stormwind in the First War, the great gold mine beneath Moonbrook was abandoned. It took the name of the Deadmines. • The Betrayal of the Masons. After the Second War, the Stonemasons' Guild rebuilt the capital and was cheated of its wages by the House of Nobles. Driven from the city, the masons came west under Edwin VanCleef and made Westfall their own. • The Abandonment. One by one, the farms fell. Stormwind did not answer. Gryan Stoutmantle, home from the ruin of Lordaeron, began to gather those who would stand and fight.

lines.index: #section:Sentinel Hill.
lines.text: Sentinel Hill.
lines.title: Sentinel Hill

lines.index: #section:Sentinel Hill rises in the middle of Westfall, just off the great road. On its crown stands a stone watchtower, and around it a small village has gathered for safety: an inn, the stalls of the MacGregor family and the posts of the militia. This is the headquarters of the People's Militia. From the top of the tower Gryan Stoutmantle and his officers watch the plains and send out their scouts. It is the last place in Westfall where the law of Stormwind is still spoken aloud, though Stormwind itself sends nothing to enforce it.

lines.index: #section:Moonbrook.
lines.text: Moonbrook.
lines.title: Moonbrook

lines.index: #section:Moonbrook was once a prosperous village in the south of Westfall. Its people are gone. The Defias Brotherhood took the town and made it the heart of its power, and its empty houses now shelter thieves and their captains. Only one trader works openly in Moonbrook, a Defias merchant who sells to anyone with coin and asks no questions. Beneath the town lies the old gold mine that the war left behind: the Deadmines. The masons of Edwin VanCleef guard its entrance, for what they are building in the depths is the Brotherhood's greatest secret.

lines.index: #section:Jangolode Mine.
lines.text: Jangolode Mine.
lines.title: Jangolode Mine

lines.index: #section:Jangolode Mine lies in the north-west of Westfall, in the hills above the Furlbrow farm. It was one of the mines that sent ore to Stormwind. The Defias hold it now, and their trappers prowl the land around its mouth. Inside, the Brotherhood has set kobolds to dig for it. They work under a master digger of their own kind. Some who have studied the sickness of the plains first looked for its source here, among the tailings of the mine.

lines.index: #section:Gold Coast Quarry.
lines.text: Gold Coast Quarry.
lines.title: Gold Coast Quarry

lines.index: #section:The Gold Coast Quarry lies on the western edge of Westfall, where the plains fall toward the sea. It gave both stone and gold to the kingdom. Now Defias pillagers hold it, and the Riverpaw gnolls toil in its pits under the lash of their own taskmasters. The gnolls do not dig for themselves. They dig for the Brotherhood, whose allies they have become across the plains. Driving the pillagers from the quarry is one of the trials that the People's Militia sets for those who would join its ranks.

lines.index: #section:Alexston Farmstead.
lines.text: Alexston Farmstead.
lines.title: Alexston Farmstead

lines.index: #section:The Alexston Farmstead is one of the old family farms of central Westfall. Its family has fled, and its fields have gone to the harvest golems, which still walk the rows as though a crop were waiting to be gathered. Bands of Defias pillagers and looters pass through the farmstead as they move between the quarry and Moonbrook, and they take whatever the last owners left behind. Clearing them from the farmstead is among the first tasks the People's Militia sets for those who wish to join it.

lines.index: #section:Saldean's Farm.
lines.text: Saldean's Farm.
lines.title: Saldean's Farm

lines.index: #section:Saldean's Farm lies north of Sentinel Hill, just beyond a fork in the great road. It is one of the few farms in Westfall whose owners have not fled. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma have watched their neighbours leave one after another, and still they keep their house, their kitchen and their wagon. The wagon nearly went the way of everything else when a Defias thief tried to steal it. He was caught, and to save his life he offered the militia the one thing it most wanted: the way to the Brotherhood's hideout.

lines.index: #section:Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm.
lines.text: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm.
lines.title: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm

lines.index: #section:Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm lies in the north of Westfall, near the Jangolode Mine. It belonged to Theodore and Verna Furlbrow until the night their fields filled with thieves. The Furlbrows fled in such haste that Theodore left his most treasured possession, a pocket watch, in the wardrobe of the farmhouse. The Defias took the farm and the deed to it as well. Now pumpkins rot in the field, and harvest golems stand guard over a crop that no one will ever gather.

lines.index: #section:The Dagger Hills.
lines.text: The Dagger Hills.
lines.title: The Dagger Hills

lines.index: #section:The Dagger Hills are the broken highlands of southern Westfall, behind Moonbrook and above the sea. Here the hardest of the Brotherhood's fighters make their camps: highwaymen who rob the roads, pathstalkers who know every trail, and brawlers who settle quarrels with their fists. The militia believes that Defias raiders who escape its patrols go to ground in these hills to plan their next attack. On the far side of the hills, near the water, a hidden way leads out of the depths of the Deadmines. Only those who have passed through the mines know where it lies.

lines.index: #section:Westfall Lighthouse.
lines.text: Westfall Lighthouse.
lines.title: Westfall Lighthouse

lines.index: #section:The Westfall Lighthouse stands on the south-western point of the land, above rocks that have broken many ships. Its keeper and his family once tended the flame. Twice the murlocs of the coast came for them, led by a great murloc called Old Murk-Eye. The first time the family fled and the light went dark, and a ship's captain died upon the rocks that night. The second time the family did not escape. The light still burns, because the drowned captain will not let it fail.

lines.index: #section:The Dead Acre.
lines.text: The Dead Acre.
lines.title: The Dead Acre

lines.index: #section:The Dead Acre lies in the south-east of Westfall, near the bridge that leads into Duskwood. It was once a farm like the others. When the Brotherhood came, the house and the fields were put to the torch, and only blackened ruins remain. The harvest machines that walk its smoking rows are the most dangerous in Westfall, great reapers that no farmer would dare approach. Defias highwaymen keep watch among the burned buildings. Of the family who once lived here, no record remains.

lines.index: #section:The Molsen Farm.
lines.text: The Molsen Farm.
lines.title: The Molsen Farm

lines.index: #section:The Molsen Farm is one of the abandoned homesteads of northern Westfall. Its family is gone, and Defias trappers have been seen about its fields. The well of the farm still gives water, but the water is no longer clean. Those who have tested it find metals in it that belong in a smelter, not in a farmer's bucket. Whatever is poisoning the soil of Westfall has reached the Molsen well, and it is spreading through the ground from somewhere else.

lines.index: #section:The Jansen Stead.
lines.text: The Jansen Stead.
lines.title: The Jansen Stead

lines.index: #section:The Jansen Stead is the northernmost farm of Westfall, close to the bridge that crosses into Elwynn. It is the first farm a traveller from Stormwind sees, and the first sign of how far the land has fallen. Its owners were driven off like so many others, and harvest golems and Defias hold the fields. Near the road, the Furlbrows wait beside their broken wagon for the chance to leave Westfall for good. The stead's well, like that of the Molsen Farm, has been found to carry poison.

lines.index: #section:Longshore.
lines.text: Longshore.
lines.title: Longshore

lines.index: #section:Longshore is the long western coast of Westfall, a strand of sand and rock beside the Great Sea. The wrecks of many ships lie along it, half buried in the sand. The coast belongs to the murlocs. Their villages crowd the beaches, and their raiders strike at anyone who walks the shore. The worst of them is Old Murk-Eye, who once led the murlocs against the Westfall Lighthouse. Among the wrecks, a rusty anchor marks the place where the drowned Captain Sanders is said to have left the first clue to his treasure.

lines.index: #section:Gryan Stoutmantle. Leader of the People's Militia.
lines.text: Gryan Stoutmantle. Leader of the People's Militia.
lines.title: Gryan Stoutmantle

lines.index: #section:Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People's Militia from the watchtower on Sentinel Hill. He came home from the tainted lands of Lordaeron to find his homeland overrun by thieves and forgotten by its king. He did not wait for help. He gathered the farmers who would not leave, gave them weapons, and made them swear to defend Westfall in the name of the Holy Light.

lines.index: #section:Stoutmantle is the answer of ordinary people to a kingdom that has abandoned them. It is his militia, not the army of Stormwind, that uncovers the truth of the Defias Brotherhood and hunts its master to his lair.

lines.index: #section:• He founded the People's Militia and inducts its members himself. • He sends his scouts after the Defias across the whole of Westfall. • He refused a plea for aid from Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire, for he had no men to spare. • He led the hunt for Edwin VanCleef.

lines.index: #section:The Militia of Sentinel Hill. The militia takes no one on words alone. Its pledges must first drive the Defias from the farms, then from the quarry, and at last from the southern hills. Only then does Stoutmantle induct them, speaking of the ruin he left behind in Lordaeron and the hope he still has for Westfall.

His old comrades want his head, and he will not walk the road without someone to guard his back.

She followed the poison through the mines and the quarry, and at last to Moonbrook, where she found signs of great works beneath the ground.

lines.index: #section:Loch Modan.
lines.text: Loch Modan.
lines.title: Loch Modan

lines.index: #section:Loch Modan is a broad basin of hills and pine woods in Khaz Modan, east of Dun Morogh. At its heart lies the Loch, the great lake that gives the land its name, held back at its northern end by the Stonewrought Dam. The town of Thelsamar stands near its western shore. Dwarven towers keep the passes that run west to Ironforge, north to the Wetlands and south toward the Searing Gorge. It is a gentler country than the snows of Dun Morogh, rich in ore, game and fish, and the dwarves of the Kingdom of Ironforge have long held it as their own.

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records when the dwarves first settled the shores of the Loch, or when the Stonewrought Dam was raised. The land is old in their history. In the Valley of Kings, two great statues stand guard over the southern road. They honor Madoran Bronzebeard and Khardros Wildhammer, who led their clans in the age of the War of the Three Hammers. It is told that their sons raised the statues after that war to watch over the road to the south, as a warning to any who would march on the dwarven realms again.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Loch Modan is a land under siege, and its defenders are few. The Ironforge Reserve has been called away to fight for the Alliance on distant fronts, and the reinforcements promised to the Loch have never come. Captain Rugelfuss holds the Valley of Kings with a single regiment, while the troggs of the Stonesplinter tribe boil out of the southern hills and overrun the Explorers' dig beside the lake. Ogres of the Mo'grosh clan raid from the north-east. Kobolds have taken the Silver Stream Mine. Worst of all, Dark Iron saboteurs have crept up to the dam itself, and they have friends among those the dwarves trust. In Thelsamar, Magistrate Bluntnose has been told that he must wait months for a handful of soldiers. He has stopped waiting, and he pays in good coin any stranger who will fight.

Dwarves, humans and a high elf keep a hunting lodge in the eastern hills. • The Stonesplinter troggs. They hold the southern valleys, the islands of the Loch and the ruins of the excavation. • The Mo'grosh ogres. Sappers and insurgents lurk about the dam, and at least one of their agents hid among the dwarves' own porters.

lines.index: #section:• The Three Hammers. After the war of the three clans, the kings of the Bronzebeards and the Wildhammers were remembered in stone at the southern gate of the Loch. • The Second War. When the Horde overran Khaz Modan in the Second War, the loch country fell under orcish rule. The dwarves won it back, but the wrecks of orcish catapults and wagons still lie in the shallows and behind the old silver mine. • The Excavation. The Explorers' League opened a dig among ancient ruins south-east of the Loch. Its diggers found strange carved idols, and soon after, the troggs came up out of the ground. • The Present Day. Now the Loch is guarded by the few who stayed behind, and by whatever help they can hire.

lines.title: Thelsamar

lines.index: #section:Thelsamar is the chief town of Loch Modan, a cluster of stone houses near the western shore of the lake. Its heart is the Stoutlager Inn, and the town is never short of hungry workers and running children. It has a forge, a gryphon roost and a branch of the Explorers' League, and a wanted poster for an ogre chieftain hangs in its street. Mountaineer Kadrell walks the road through town, and Magistrate Bluntnose keeps its order. Thelsamar lacks many comforts of Ironforge: its smith is always short of bronze, and he wishes some trader would bring coal to town.

lines.text: Stonewrought Dam.
lines.title: Stonewrought Dam

lines.index: #section:The Stonewrought Dam closes the northern end of the Loch, a wall of dwarven stone so vast that the lake itself rests against it. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII keeps it, with a few engineers and mountaineers. Most of its guards have been sent to the front, including its chief inspector. The loss is felt. The Dark Irons have already broken the Thandol Span and pillaged Dun Modr to the north, and Hinderweir is certain that the dam is next. Their sappers have been seen on its eastern ramp.

lines.title: Algaz Station

lines.index: #section:Algaz Station is the northern guard post of Loch Modan. Its tower stands where the tunnel of North Gate Pass comes down from Dun Morogh, and just south of Dun Algaz, the pass that leads on to the Wetlands. Many mountaineers are posted here. From the top of the tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches the roads and speaks gladly of his own exploits. An armorer and a travelling merchant serve the garrison. North of the station, the mountaineers guarding Dun Algaz have found the road ahead thick with orcs.

lines.title: Silver Stream Mine

lines.index: #section:The Silver Stream Mine lies in the north of Loch Modan, between Algaz Station and the dam. It gave the dwarves silver for many years before it ran dry. The Miners' League then turned it into a storehouse and filled it with crates of good dwarven tools. Now the Tunnel Rat kobolds have moved in and put their paws on everything. The mountaineers mean to clear the mine, but the League would like its gear carried out first, before the soldiers break it.

lines.text: Ironband's Excavation Site.
lines.title: Ironband's Excavation Site

lines.index: #section:Ironband's Excavation Site is a dig of the Explorers' League among ancient ruins south-east of the Loch. Prospector Ironband leads it, with Magmar Fellhew to manage the work. The diggers had just uncovered a great number of carved stone idols when the Stonesplinter troggs surfaced in the ruins and drove them out. The idols seem to draw the troggs and drive some of them berserk. The diggers fled so fast that they left most of their tools behind. A trogg chieftain and his shaman now rule the site.

lines.text: Mo'grosh Stronghold.
lines.title: Mo'grosh Stronghold

lines.index: #section:Mo'grosh Stronghold is a nest of caves in the hills north-east of the Loch. A clan of ogres has made its camp there, and from it they strike at Thelsamar, the dam and the excavation alike. They mine rare crystals in the caves. Not long ago they ambushed an ore caravan coming from the Wetlands and carried the ore into their camp. Their chieftain, Chok'sul, is wanted by the Magistrate of Thelsamar.

lines.index: #section:The Farstrider Lodge.
lines.text: The Farstrider Lodge.
lines.title: The Farstrider Lodge

lines.index: #section:The Farstrider Lodge stands in the eastern hills of Loch Modan. Its tall timbers and sweeping roofs are of elven style, and no chronicle records who raised it. Today it is a lodge of hunters, where the skill of the hunt is prized above all else. Marek Ironheart deals there in crocolisk skins and meat. A high elf, Vyrin Swiftwind, keeps her own counsel, and a young human named Daryl boasts to anyone who will listen. Traders sell bows and guns to those who come to hunt.

lines.index: #section:Valley of Kings.
lines.text: Valley of Kings.
lines.title: Valley of Kings

lines.index: #section:The Valley of Kings is the south-western corner of Loch Modan, where the road from South Gate Pass comes down into the green. Two great statues of dwarven kings, Madoran Bronzebeard and Khardros Wildhammer, stand over the valley and face the south. Nearby rises the southern guard tower of Captain Rugelfuss, whose regiment dares not leave its post for fear of invasion. Further south, a locked gate leads toward the Searing Gorge, and Mountaineer Pebblebitty opens it only for those who prove their worth.

lines.index: #section:The Loch.
lines.text: The Loch.
lines.title: The Loch

lines.index: #section:The Loch is the great lake of Khaz Modan, still and cold beneath the hills. Fishers work its western shore, and hunters seek the crocolisks that have dug in on its islands. Threshadons swim in its depths. The islands are not safe: troggs hold the largest of them, and they fell upon a gnomish flier who crashed into the water nearby. Old wreckage lies scattered along the shallows, and the fishers still find lost things among the debris.

lines.index: #section:Grizzlepaw Ridge.
lines.text: Grizzlepaw Ridge.
lines.title: Grizzlepaw Ridge

lines.index: #section:Grizzlepaw Ridge rises south of Thelsamar, between the town and the trogg country of the south-west. It belongs to the bears. Their dens are scattered along the slopes, and among them lairs a black bear of great size, Ol' Sooty, whom the hunters of the Farstrider Lodge have long tried and failed to bring down. Travellers on the road below keep an eye on the hills, for the old bear sometimes comes down.

lines.index: #section:Stonesplinter Valley.
lines.text: Stonesplinter Valley.
lines.title: Stonesplinter Valley

lines.index: #section:Stonesplinter Valley winds among the mountains of south-western Loch Modan, and it has given its name to the troggs who now crowd it. Their scouts watch the road, their seers and skullthumpers hold the southern hills, and their chieftain Grawmug keeps to the deepest of their caves. Mountaineers who patrol this country do not always return. It was here that Mountaineer Ylva went looking for one such lost patrol, and here that she fell.

lines.index: #section:South Gate Pass.
lines.text: South Gate Pass.
lines.title: South Gate Pass

lines.index: #section:South Gate Pass is the southern tunnel between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. It runs from the tower of South Gate Outpost in the west to the Valley of Kings in the east, and it is the shortest road from Ironforge to Thelsamar. The passage lies high, and snow gathers in it the whole year round. One shaman of the Loch has sent for a jar of it, for a working he did not explain. Mountaineers carry casks of stout through it from Dun Morogh.

lines.index: #section:Captain Rugelfuss. Captain of the Southern Tower.
lines.text: Captain Rugelfuss. Captain of the Southern Tower.
lines.title: Captain Rugelfuss

lines.index: #section:Captain Rugelfuss commands the regiment that guards the southern gate of Loch Modan, in the tower beneath the statues of the Valley of Kings. He has no patience for salutes. The Alliance is hard pressed abroad, he says, and that makes the dwarven lands all the more precious, while the troggs rising out of them are a grave danger to the king.

lines.index: #section:Rugelfuss is the soldier left holding the door. The Ironforge Reserve has been called to the front, and his few mountaineers cannot leave the gate without inviting invasion. So he fights the troggs in the only way left to him: by sending volunteers into the hills in his place.

lines.index: #section:The Stone Teeth. Bound to his gate, Rugelfuss could not carry the war into the hills himself. He asked instead for proof: the stone teeth of troggs slain beyond his walls. Every tooth laid on his table was one trogg fewer in the valley, and a small sign that the dwarves were not yet beaten.

lines.index: #section:The Chieftain of Stonesplinter. At last his scouts learned who led the rising. The troggs followed a chieftain called Grawmug, who never went anywhere without his two fiercest guards, Gnasher and Brawler. Rugelfuss wanted all three dead. Without their leaders, he judged, the troggs might at last be driven back into the ground.

When the banner was raised again, the trogg who had killed her came out to meet it and died. Rugelfuss took the standard back to be cleaned and hung in the tower. Ylva had never been one for caution, he said. Now at least they knew.

lines.text: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Keeper of the Stonewrought Dam.
lines.title: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII

lines.index: #section:Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII keeps the Stonewrought Dam, the great wall of stone that holds back the Loch. He is the seventh of his name to bear his title, and no chronicle records the six before him. He is a worried dwarf, and he has reason to be. His best inspector and most of his guards have been sent to the Alliance front, and the Dark Irons are moving in the north.

lines.index: #section:Hinderweir sees the pattern that others miss. First the Thandol Span was destroyed, then Dun Modr was pillaged. He has no doubt that the dam is the next target of the Dark Iron clan, and if it falls, the Loch falls with it.

lines.index: #section:A Clue on the Ramp. Dark Iron sappers had been seen on the eastern ramp of the dam. Among their leavings was a barrel of a strange-smelling powder. Hinderweir judged it an explosive of some kind, and he sent a sample north through the Algaz Gate to Ashlan Stonesmirk, the powder master of the regiment at Dun Modr, with orders to keep to the roads.

lines.index: #section:Seaforium. Stonesmirk knew the powder by its silver crystals and its smell: seaforium. Dry, it was harmless. Wet, it could tear a mountain apart. He sent back a disarming colloid, and word of what else was needed: the venom of the lurker spiders of the hills, the tear of a crocolisk and a rare crystal of the kind the Mo'grosh ogres mine.

The charge lay at the foot of the dam, under the water, and the mixture was stirred into it in time. The dam was saved. Hinderweir did not pretend that it was saved for good.

lines.index: #section:Prospector Darteus Ironband leads the Explorers' League dig among the ancient ruins south-east of the Loch. He is stout and honest, and he values results. Lately he has had few. The Stonesplinter troggs have overrun his site, his blastpowder never arrives, and one of his fellow prospectors in the south has fallen silent.

lines.index: #section:The Carved Idols. Ironband's report is short and patient. The dig goes on, slowed by troggs more aggressive than usual. Most finds are interesting and no more. One is not: the carved idols draw the troggs to them, and drive some of them berserk. More study is needed. And, once more, where is his blastpowder?

lines.index: #section:The Missing Powder. Jern Hornhelm had sent powder weeks before, and it never came. The next shipment went by porters along the curve of the Loch, and on the road the Dark Irons struck. One of the porters, Saean, was their man, though he had worked beside the others for nearly a year. When Miran brought the rest of the powder through at last, Ironband was glad of it, and troubled that the Dark Irons had friends able to lay hands on such things.

lines.title: Magistrate Bluntnose

lines.index: #section:Magistrate Bluntnose governs Thelsamar, and he is losing patience with Ironforge. It took two months to hear that the town would be spared a few soldiers, and he has been told it will be two more before they arrive. Meanwhile Thelsamar, the excavation and the dam stand open to attack.

He cannot understand why a dwarven armorer would choose to live among humans.

lines.index: #section:Mountaineer Rockgar guards the road where it enters Dun Algaz, the pass to the Wetlands. He called for volunteers to scout the pass, and the scouting soon turned bloody. Orcs of the Dragonmaw clan, who usually hide in the Wetland hills, have pushed into Dun Algaz itself. If they hold it, Loch Modan will be cut off from Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's port and stronghold in the north.

She wants proof that a traveller can survive what waits beyond, and she is a hard judge. The great beast Margol the Rager once carried her broken axe head in its horn, and she had hoped to kill it herself.

He sent the prospector plenty of blastpowder weeks ago, and he cannot understand where it went. Ironband is honest and gets results, Jern says, so when the results stop, he suspects that someone is working against him.

lines.index: #section:Bingles Blastenheimer is a gnome who was sent to fly over Gnomeregan and spy upon the lost city. He did not report back. His gyrocopter came down in the Loch instead, and troggs from a nearby island fell upon him and carried off his tools and his special Blastencapper explosives. His friends in Ironforge feared he had blown himself up. He finds that very unfair.

He is very proud of the scar over his eye, and always ready to tell how he got it.

lines.index: #section:Marek Ironheart is a dwarf hunter of the Farstrider Lodge, where hunting skill is prized above all else. He deals in the skins and meat of the Loch's famous crocolisks. He loves to tell of the day one of them nearly took his hand, until he jammed his knife into its jaws and scrambled free. He lost the knife in the struggle. The crocolisk, which he calls Daggerfang, still hunts the lake's edge.

lines.index: #section:Vidra Hearthstove feeds Thelsamar. There is never a shortage of empty bellies in town, from the children who run in and out to the diggers who come back from the excavation at night. Her blood sausages are famous across the Loch. She makes them from bear meat, stuffs them into boar casings and spices them with spider ichor, and she expects those who want them to fetch the makings.

Chok'sul keeps to the upper reaches of the Mo'grosh Stronghold in the north-east, and he greets strangers the way ogres do, by wondering whether they are good to eat.

Her helm was struck from her head by a spiked club. She had set out alone to find a patrol of mountaineers who never returned. She had sworn that the troggs would learn that Ironforge does not fall.

lines.title: Braldir Ashmantle

lines.index: #section:Braldir Ashmantle keeps the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, on a sacred peak reached by a hidden path in the crags of Loch Modan. Many who climb so high come for tales of treasure and find only stone and silence. Braldir lets no one walk the shrine who has not been sent. To those who walk the shaman's path, he teaches that fire is not only fury and ruin. It is the forge and the breath of creation, and every force needs another to temper it.

lines.title: Norric Lochthane

lines.index: #section:Norric Lochthane is a shaman who lives in a burrow hut on the north-western shore of the Loch, south of the Stonewrought Dam. He teaches the lesson of water: that it carves stone, cleanses filth and heals the weary, but only while it is pure. Tainted, it ruins all it touches. His teaching sends his students far afield, to a shaman's family in the Wetlands and to a fouled pond in Westfall.

lines.text: The Stonesplinter are the troggs of Loch Modan. They take their name from Stonesplinter Valley in the south-west, and they are the greatest danger the Loch faces. No chronicle records when they first came up from the deep places here.

lines.index: #section:They hold Stonesplinter Valley and the southern hills, where their chieftain Grawmug keeps the deepest cave. They have taken the largest island of the Loch. At Ironband's Excavation Site, where they surfaced among the ruins, a chieftain called Galgosh and a tribal shaman called Magosh rule the diggings. Their ranks hold scouts, skullthumpers and bonesnappers, and seers, shamans and geomancers who work a crude magic of the earth.

lines.index: #section:The Stonesplinter are drawn to the carved idols of the excavation, and some of them are driven berserk by the idols. Prospector Ironband hopes that the idols will one day explain the bond between the troggs and the titans. Until then, the mountaineers of the southern tower fight them with what little they have. They count the troggs they kill by their stone teeth.

lines.index: #section:The Mo'grosh are a clan of ogres who have made their home in the caves of the Mo'grosh Stronghold, in the north-east of Loch Modan. No chronicle records where they came from or when they settled there.
lines.text: The Mo'grosh are a clan of ogres who have made their home in the caves of the Mo'grosh Stronghold, in the north-east of Loch Modan. No chronicle records where they came from or when they settled there.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:They are brutes, enforcers and shamans, with mystics among them, and they follow a chieftain called Chok'sul. They mine crystals in their caves, rare enough that the dwarves must fight for a single one. They raid the roads of the Loch, and they are blamed for attacks on Thelsamar, the Stonewrought Dam and the excavation. They once ambushed an ore caravan bound for Thelsamar from the Wetlands and carried the ore off to their camp.

lines.text: The Tunnel Rats are the kobolds of Loch Modan. They have moved into the foothills west of Thelsamar and dug their dens along the mountainside, and they have taken the old Silver Stream Mine in the north.

lines.index: #section:They are diggers, foragers, scouts and surveyors, and their geomancers carry a fire tar that even the shamans of the Loch find useful. lines.index: #section:Silverpine Forest.
lines.text: Silverpine Forest.
lines.title: Silverpine Forest

lines.index: #section:Silverpine Forest runs south from the glades of Tirisfal to the great wall of Gilneas. Dark pines crowd its hills, and to the east its shores fall away into the grey water of Lordamere Lake. Once it was a quiet country of farms, orchards and mills. Now it is a land of the dead and the cursed. The Forsaken hold its roads from the Sepulcher, the Scourge hold an island fortress in the lake, and in the hills howl the wolf-men of a mad archmage of Dalaran.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records the year when the first humans settled Silverpine, or which lord first claimed it. Its people farmed the valleys, tended orchards and worked the mills. Above the hamlet of Pyrewood stood the keep of the noble Baron Silverlaine. When King Genn Greymane sealed his kingdom after the Second War, the Greymane Wall rose across the south of the forest, and the gates of Gilneas closed behind it. The folk of Silverpine were left on the northern side.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:The Dark Lady has given her lieutenant Varimathras the task of taking the lands to the south, and Silverpine is the first step. High Executor Hadrec commands the Forsaken at the Sepulcher, but his enemies are many. Rot Hide gnolls, raised and bound by the traitor mage Thule Ravenclaw, carry corpses out of Tirisfal to Fenris Isle. The worgen of Archmage Arugal hunt the woods, and the villagers of Pyrewood turn into beasts each night. At Ambermill, the wizards of Dalaran work on a secret of their own and guard the roads with a heavy hand. At the Greymane Wall, frightened human refugees gather before gates that will not open. In these days, the paladins of Tyr's Watch have sent an agent to the Sepulcher, and a traveller of the Skyborne has come to the forest, bringing grief with her.

They took Baron Silverlaine's keep, and Arugal made it his own. • The Forsaken. In time the Forsaken came south out of Tirisfal and made the Sepulcher their stronghold in the forest.

lines.index: #section:The Sepulcher.
lines.text: The Sepulcher.
lines.title: The Sepulcher

lines.index: #section:The Sepulcher is the stronghold of the Forsaken in Silverpine. It stands on a wooded hill in the heart of the forest, an old burial ground where the dead now keep watch over the living world. From here High Executor Hadrec sends out his Deathstalkers and the Deathguard hold the roads. A dead archmage studies the curse of the worgen, a shadow priest gathers every scrap of news, and an apothecary of the Society works on the new plague. Bats carry riders north to the Undercity. In these days the Sepulcher also shelters an envoy of Tyr's Watch and a young woman of the Skyborne.

lines.index: #section:Pyrewood Village.
lines.text: Pyrewood Village.
lines.title: Pyrewood Village

lines.index: #section:Pyrewood is a small village in the south of Silverpine, below the walls of Shadowfang Keep. By day it looks like any other human hamlet: a town hall, an inn, smiths and tailors at their work, and watchmen in the streets. When the sun goes down, its people become worgen. Arugal has laid enchanted shackles upon them all, and he rules the village through its own council, whose members are his puppets. In the inn lies the study of an apothecary who fell to the same curse. A Deathstalker hides in the town hall, waiting for the council to come home.

lines.index: #section:Ambermill.
lines.text: Ambermill.
lines.title: Ambermill

lines.index: #section:Ambermill is a village in the hills of south-eastern Silverpine, near the shore of Lordamere Lake. It was never an important place. Yet the magi of Dalaran have filled it with wizards, conjurers and armed warders, and they ship crates of maps and runed pendants to it by wagon from Hillsbrad. The Forsaken believe they know why. Ambermill lies over a sleeping node of ley energy, and an archmage has been working to wake it. What the Kirin Tor mean to do with such power, no one at the Sepulcher can say.

lines.index: #section:Fenris Isle.
lines.text: Fenris Isle.
lines.title: Fenris Isle

lines.index: #section:Fenris Isle lies in Lordamere Lake, east of the Decrepit Ferry. It is the stronghold of the Scourge in Silverpine. The Rot Hide gnolls swarm its shores and its ruined keep. A boat brings the corpses of Tirisfal across the water from the ferry, and on the island those corpses serve their new master. Vile Fin murlocs hunt its beaches, and moss-covered lake beasts crawl among the reeds. Of late the Deathguard have seen the gnolls throw a great body onto a pyre by the shore. It was the body of a tauren.

lines.index: #section:Fenris Keep.
lines.text: Fenris Keep.
lines.title: Fenris Keep

lines.index: #section:Fenris Keep is the fortress on Fenris Isle. Thule Ravenclaw rules there with his Rot Hide gnolls. In its yard, near the old stable, the gnolls buried a headless body in an unmarked grave. They kept the head as a toy. It still speaks. Alaric, the head servant of Thule, spent the best days of his life in this keep, and he knows its secrets, among them a hidden niche in the south-western tower. Of late the gnolls have also kept a living prisoner in a cage inside the walls.

lines.index: #section:The Decrepit Ferry.
lines.text: The Decrepit Ferry.
lines.title: The Decrepit Ferry

lines.index: #section:The Decrepit Ferry is an old landing on the shore of Lordamere Lake, east of the Sepulcher. It is rotten and nearly forgotten, but it is not idle. Servants of Thule Ravenclaw guard it, and Rot Hide gnolls come and go. In the boat moored there lie heaps of bodies wrapped for travel. Across the water, a second dock stands on Fenris Isle. The Forsaken have learned that the bodies come from the mass graves of Tirisfal, among them a woman of Brill named Deliah, and that they all end their journey on the island.

lines.text: The Dead Field.
lines.title: The Dead Field

lines.index: #section:The Dead Field is an abandoned farmstead in northern Silverpine. The Rot Hide gnolls have made it a camp, and the Deathstalkers who watched it thought the gnolls were readying for war. The Forsaken struck at them more than once, and each time they were routed by a banshee named Nightlash, who came to the gnolls' aid with her magic. Hadrec wanted her destroyed. It is said that when Nightlash falls, her essence turns to dust.

lines.text: The Ivar Patch.
lines.title: The Ivar Patch

lines.index: #section:The Ivar Patch was the farm of a man named Ivar, in the far north of Silverpine. When the plague came, Ivar, most of his family and his workers all fell and rose again among the Scourge. Ivar still haunts his barn as a ghoul. The Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick were ambushed here on their mission, and they made his old house their shelter. From its windows Rane keeps watch, while Quinn heals upstairs.

lines.text: Malden's Orchard.
lines.title: Malden's Orchard

lines.index: #section:Malden's Orchard lies in the far north-east of Silverpine, near the border of Tirisfal. Its trees stand unpicked, and whoever lived in its cottage is gone. Worgs now fill the orchard, so many that a Deathstalker sent to scout it was trapped inside the cottage for days. The worgs watched the door and waited for him to come out. Among them hunts a great black worg known as Gorefang.

lines.text: Valgan's Field.
lines.title: Valgan's Field

lines.index: #section:Valgan's Field is a wheat farm in northern Silverpine, just north of a bridge over a small river. When Archmage Arugal first came to the forest, it was here that he stayed. He left spellbooks behind him, and the Deathstalkers who found them could not carry them away. Among them was a spell that Arugal called his remedy. Worgen roam the land around the farm now.

lines.text: North Tide's Hollow.
lines.title: North Tide's Hollow

lines.index: #section:North Tide's Hollow is a stretch of woods just north of the Sepulcher, toward the western sea. The Moonrage worgen have made it one of their haunts. Their gluttons and their darksouls prowl among the trees, and each wears an enchanted shackle of Arugal's making. The dead archmage at the Sepulcher has studied these shackles closely. They were the first proof, he says, that Arugal's magic was weaker than the world believed.

lines.text: Olsen's Farthing.
lines.title: Olsen's Farthing

lines.index: #section:Olsen's Farthing is a ruined farmstead beside the main road, south of the Sepulcher. It once did its trade with every wagon that passed through the forest. The farm is now overrun by the dead. Raiders and slaves in the service of Thule Ravenclaw have gathered there, and they fall upon anyone who comes near. The Forsaken must pass them every time they take the southern road.

lines.index: #section:The Skittering Dark.
lines.text: The Skittering Dark.
lines.title: The Skittering Dark

lines.index: #section:The Skittering Dark is a web-choked hollow in the north-west of Silverpine, near the sea. Great moss stalkers and mist creepers nest there, and bears roam its edges. The apothecaries of the Sepulcher prize the blood of its spiders. Mixed with a toxin drawn from the heart of a grizzled bear, it makes a deadly elixir, and the Society hopes it will be a step toward the new plague. A Forsaken fisherman casts his line from the nearby shore, as though the spiders were no concern of his.

The apothecaries of the Sepulcher prize the blood of its spiders. Mixed with a toxin drawn from the heart of a grizzled bear, it makes a deadly elixir, and the Society hopes it will be a step toward the new plague. A Forsaken fisherman casts his line from the nearby shore, as though the spiders were no concern of his.

lines.index: #section:Deep Elem Mine lies in the hills of central Silverpine, south-east of the Sepulcher. Arugal's magic spread even here, and the mine's own foreman, Grimson the Pale, became its victim. The Moonrage worgen now hold the tunnels. The Forsaken want the mine for the war to come, for its ore would feed Varimathras's advance into the south. Dalar Dawnweaver believes that with the foreman dead, the mine will belong to the Dark Lady.

lines.index: #section:Shadowfang Keep rises on a hill in southern Silverpine, just north of Pyrewood Village. It was the keep of Baron Silverlaine, until the worgen took it and Archmage Arugal made it his home. From the road, the keep shows only its dark walls. The Sons of Arugal walk the forest from here, great worgen who serve the archmage as his children. The Forsaken have sent Deathstalkers inside. None of them has returned.

lines.index: #section:The Greymane Wall.
lines.text: The Greymane Wall.
lines.title: The Greymane Wall

lines.index: #section:The Greymane Wall runs across the southern edge of Silverpine and seals the kingdom of Gilneas from the north. King Genn Greymane raised it after the Second War, and its gates have stayed shut ever since, even when the plague came. Before the wall, humans who fled the north have made a camp of the desperate. Many are sick. A blind smith works among them. Worgen and worgs prowl close by, and the Forsaken fear that the curse is passing to the refugees. The Gilneans have made it plain that no one will be let through.

lines.title: Pyrewood Villagers

lines.index: #section:The villagers of Pyrewood live two lives. By day they are human: watchmen, elders, smiths, tailors and leatherworkers going about their work. When the sun sets, the curse of Archmage Arugal takes hold, and they become worgen of the Moonrage. Each of them wears an enchanted shackle that Arugal cast upon them.

lines.title: The Wizards of Ambermill

lines.index: #section:The wizards of Ambermill are magi of Dalaran and the servants who guard them: apprentices, conjurers, mages, watchers, warders and protectors, even a brewmaster and a miner. They answer to the Kirin Tor, and they have made a sleepy village of Silverpine into a fortress of their own.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Ambermill sits upon a ley energy node that has long lain dormant. The Kirin Tor chose it for that reason, and their archmage Ataeric has been weaving its energies awake for some great purpose. The runed pendants they carry are old tools of the Kirin Tor, used to channel such power. The wizards also keep a camp north of Pyrewood, where their crates from Hillsbrad arrive.

Their task was to judge the strength of the wildlife and of the Scourge. The ghoul Ivar ambushed them at his farm. They won the fight, but Quinn was badly hurt. Rane held Ivar's old house while Erland went on alone.

lines.text: Genn Greymane. King of Gilneas.
lines.title: Genn Greymane

lines.index: #section:Genn Greymane is the king of Gilneas. He is a proud and stubborn ruler, a warrior who trusts his own people and few others. It was he who withdrew Gilneas from the Alliance after the Second War, and he who raised the great wall across the south of Silverpine. Behind that wall his kingdom has kept its own counsel through all the ruin of the north.

lines.index: #section:Greymane is the lord who chose to stand alone. His wall spared Gilneas the costs of other nations' wars. It also left the north to face the Scourge without the Gilnean army. Whether the wall saved his kingdom or only hid it, no one outside can tell.

lines.index: #section:• When Stormwind fell, he came with the other human rulers to the council in Lordaeron called by King Terenas. He doubted the danger, and boasted that the army of Gilneas could meet any threat. • He joined the Alliance of Lordaeron with reluctance, and gave it far less than his realm could have given. • After the war he quarrelled with his fellow kings over the cost of the orcish internment camps and of Nethergarde Keep. When he complained of the keep's expense, the young King Varian Wrynn answered that no price could be set on their safety. • He sought a hand in the fate of leaderless Alterac, and backed a claimant to its throne. • He withdrew Gilneas from the Alliance, built the Greymane Wall and closed its gates.
