lines.index: #section:The Wall of His Name. Greymane believed that Gilneas owed nothing to the wars of other realms. When the Alliance asked his people to pay for the prison camps of the orcs, he refused, and he took his kingdom out of the Alliance altogether. Then he walled it off. The Greymane Wall rose across the northern border of Gilneas. When the plague came to Lordaeron, its gates stayed shut. No Gilnean army marched north to help the dying kingdom.

lines.index: #section:Darkshore.
lines.text: Darkshore.
lines.title: Darkshore

lines.index: #section:Darkshore is a long, grey coast in the north-west of Kalimdor, across a narrow strait from the great tree Teldrassil. Its forests are dim even at noon, its beaches are cold, and its hills are full of ruins older than any kingdom of men. The night elves hold it from the small harbor town of Auberdine. They have made it a gate between their new home and the wider world. Yet the land they guard is sick. Its rivers run foul, its beasts have gone mad, and old enemies have come back to the ruins of the elves' own past.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Long before the Great Sundering, these hills looked down upon the shores of the Well of Eternity. Here Queen Azshara raised the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran for her favored Highborne, and set the lord Athrikus Narassin to govern them from his Tower of Althalaxx. When the War of the Ancients ended and the Well was destroyed, the towns fell and the land was torn. What remained became a coast of the new sea. The ruins of Mathystra, once a great bastion of the elves, crumbled in the north. After the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the night elves raised Teldrassil off this coast. No chronicle records the year when Auberdine was built.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Auberdine is a humble town, but it is busy. Ships carry travellers to Teldrassil and across the sea to the human lands. A new vessel now links it to Stormwind Harbor, and another sails by way of Southshore to Menethil Harbor. The town needs every friend those ships can bring. The Blackwood furbolgs have turned against the elves. A sickness spreads through the thistle bears and the deer, and it seems to flow from Felwood to the east. Naga hold the ruins of Mathystra. The Twilight's Hammer digs at the Master's Glaive, and a cult of warlocks gathers at the Tower of Althalaxx. When the elder of Auberdine asked Stormwind for aid, Stormwind had none to give. Darnassus has sent little more.

lines.title: The Present Day

lines.index: #section:• The night elves of Auberdine. Sentinels, druids and scholars who keep the town, and study the corruption that surrounds it. • The dwarves. Miners, smiths and traders from Ironforge, and the scholars of the Explorers' League, who dig in the south. • The Blackwood furbolgs. Once friends of the elves, now maddened and hostile in their camps. • The naga. The Stormscale naga haunt Mathystra and the cave behind Cliffspring Falls. • The Greymist murlocs. They crowd the coast and prey on ships and fishermen. • The restless dead. The spirits of the Highborne still wander the ruins of Ameth'Aran. • The moonkin. They roam the eastern hills, and grow more hostile each season.

lines.index: #section:• The Twin Towns. In the age of Azshara, Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran prospered beside the Well of Eternity, while the world beneath them slid toward madness. • The Sundering. In the chaos of the war, Athrikus Narassin promised the people of Ameth'Aran life eternal through his magic. Their spirits have never found rest. • The Long Sleep. Many druids followed Malfurion Stormrage into the sleep of the Emerald Dream. Some who slept have lately awakened, and they find their old homes in ruins. • The New Home. After the war against the Burning Legion, the night elves made Teldrassil their home, and Auberdine became its door to the world.

lines.index: #section:Auberdine.
lines.text: Auberdine.
lines.title: Auberdine

lines.index: #section:Auberdine is the harbor town of Darkshore, built on the coast facing Teldrassil. Its elder, Thundris Windweaver, and its village council govern it. Sentinels guard it, and a moonwell at its heart gives the pure water its druids and priestesses need. Night elves and dwarves share its inn, its forges and its docks. From its piers a ship crosses to Rut'theran Village below Teldrassil, and another sails to Menethil Harbor. Now two new routes have come: one to Stormwind Harbor, and one to Menethil by way of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The town hopes the ships will bring aid. So far they have brought only travellers.

lines.index: #section:Ruins of Mathystra.
lines.text: Ruins of Mathystra.
lines.title: Ruins of Mathystra

lines.index: #section:The Ruins of Mathystra lie in the far north-east of Darkshore. Mathystra was once a great bastion of the elves, and fragments of its magic still lie among the grass and broken stones. The Stormscale naga now hold it, and they are pillaging the place their own ancestors once called home. Their beastmistresses bend the great beasts of the sea to their will. Of late, something older has been found beneath the ruins. An elemental guardian watched over a stair that leads down into the dark, and even the Ancients do not yet know what lies below.

lines.text: Bashal'Aran.
lines.title: Bashal'Aran

lines.index: #section:Bashal'Aran was one of the twin towns that Queen Azshara raised for her Highborne. Its ruins lie east of Auberdine. Demonic sprites, grells and satyrs of the Deth'ryll band have made them their den, and they grow stronger by feeding on the magic that still clings to the stones. Yet there is one shrine on a bluff in the west of the ruins that they will not approach. A blue light hangs about it. Within it waits the spirit of Asterion, bound there by his own master for longer than any living elf can remember.

lines.title: Ameth'Aran

lines.index: #section:Ameth'Aran was the twin of Bashal'Aran, a town of the Highborne beside the Well of Eternity. It was ruined in the war that sundered the world. Its people did not truly die. They clung to the promise of Athrikus Narassin, and now they wander the ruins as cursed and wailing spirits, still bearing the magical tools of their old craft. Two great tablets among the stones tell the story of the town and of its fall. An ancient blue flame still burns here. It is hot enough to destroy things that no other fire can touch.

lines.text: Tower of Althalaxx.
lines.title: Tower of Althalaxx

lines.index: #section:The Tower of Althalaxx rises in the north-east of Darkshore. It was the seat of Athrikus Narassin, the Highborne lord who governed Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran for Queen Azshara and spent most of his days away from them here. After ten thousand years, the tower has a master again. A company of warlocks calling itself the Cult of the Dark Strand has taken it, and the strongest of them keep to the upper rooms. A watcher of Auberdine, Balthule Shadowstrike, keeps his camp nearby. He has seen flashes of light from the top of the tower, and heard screams.

lines.text: Grove of the Ancients.
lines.title: Grove of the Ancients

lines.index: #section:The Grove of the Ancients lies in the south of Darkshore, sheltered by the mountains. Here dwell the Ancients, great spirits of the forest who have stood beside the night elves since the oldest days. Onu, an Ancient of Lore, gathers word of every threat in the land, and the druids of Auberdine heed his warnings. Beside him stands Arbal, an Ancient of War. The grove is patient, as all the Ancients are, but it is not idle. From here the fight against the naga and the Twilight's Hammer is quietly planned.

lines.title: Twilight Vale

lines.index: #section:The Twilight Vale is the name given to the southern woods of Darkshore, from the ruins of Ameth'Aran down to the borders of Ashenvale. Its roads link Auberdine with Maestra's Post and Astranaar, and messengers pass along them at their peril. Blackwood furbolgs ambush travellers, moonstalkers prowl the trees, and the sick bears of the forest attack anyone who comes near. The Grove of the Ancients, the Master's Glaive and the dig of the Explorers' League all lie within the vale. Those who travel it keep to the road.

lines.title: Mist's Edge

lines.index: #section:Mist's Edge is the long grey water along the coast of Darkshore, where the Cliffspring River empties into the sea. Its beaches are littered with the carcasses of great sea creatures and with the wreckage of ships. Two of those ships, the Silver Dawning and the Mist Veil, lie at the bottom north of Auberdine, sunk by murlocs as they came into harbor. Crabs scuttle along every stretch of sand. The Greymist murlocs raise their huts along the shore, and their chieftains hunt fishermen and Sentinels alike.

lines.index: #section:Cliffspring River.
lines.text: Cliffspring River.
lines.title: Cliffspring River

lines.index: #section:The Cliffspring River comes down from the eastern mountains and runs to the sea north of Auberdine. A bridge spans it above its first waterfall. Its water was once clean. Now it is turning foul, and the elder of Auberdine fears the taint will reach the town itself. The northern camps of the Blackwood furbolgs stand along its banks, and their bonfires burn by the water. Thundris Windweaver believes that the furbolgs foul the river, but that the true root of the poison lies further east, in Felwood.

lines.index: #section:Cliffspring Falls.
lines.text: Cliffspring Falls.
lines.title: Cliffspring Falls

lines.index: #section:Cliffspring Falls pour down from the mountains east of Auberdine. Most of the region drinks from them, and now a poison flows in their waters and sickens the deer of Darkshore. Behind the falls lies a cave where rare mushrooms grow. The Ancients warned the people of Auberdine to keep away from it, for they sensed that a new evil had made its home there. They were right. The naga have taken the cave, and a naga lord called Sinslayer leads them.

lines.index: #section:Blackwood Den.
lines.text: Blackwood Den.
lines.title: Blackwood Den

lines.index: #section:Blackwood Den lies in the far south of Darkshore, near the border of Ashenvale. It is a cluster of furbolg camps around a small cave, and it belongs to the Blackwood tribe. A night elf named Volcor was wounded here by the furbolgs and took refuge deep in the cave. His faithful companion, Grimclaw, went north alone to find help. The den is a grim sign of how far the furbolgs have fallen. They once lived in peace with the elves. Now they attack any elf who strays near their fires.

lines.index: #section:Remtravel's Excavation.
lines.text: Remtravel's Excavation.
lines.title: Remtravel's Excavation

lines.index: #section:Remtravel's Excavation is the dig of the Explorers' League in the south-west of Darkshore. Here Prospector Remtravel and his crew uncovered signs of a great and ancient society. Then the ground itself turned against them. Golems of stone rose from the earth and overran the site, and the Gravelflint troggs came with them. The crew fled to Auberdine. The prospector did not. He is still somewhere at the dig, searching for a mysterious fossil he has already lost once. What the League will make of the fossil, no one in Auberdine can say.

lines.text: The Master's Glaive.
lines.title: The Master's Glaive

lines.index: #section:The Master's Glaive stands in the south of Darkshore: a vast blade driven into the skull of a fallen giant. Onu teaches that one of the old lords of the earth died here in ages past, impaled by the glaive. The lord is long dead, but slivers of his power may remain in his bones. The Twilight's Hammer has come to seek them. Its cultists camp beneath the blade, and their books hold pages of ancient elven magic twisted to call their old masters back into the world.

lines.text: Thundris Windweaver. Elder of Auberdine.
lines.title: Thundris Windweaver

lines.index: #section:Thundris Windweaver is the elder of Auberdine. He keeps the day to day affairs of the town with a just and steady hand. He is also its keenest student of corruption. He has seen this sickness before, in times long past, and he knows that it does not stop at the borders of a forest.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Thundris sees the whole shape of Darkshore's trouble. The rage of the furbolgs, the foul river and the tools of the old Highborne are, to him, parts of one war. He also wants Auberdine to be known. The great cities remember only what the Great Sundering took from the night elves. He would have them remember the town that still stands.

lines.index: #section:The Blackwood Corrupted. Thundris mixed moonwell water with the furbolgs' own food and had it set beside their fire. Those who ate were cleansed for a moment. In that moment, the satyr who held them in thrall came out to see what had gone wrong. His talisman was brought to Auberdine. Thundris called it one battle won in a long war.

Since that day he has vowed that no more of his people will suffer in the same way, and he watches the furbolgs of Darkshore closely.

lines.index: #section:Onu is an Ancient of Lore, one of the great spirits of the forest, and he keeps the Grove of the Ancients in the south of Darkshore. He speaks slowly and with long pauses, and he does not hurry. He knows that all things come to pass in their appointed time.

lines.index: #section:Athrikus Narassin. Master of the Dark Strand.
lines.text: Athrikus Narassin. Master of the Dark Strand.
lines.title: Athrikus Narassin

lines.index: #section:Athrikus Narassin was a Highborne lord and a favored servant of Queen Azshara. She gave him the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran to govern, though he kept to his tower. When the world broke, he promised the people of Ameth'Aran life eternal through a spell. Their spirits remain in the ruins still. He also bound his own second, Asterion, in a prison of stone and magic. Athrikus lives, and he leads the Cult of the Dark Strand.

lines.index: #section:Asterion. The Prisoner of Bashal'Aran.
lines.text: Asterion. The Prisoner of Bashal'Aran.
lines.title: Asterion

lines.index: #section:Asterion was a Highborne mage, second only to Athrikus Narassin in the twin towns, and famed for strength of arm as well as of spell. When he last walked free, the Well of Eternity still stood. His master sealed him in a shrine at Bashal'Aran with an Ancient Moonstone Seal, and for more than a thousand years he stared at its pillars. His tongue is sharp. He fears his long solitude has broken his mind.

lines.title: Anaya Dawnrunner

lines.index: #section:Anaya Dawnrunner lived in Ameth'Aran when the war at the Well of Eternity tore the world apart. She was the beloved of Cerellean Whiteclaw. When the town fell, he believed her dead. Ten thousand years later he found her spirit wandering its ruins, bound there like the others who trusted the promise of Athrikus.

lines.title: Cerellean Whiteclaw

lines.index: #section:Cerellean Whiteclaw heard, after the battles at the Well of Eternity, that Ameth'Aran had been destroyed and his love Anaya with it. He followed Shan'do Stormrage into the long sleep and carried his sorrow into his dreams. Now he is awake, and her memory still haunts him. Wandering the woods, he found her spirit in the ruins.

lines.title: Gershala Nightwhisper

lines.index: #section:Gershala Nightwhisper studies the deformation of peoples by magic. The naga and the satyrs were once elves. The elves of Quel'Thalas who now call themselves blood elves have begun to toil with demonic magic, and Gershala fears they walk the same road. Azeroth, in her words, cannot bear the birth of another race of monsters.

She warns that some in Darnassus refuse to see the corruption spreading through the land.

lines.index: #section:Gorbold Steelhand came to Auberdine to supply the ships that put in there. It seemed a good trade. Then the murlocs sank the Silver Dawning and the Mist Veil as they sailed into harbor, and their captains went down with them. Business has all but stopped. Gorbold wants the captains' lockboxes brought up for the sake of the crews who remain.

lines.index: #section:Jai'vhanel, called Swordfeather, is a great owl with feathers black as jet. For a long time she was a guardian of the land around Ameth'Aran. Then she went mad, and she began to attack travellers on the road to Auberdine. No one knows what drove her to it. The Sentinels set a bounty on her.

lines.title: Murkdeep

lines.index: #section:Murkdeep is a murloc of the Greymist tribe who guards a camp of huts on the coast south of Auberdine. He has killed at least one Sentinel. He is also thought to have sunk two cargo ships off the coast. The village council has posted a bounty on him, and the townsfolk say they will sleep more soundly when it is paid.

lines.text: Cult of the Dark Strand.
lines.title: Cult of the Dark Strand

lines.index: #section:The Cult of the Dark Strand is a company of warlocks that has taken the Tower of Althalaxx in Darkshore. It had no name that the Sentinels knew until Balthule Shadowstrike pieced one together from scraps of its parchment. Its fanatics and voidcallers serve Athrikus Narassin, the ancient Highborne lord of the tower.

lines.index: #section:The cult draws on soul gems. Athrikus kept the souls of Highborne trapped in them, and hid them in the satyr lands of northern Ashenvale, at Night Run and Satyrnaar. The cult also works at Ordil'Aran in Ashenvale. It has dealings with the orc warlock Ilkrud Magthrull of the Fire Scar Shrine, who kept notes on its plans. Delgren the Purifier has made its end his task.

lines.text: Blackwood Furbolgs.
lines.title: Blackwood Furbolgs

lines.index: #section:The Blackwood are a tribe of furbolgs in Darkshore. They were friends of the night elves, and the elves still remember them so. Now they are corrupted. They live in camps along the Cliffspring River in the north and in the south, and they attack any elf who comes near.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The elves of Auberdine have traced part of the Blackwood's madness to the satyrs. A satyr corruptor holds them through a talisman. When the furbolgs ate food mixed with moonwell water, they were cleansed for a short time. The elder of Auberdine hopes that one day they may be freed for good. Yet the deeper poison runs in the land and the water, and it comes from Felwood.

lines.index: #section:The Barrens.
lines.text: The Barrens.
lines.title: The Barrens

lines.index: #section:The Barrens is a vast savannah of yellow grass, thorn trees and cracked red earth in the heart of Kalimdor. It stretches from the forests of Ashenvale in the north to the canyons of Thousand Needles in the south, and from the cliffs of Stonetalon and Mulgore in the west to the shore of the Great Sea in the east. Few places in the world are so wide, so dry or so full of life that bites. Herds of kodo and zhevra cross it, lions and raptors hunt it, and a dozen peoples fight over its scattered water. Every road of the Horde runs through it, and every enemy of the Horde knows it.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The chroniclers of the tauren say that the Barrens was once a green and teeming land. War and cataclysm scorched it long ago and left a dry husk behind, and no one living remembers it otherwise. The tauren roamed its plains for generations, hunted from one camp to the next by the centaur. The quilboar raised their thorn warrens in the south, and the harpies nested on its western hills. When the orcs came to Kalimdor after the Third War, Thrall led them across these plains. On the long march he met Cairne Bloodhoof and his people under centaur attack, and the orcs guarded the tauren caravans until they reached Mulgore. After the war at Mount Hyjal, the Horde made the Barrens the road between its new homes: Orgrimmar and Durotar to the east, Thunder Bluff to the west.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:The Barrens belongs to the Horde in name, and to whoever is strongest in each valley in truth. The Crossroads, a fortified town of orcs, holds the center. The tauren of Camp Taurajo guard the south. Goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel trade with every side at the port of Ratchet. Enemies press in from every quarter. The Kolkar centaur have found new leaders. The Razormane and Bristleback quilboar war on the Horde and on each other. Soldiers of Theramore hold Northwatch Hold on the coast, dwarves of Ironforge dig at Bael Modan, and the Venture Company poisons a lake in the north. Cultists of the Burning Blade work their rites on Dreadmist Peak. Strangest of all, the oases have begun to change, and the druids fear that something beneath the land is dreaming.

lines.index: #section:The Crossroads.
lines.text: The Crossroads.
lines.title: The Crossroads

lines.index: #section:The Crossroads is the heart of the Horde in the Barrens, a walled town of orcish huts on a hill where the great roads meet. One runs north to the Mor'shan Rampart and Ashenvale, one east to Durotar and Ratchet, one south to Camp Taurajo, and one west toward Stonetalon and Mulgore. Thork keeps its walls, Sergra Darkthorn trains its hunters, and the guards on its tower watch the grass for centaur. An orc, a tauren druid and a Forsaken apothecary may share the same fire here, and the wind riders of Devrak carry word to Orgrimmar. Of late, traders of a company called Durotar Supply and Logistics have raised a trading post just west of the walls.

lines.index: #section:Camp Taurajo.
lines.text: Camp Taurajo.
lines.title: Camp Taurajo

lines.index: #section:Camp Taurajo is the tauren stronghold of the southern Barrens, a ring of tents and totems on the road to Thousand Needles. It guards the plains that lead to Mulgore, and its braves ride out against the quilboar camps on every side. The hunter Jorn Skyseer teaches here, the smith Tatternack Steelforge studies the weapons of the enemy, and in a cage at the camp's edge sits Mangletooth, a quilboar whom his own tribe left to rot. Grunt Logmar has lately heard that human soldiers from Dustwallow Marsh are toppling the landmarks of the tauren pathfinders on the eastern border.

lines.index: #section:Ratchet.
lines.text: Ratchet.
lines.title: Ratchet

lines.index: #section:Ratchet is a goblin port on the eastern shore of the Barrens, at the edge of the Merchant Coast. The goblin Gazlowe built it with the gold he earned raising Orgrimmar, and it belongs to the Steamwheedle Cartel. Here orc and human can buy and sell side by side, for the bruisers of the town keep the peace with a heavy hand. Ships sail from its docks to Booty Bay across the sea. Its tinkers build shredders, its brewers keep old recipes, and its merchants chase every rumor of profit from the Sludge Fen to the Wailing Caverns. Pirates and sharks are its only true enemies, and it has plenty of both.

lines.index: #section:Northwatch Hold.
lines.text: Northwatch Hold.
lines.title: Northwatch Hold

lines.index: #section:Northwatch Hold is a stone fortress of the Alliance on a hill above the southern Merchant Coast. Humans raised it after the war at Mount Hyjal, and Admiral Daelin Proudmoore made use of it in his war against the Horde. Today it is held by soldiers of Theramore under Captain Fairmount. Its marines are nervous and quick to fire. Their cannons have sunk more than one ship bound for Ratchet, and they keep prisoners whom they call threats to the Alliance, some of them no more than deckhands. To the orcs, its walls are a spear pointed at the heart of the Barrens.

lines.index: #section:Far Watch Post.
lines.text: Far Watch Post.
lines.title: Far Watch Post

lines.index: #section:Far Watch Post stands at the eastern edge of the Barrens, near the bridge over the Southfury River into Durotar. It is a small camp of orcs with a watchtower and a few catapults, and it is the first post that new recruits reach when they leave the orcish homeland. Kargal Battlescar signs their papers and sends them on to the Crossroads. The warrior Uzzek tests the young fighters of the Horde here, and Ak'Zeloth, an agent of the warlock Neeru Fireblade, prepares stones of power against the demons of Dreadmist Peak.

lines.text: The Mor'shan Rampart.
lines.title: The Mor'shan Rampart

lines.index: #section:The Mor'shan Rampart is a wall of timber and stone at the northern end of the Gold Road, where the grass of the Barrens meets the trees of Ashenvale. It is the gate of the Horde's war in the forest. The orcs of the Warsong cut lumber in Ashenvale, and the night elves answer every axe with arrows. From the watchtower of the rampart, Kadrak directs the Ashenvale campaign. He sends runners to the new outposts on the Zoram Strand and at Splintertree Post, and he brings their reports home.

lines.index: #section:Lushwater Oasis.
lines.text: Lushwater Oasis.
lines.title: Lushwater Oasis

lines.index: #section:The Lushwater Oasis lies south of the Crossroads, a spread of palms and pools in the dry grass. It is one of the new oases that have bubbled up from beneath the Barrens in recent years. On its northern side rises a rocky hill, and inside the hill opens the mouth of the Wailing Caverns, from which the wind moans day and night. The Kolkar centaur of Hezrul Bloodmark camp around the water. Two disciples of the druid Naralex keep watch on the hill above the caverns, and the beasts that drink here have begun to grow strange.

lines.index: #section:The Stagnant Oasis.
lines.text: The Stagnant Oasis.
lines.title: The Stagnant Oasis

lines.index: #section:The Stagnant Oasis lies southeast of the Crossroads, a still and murky pool among the grasslands. The Kolkar centaur have raised a command tent on its shores, and the dervish Verog comes to it when his tribe calls. A fissure in the earth beneath the water holds a strange power. Dry and dead seeds dropped into it came to life. The snapjaw turtles of the pool carry a taint in their shells that no druid has seen before. South of the oasis, the sunscale raptors keep their nests.

lines.index: #section:The Forgotten Pools.
lines.text: The Forgotten Pools.
lines.title: The Forgotten Pools

lines.index: #section:The Forgotten Pools lie northwest of the Crossroads, north of the western road. They are the northernmost of the oases of the Barrens. A fissure in the earth opens beneath their waters, and gases bubble up from it without end. It was here that the druid Tonga Runetotem first found a sign of the power that is leaking into the land. The Kolkar centaur roam the pools, and their chieftain Barak Kodobane has made his camp nearby.

lines.index: #section:Field of Giants.
lines.text: Field of Giants.
lines.title: Field of Giants

lines.index: #section:The Field of Giants covers the southern plains of the Barrens, between Camp Taurajo and the border of Dustwallow Marsh. Great towers of dried earth rise from the grass, and from afar they look like giants standing still. Thunder lizards and kodo graze among them. Of late, insect-like creatures called silithid have appeared in the field. They dig hives, lay eggs and seem to think in a way no beast should. Korran of the Crossroads studies them for his masters in Orgrimmar, and the hunter Jorn Skyseer fears they herald a grim future.

lines.index: #section:Bael Modan.
lines.text: Bael Modan.
lines.title: Bael Modan

lines.index: #section:Bael Modan is a dwarven dig site in the far south of the Barrens, guarded by the stone walls of Bael'dun Keep. The dwarves blast deep holes into the earth, and their machines tear at the hills. Their flying machine circles above them. The land they dig was once the home of the Stonespire tauren, and it was holy to them. The tribe was driven off, and only the wanderer Gann Stonespire still walks the roads nearby, seeking revenge. The first great find of the dig was a stone called the Tear of the Moons. The dwarves' general locked it away as cursed.

lines.index: #section:Dreadmist Peak.
lines.text: Dreadmist Peak.
lines.title: Dreadmist Peak

lines.index: #section:Dreadmist Peak rises northwest of the Crossroads, its summit wrapped in a red mist. The cultists of the Burning Blade hold its heights. In a cave near the top, above an altar of fire, they keep the Demon Seed, a tool of the Burning Legion. The pools at the summit feed the weather of the northern plains, and the druids fear that the cult has poisoned them, and that the sickness spreading among the gazelles of the plains begins there. Even Neeru Fireblade of Orgrimmar has asked for the Seed to be destroyed. It is said that in the years after the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore herself fought a demon upon this peak.

lines.index: #section:Blackthorn Ridge.
lines.text: Blackthorn Ridge.
lines.title: Blackthorn Ridge

lines.index: #section:Blackthorn Ridge is a thorny valley in the south of the Barrens, north of the great warren of Razorfen Kraul. The Razormane quilboar hold it. Three chieftains have climbed out of the Kraul to command their war on the Horde: Nak the seer, Kuz the tracker, and Lok Orcbane, their warlord. Their camps lie among the thorns. On the ridge above the valley, the orc shaman Brine keeps a lonely camp beside a pool of pure water, and teaches the young shaman of the Horde the call of water.

lines.title: Honor's Stand

lines.index: #section:Honor's Stand lies on the western road of the Barrens, where it climbs toward the Stonetalon Mountains. No chronicle records who named it, or what stand it remembers. Two travellers of the Horde keep camp by the road here. Seereth Stonebreak is a shaman who hears the spirits of Stonetalon crying out against the Venture Company. Makaba Flathoof is a tauren whose village was burned by the Grimtotem, and who wants only to see more of them dead.

lines.index: #section:The Merchant Coast.
lines.text: The Merchant Coast.
lines.title: The Merchant Coast

lines.index: #section:The Merchant Coast is the eastern shore of the Barrens, from Ratchet south to the walls of Northwatch Hold. It takes its name from the trade that flows through the goblin port. South of Ratchet, the pirates of the Southsea Freebooters have raised camps on the beach. They raid the ships of Gazlowe and of the trade princes, and they answer to Baron Longshore, captain of the Heedless. A tinker of Ratchet once sent a machine against them. It never came home. Its pieces now lie scattered across the pirates' camp.

lines.text: Boulder Lode Mine.
lines.title: Boulder Lode Mine

lines.index: #section:Boulder Lode Mine lies in the far northeast of the Barrens, beyond the Sludge Fen. Orcish timbers still frame its tunnels, but the Venture Company has claimed it. Word travels fast to Ratchet, and the latest word says that one of the goblin miners has dug up an emerald as big as a fist. The wharfmaster of Ratchet knows buyers who would pay well for it, and he is not the only one who has heard.

lines.index: #section:Thorn Hill.
lines.text: Thorn Hill.
lines.title: Thorn Hill

lines.index: #section:Thorn Hill rises east of the Crossroads, between the town and the road to Durotar. Its slopes are wrapped in the great thorn vines of the Razormane quilboar. From here the raider Kreenig Snarlsnout struck at the caravans from Durotar and grew fat on the supplies of the Horde. Worse lurks in a cave on the plateau. The quilboar speak of Chol'aruk, the Ravener, a monstrous beast of their own kind that no one believed in until warriors went in to find it.

lines.index: #section:Raptor Grounds.
lines.text: Raptor Grounds.
lines.title: Raptor Grounds

lines.index: #section:The Raptor Grounds are a small valley south of Ratchet and west of Northwatch Hold. The sunscale raptors keep their nests here, and they are cleverer than raptors have any right to be. They stole a shipment of silver from the guard tower of the Crossroads, the pay of its soldiers, and carried it back to their nests. No one knows what a raptor wants with silver. The goblin Mebok Mizzyrix believes their cunning lies in their horns.

lines.index: #section:The Sludge Fen.
lines.text: The Sludge Fen.
lines.title: The Sludge Fen

lines.index: #section:The Sludge Fen lies in the northeast of the Barrens. The Venture Company has raised an oil derrick over it, and what was a pool of water is now a mire of black sludge. Supervisor Lugwizzle runs the works from the top of the derrick, and goblin shredders stalk the shore. The tinkers of Ratchet envy the company's new machines. One of them, Wizzlecrank, crept in to steal a shredder and found too late that he had no key to make it walk.

lines.index: #section:Agama'gor.
lines.text: Agama'gor.
lines.title: Agama'gor

lines.index: #section:Agama'gor is a camp of the Bristleback quilboar in the center of the Barrens, north of the road that leads west from Camp Taurajo. Its geomancers dig blood-red stones from the earth, which the quilboar carry as totems of strength. Grunts from Camp Taurajo have fought here and not always come home. One of them, Grunt Dogran, lay wounded near the camp while his comrades sent for healing. Across the road, the Razormane of Bramblescar watch the Bristleback with hatred.

lines.text: Bramblescar.
lines.title: Bramblescar

lines.index: #section:Bramblescar is a thorn camp of the Razormane quilboar in the middle of the Barrens, east of the road between the Crossroads and Camp Taurajo. The Razormane here are at war with the Bristleback of Agama'gor, across the road, and they attack anyone else who comes near. Close by, in a small tauren camp, the orc Mankrik and his wife fought their last battle together. Mankrik believes that the Razormane raiders of these parts carried off the bone jewels she wore.

lines.index: #section:Gold Road.
lines.text: Gold Road.
lines.title: Gold Road

lines.index: #section:The Gold Road is the great highway of the Barrens. It runs from the Mor'shan Rampart in the north, through the Crossroads and Camp Taurajo, to the Great Lift at the edge of Thousand Needles in the south. It takes its name from the trade caravans that travel it. Its northern stretch is watched by Horde towers. Its southern stretch is lonelier, and a walker who strays from it at dusk may end up in a tree with hyenas circling below.

lines.text: The Dry Hills.
lines.title: The Dry Hills

lines.index: #section:The Dry Hills rise in the far northwest of the Barrens, the green foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains. The Witchwing harpies nest here under Serena Bloodfeather and swoop down on the caravans of the northern road. On a ridge above the hills lives a hermit tanner named Walton, who wants no company. The hunter Vrang Wildgore keeps his traps in the valley below. Of late, men in the livery of Kul Tiras have been seen searching that valley, camped beside a wrecked caravan.

lines.title: Grol'dom Farm

lines.index: #section:Grol'dom Farm is a pig farm of the orcs on the road between the Crossroads and Durotar, one of the many that have sprung up since Orgrimmar was founded. It is a quiet place of pens and swine. Its master, Kranal Fiss, is a shaman of the Horde. He sends those who would tame fire to a hidden shrine in Durotar, and asks them to bring the torch back to him aflame.

lines.index: #section:Fray Island is a small dry island off the eastern shore of the Barrens. Its master, Klannoc Macleod, calls himself the Islander, and he runs a proving ground for warriors of every race. Those who would learn from him must first pass the Affray: they step into the midst of a crowd and fight challenger after challenger until the champion comes out to meet them.

lines.text: Thork. Warden of the Crossroads.
lines.title: Thork

lines.index: #section:Thork keeps the Crossroads for the Horde. Every newcomer to the Barrens is sent to him, whether an orc from Durotar, a tauren from Thunder Bluff, or a stranger sent by the Warchief himself. He greets them gruffly, sizes them up, and puts them to work. His great worry is the road to Durotar, where the Razormane quilboar fall upon the caravans that feed his town.

lines.text: Sergra Darkthorn. Huntmistress of the Crossroads.
lines.title: Sergra Darkthorn

lines.index: #section:Sergra Darkthorn sets the young of the Horde on the hunter's path in the Barrens. She sends them first against plainstriders and zhevra, then against prowlers and raptors, and at last against Echeyakee, the white lion. She tolerates no insolence. The Warchief has declared the women of the Horde the equals of its men, and she means to be treated so. Some of her own comrades call her hard, but she asks her hunters to consider the lives they take.

lines.index: #section:Gazlowe. Master of Ratchet.
lines.text: Gazlowe. Master of Ratchet.
lines.title: Gazlowe

lines.index: #section:Gazlowe is the goblin who founded Ratchet and still runs it. He is a builder by trade and a merchant by nature. When the orcs came to Kalimdor, Thrall hired him as the chief engineer of the new nation of Durotar, and his crews helped raise the walls of Orgrimmar. Thrall paid him well. With that gold, Gazlowe built a port of his own at the mouth of the Southfury River, where anyone may trade so long as they pay.

lines.index: #section:The Shark. A great shark began to circle the waters by the dock, attacking sailors and small boats. The dockworkers called it Bruuz, and soon no crew would go into the water. Gazlowe posted a reward for its fin. When the fin came, he said he might put it in his soup, to have the last laugh.

lines.index: #section:Mankrik. The Grieving Warrior.
lines.text: Mankrik. The Grieving Warrior.
lines.title: Mankrik

lines.index: #section:Mankrik is an orc warrior of the Crossroads. He and his wife were fighting beside the tauren in a small camp when the quilboar overran them. She held three of them off alone. He led others away, and when he turned back he saw her fall. Then they brought him down. A tauren druid found him on the Gold Road and tended his wounds. Now he stands at the Crossroads from dawn to dusk, staring at the horizon, and he has killed every quilboar he has met since.

lines.text: Mangletooth. The Caged Quilboar.
lines.title: Mangletooth

lines.index: #section:Mangletooth is a mystic of the Razormane tribe who sits in a cage at Camp Taurajo. He snorts between his words, and his words are bitter. His people turned their backs on him and left him to rot, and he has not forgiven them. He still knows the magic of Agamaggan, the boar spirit of his people, and he trades it for revenge.

lines.text: Tonga Runetotem. Druid of the Crossroads.
lines.title: Tonga Runetotem

lines.index: #section:Tonga Runetotem is a tauren druid sent from Thunder Bluff to learn what strange power is leaking into the Barrens. He grieves for the green land the Barrens once was. In the new oases he found fissures in the earth, and in their waters a power that can raise life from dead seeds and twist the beasts that drink it. To him, it is as if the land dreams and cannot wake.

lines.index: #section:Regthar Deathgate is an orc warrior who holds a line of bunkers west of the Crossroads. His war is with the Kolkar centaur. They were once scattered and disorderly in the Barrens, but new leaders have risen to rally them, and Regthar means to see each of those leaders dead. Their heads he keeps together.

Regthar Deathgate judges the centaur undisciplined, unable to focus their rage as the orcs can, yet he does not call them weak.

He sends his choicest cuts by wind rider to Gryshka, the innkeeper of Orgrimmar, whom he calls his friend. When a letter comes back from her, he laughs that a fine steak will make any lady blush, and he speaks of a wedding.

lines.title: Jorn Skyseer

lines.index: #section:Jorn Skyseer teaches the hunter's path at Camp Taurajo. He speaks of each great beast by its tauren name, and he teaches that the strength of the prey passes to the hunter. His sister Mahren hunts the beasts of the sea along the coast.

What he found in their blades troubled him: the quilboar are further along than anyone thought.

lines.index: #section:Gann Stonespire wanders the roads of the southern Barrens alone. The land where the dwarves now dig at Bael Modan was the home and provider of his tribe. Their blasts drive holes into it and their machines rip it apart. Gann tried to reach a peaceful settlement with them and failed. Now he seeks their journals, their explosives and the ruin of their flying machine.

lines.index: #section:Walton. The Hermit Tanner.
lines.text: Walton. The Hermit Tanner.
lines.title: Walton

lines.index: #section:Walton is a tanner who lives alone on a ridge above the Dry Hills. He trades hides with the hunter Vrang Wildgore, who warns visitors not to be alarmed by his looks. Walton was once a sailor of the navy of Kul Tiras. When Daelin Proudmoore made war on the Horde, Walton objected to the admiral's methods, above all the killing of civilians. There is more to his story, he says, and he does not tell it all.

lines.index: #section:Vrang Wildgore is a hunter and trapper of the northern Barrens. He trades raw lion hides to a tanner who lives on the ridge above him, and in return he receives the finished leather of his trade.

lines.index: #section:Chol'aruk. The Ravener.
lines.text: Chol'aruk. The Ravener.
lines.title: Chol'aruk

lines.index: #section:Chol'aruk is a monstrous quilboar that makes its lair in a cave on Thorn Hill. The Razormane call it the Ravener. Those who have seen it say it is five times the size of a common quilboar, that its thirst for blood is never sated, and that it could swallow an orc whole. Most folk do not believe such tales. Gur'ak of the Crossroads believes them, and so does Bainham, a soldier of the Alliance in Ratchet. Each has fought a beast like it before, and each lost comrades to it.

lines.index: #section:Kolkar Centaurs.
lines.text: Kolkar Centaurs.
lines.title: Kolkar Centaurs

lines.index: #section:The Kolkar are a tribe of centaur who roam the Barrens and the lands around it. Their riders camp beside the oases, hunt the beasts that come to drink and fall upon travellers on the roads. They raided the tauren for years before the orcs came, and they have raided the Horde ever since.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:For a long time the Kolkar of the Barrens were scattered and disorderly. Now new leaders have risen among them: Barak Kodobane near the Forgotten Pools, Verog the Dervish at the Stagnant Oasis, and Hezrul Bloodmark, the greatest of them, at the Lushwater Oasis. Under these chieftains the tribe has become a true threat. Regthar Deathgate hunts them from his bunkers west of the Crossroads, and when their leaders fell, a war band came from the Kolkar homeland in Desolace to take revenge. In Durotar, another band holds the rocky gorge of Kolkar Crag.

lines.index: #section:Razormane Quilboar.
lines.text: Razormane Quilboar.
lines.title: Razormane Quilboar

lines.index: #section:The Razormane are a tribe of quilboar of the northern and southern Barrens. They raise their camps among great thorn vines that grow up from the earth, and they revere the boar spirit Agamaggan, whose blood is said to have made the thorns. Before the orcs came, they roamed the land that is now Durotar, and they have never accepted its loss.

lines.index: #section:The Razormane are at war with the Horde and with their cousins of the Bristleback tribe. They hold Thorn Hill east of the Crossroads, Bramblescar in the middle plains and Blackthorn Ridge in the south. Their raids on the caravans from Durotar were led by three of their tribe who came out of Razorfen Kraul: Nak, Kuz and Lok Orcbane. The smith of Camp Taurajo has found that their weapons are growing sturdier. In a cave on Thorn Hill, the Razormane speak of a monstrous beast of their own blood, the Ravener.

lines.index: #section:Redridge Mountains.
lines.text: Redridge Mountains.
lines.title: Redridge Mountains

lines.index: #section:The Redridge Mountains rise east of Elwynn Forest, a country of red stone ridges, tall elms and fast cold rivers. At their heart lies Lake Everstill, and on its western shore stands Lakeshire, the easternmost township of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Its roads run west to Elwynn, south-west to Duskwood and north through the pass to the Burning Steppes. In better years Redridge was a land of fishermen, millers and ore diggers. In these days it is a land at war, and it fights that war almost alone.

In these days it is a land at war, and it fights that war almost alone.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records the year when the first humans settled Redridge. As Stormwind grew rich on the farms of its heartland, its people spread into the hills around it, and in time a town rose on the shore of the lake. The mountains are said to have once reached farther north. When the Dark Iron Dwarves called upon the Firelord in their war against their kin, the fire that raised Blackrock Mountain burned the northern ranges into the ash-choked waste now called the Burning Steppes. The southern valleys stayed green, and they stayed in human hands.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Orcs of the Blackrock clan have come down out of the Burning Steppes. In league with the warlock Morganth, they stormed Stonewatch Keep and slew most of the soldiers who held it. Then the warlock turned on his allies and raised a tower of his own in the north-east, served by the Shadowhide gnolls. The orcs pressed on to Lakeshire itself, and their assault was so fierce that the great bridge over the Everstill fell into the water. Magistrate Solomon has written for help to Stormwind, to Westfall and to Darkshire. None has come. The township holds on with a few guards, a rebuilt bridge and the strangers who answer its bounties. New things stir as well. Merchants of a trading company have raised a post at the Three Corners crossroads, and a new road now leads out of Redridge toward the Riverglades. In the far south-east, a second Blackrock war band has made its camp in Render's Valley.

lines.index: #section:• The people of Lakeshire. Fishermen, smiths, stable hands and innkeepers, who have learned to live behind barricades. • The Stormwind guard. A small garrison under Marshal Marris, too few for the war it must fight. • The Blackrock orcs. They hold Stonewatch Keep, the northern pass and the south-eastern valleys. • The Shadowhide gnolls. They prowl Galardell Valley in the service of Morganth. • The Redridge gnolls. A separate pack that raids the hills north of Lakeshire and the southern road. • Murlocs. They have come up the rivers to fish Lake Everstill empty, far from any sea. • Black dragon whelps. They hunt in the hills south of the lake, and no one can say where they come from.

lines.index: #section:Lakeshire.
lines.text: Lakeshire.
lines.title: Lakeshire

lines.index: #section:Lakeshire sits on the western shore of Lake Everstill, a town of stone houses, a busy inn, a town hall and a stable. It is ruled by Magistrate Solomon and his court, and guarded by Marshal Marris and a small garrison of Stormwind soldiers. Barricades now close its northern edge. Foreman Oslow's workers labor to rebuild the Everstill Bridge, which the Blackrock brought down in their last assault. The inn is the heart of the town. There Chef Breanna cooks what she can find, the barkeep waits on a shipment of drink that never arrives, and the talk is all of orcs, gnolls and the aid Stormwind promised.

lines.title: Lake Everstill

lines.index: #section:Lake Everstill fills the heart of the Redridge Mountains, clear and blue beneath the red ridges. Its spotted sunfish have long been the pride of Lakeshire's fishermen. Now murlocs have come in great numbers to its shores, dropping their crude anchors and taking the fish for themselves. The dockmaster finds it strange to see them so far from the sea, and he wonders what they might be fleeing. Beneath the water lies more than fish. When the Blackrock struck at a boat crossing from the ruined bridge, its cargo sank to the bottom, and the lake has kept it.

lines.index: #section:Stonewatch Keep.
lines.text: Stonewatch Keep.
lines.title: Stonewatch Keep

lines.index: #section:Stonewatch Keep was the fortress that guarded the eastern reaches of Redridge for the crown. A small garrison of Stormwind soldiers held it until the Blackrock orcs came, strengthened by the dark magic of Morganth. The orcs fought with a savagery that the survivors still speak of, and the keep fell. Its walls now shelter the warlord Gath'Ilzogg and his captains, and from there the orcs raid north and west toward Lakeshire. Magistrate Solomon counts the keep as the first thing the kingdom must win back.

lines.index: #section:Stonewatch Tower.
lines.text: Stonewatch Tower.
lines.title: Stonewatch Tower

lines.index: #section:Stonewatch Tower is the watchtower that stands beside Stonewatch Keep. Unlike the keep, it survived the battle whole, and the orcs now use it as their own lookout over the road from Lakeshire. At its top, among the barrels, lies a forgotten jar that once held a foul liquor. The High Mage Theocritus chose that jar as a hiding place for one of his glyphs, so that his scrying eye could look into the minds of those within the keep.

lines.index: #section:Stonewatch Falls.
lines.text: Stonewatch Falls.
lines.title: Stonewatch Falls

lines.index: #section:Below Stonewatch, the river that drains Lake Everstill tumbles down the hillside and gathers in a deep pool in the eastern hills. This is Stonewatch Falls. Murlocs have raised their huts along its banks and fish its waters, as their kin do on the shores of the great lake. Above the falls stand the walls of the lost keep. The falls lie between the orcs of Stonewatch and the gnolls of Galardell Valley, and few from Lakeshire now come this far east.

lines.index: #section:Tower of Ilgalar.
lines.text: Tower of Ilgalar.
lines.title: Tower of Ilgalar

lines.index: #section:The Tower of Ilgalar rises in the north-eastern hills of Redridge. It is the lair of the warlock Morganth, who raised it after he turned on his orcish allies. Shadowhide gnolls guard its approaches, and the tower's halls are hung with the bones of dragons, whose purpose no one outside can guess. Near its walls an old lion statue has kept a lonely watch for decades. Far to the west, the mage Theocritus watches the tower through the Eye of Azora in his own tower.

lines.index: #section:Galardell Valley.
lines.text: Galardell Valley.
lines.title: Galardell Valley

lines.index: #section:Galardell Valley lies in the north-east of Redridge, about the foot of the Tower of Ilgalar. It is the country of the Shadowhide gnolls, who serve the warlock Morganth. Their camps fill the valley, and their leader, Lieutenant Fangore, keeps his post in its northern reaches. Among them walk darkweavers who work the warlock's shadow magic. Travellers who stray here seldom meet a single gnoll. The Shadowhide answer a cry for help faster than any other pack in the mountains, and Fangore's call brings the whole valley running.

lines.index: #section:Alther's Mill.
lines.text: Alther's Mill.
lines.title: Alther's Mill

lines.index: #section:Alther's Mill is the lumber mill of Lakeshire, in the hills north-east of the town. Foreman Oslow depends on it for the timber he needs to rebuild the Everstill Bridge. It is no longer a safe place to work. Great tarantulas have made nests among the stacked logs, and Blackrock orcs have been seen nosing about the mill. Oslow holds old Alther to blame for the mess. The mill has other uses too. An agent of SI:7 named Lucius keeps a locked chest there, and those he trains in the thief's arts must go and open it.

lines.index: #section:Rethban Caverns.
lines.text: Rethban Caverns.
lines.title: Rethban Caverns

lines.index: #section:The Rethban Caverns run deep into the foothills north of Lakeshire. They take their name from Bart Rethban, who first found the dark ore of their walls. Lakeshire used to keep a store of that ore, for scribes value its color for their inks. Now the Redridge gnolls live in the caverns, and their drudgers dig the ore for themselves. Foreman Oslow's workers are too busy with the town's defenses to go after it. A dwarf of the Barleybrew family in Lakeshire has made the caverns into a test of nerve for warriors.

lines.index: #section:Redridge Canyons.
lines.text: Redridge Canyons.
lines.title: Redridge Canyons

lines.index: #section:The Redridge Canyons cut through the hills north of Lakeshire, on the road toward the Burning Steppes. They are the hunting grounds of the Redridge gnolls. Brutes and mystics range along the ridges above the town's stable, stealing any horse that strays. Their leader, Yowler, has his den in the canyons, and on quiet nights the whole town can hear his pack baying in the hills. Farther north, near the pass, the Blackrock have made their camp, so that Lakeshire is hemmed in by gnoll and orc alike.

lines.index: #section:Lakeridge Highway.
lines.text: Lakeridge Highway.
lines.title: Lakeridge Highway

lines.index: #section:The Lakeridge Highway runs east from Lakeshire's southern bridge, along the southern shore of Lake Everstill toward Stonewatch. It was built for trade, and it joins the town to the eastern reaches of the mountains. Since the orcs took the keep, few wagons use it. Gnolls camp along the southern road, murlocs hunt on the shore, and condors wheel above the hills. Deputy Feldon keeps watch at its western end and pays for any news of what is gathering along it.

lines.index: #section:Three Corners.
lines.text: Three Corners.
lines.title: Three Corners

lines.index: #section:Three Corners is the crossroads at the western edge of Redridge. From it one road leads to Lakeshire, one to Goldshire in Elwynn and one to Darkshire in Duskwood. Guard Parker patrols the stretch of road toward Duskwood. In these days the crossroads has become a place of trade. The Azeroth Commerce Authority, a company of merchants, has set up its local hub here, with quartermasters, clerks, mules and a pile of crates awaiting inspection. Its couriers bring back empty crates from across the land.

lines.index: #section:Render's Camp.
lines.text: Render's Camp.
lines.title: Render's Camp

lines.index: #section:Render's Camp is the Blackrock encampment in the north-west of Redridge, just west of the pass to the Burning Steppes. Here the champions who lead each unit of the orcish host make their quarters. Behind it lies Render's Rock, a great cave where the orcs keep their prisoners. Among them was a corporal of Stormwind dragged away from the battle at Stonewatch Keep, whose name is still posted outside the Lakeshire inn. Blackrock trackers range the hills around it, watching the road from the south.

lines.text: Render's Valley.
lines.title: Render's Valley

lines.index: #section:Render's Valley lies in the far south-east of Redridge, among the hills above the southern forests. The Blackrock have raised camps here as well, beyond the reach of Stonewatch, and their summoners and outrunners gather in the valley, far beyond the reach of Lakeshire's few patrols. Marshal Marris knew of orcs in this corner of the mountains, but not how many. Now a war band has settled there under an orc called Incinerator Gar'im, whose shadowcasters are said to be the most dangerous of their kind.

lines.index: #section:Magistrate Solomon. Magistrate of Lakeshire.
lines.text: Magistrate Solomon. Magistrate of Lakeshire.
lines.title: Magistrate Solomon

lines.index: #section:Magistrate Solomon governs the township of Lakeshire and sits in judgment over its court. He is a man of law and letters, and he has turned both into weapons. His decrees name the enemies of the kingdom, and his bounties pay for their heads. Yet his letters are what he trusts most. Again and again he has written to the great and the powerful, begging them to save his town.

lines.index: #section:Solomon speaks for a forgotten frontier. His pleas reveal, one by one, that Lakeshire is not alone in its abandonment. Westfall and Darkshire have been left to fend for themselves as well, and Solomon begins to suspect that something is deeply wrong in Stormwind.

lines.index: #section:The State of Lakeshire. Solomon's report told the whole grim story: the alliance of orc and warlock, the fall of the keep, the broken bridge, the lack of soldiers, food and bandages. The general in Stormwind praised him and promised reinforcements as soon as the king gave the word. Solomon read the reply twice. He thought it a mystery, and he feared it marked the beginning of the war, not its end.

lines.index: #section:Letters to the Shires. Solomon turned next to his neighbours. Stoutmantle answered with a heavy heart: his militia was fighting its own war. Lord Ebonlocke thought the request close to madness, for Darkshire had raised its Night Watch only because Stormwind had left it too. When both answers were in his hands, Solomon understood that the army had withdrawn from all three shires. He called it treachery.

He knows that bravery alone will not win this war, and he counts his enemies by the axes, orbs and heads that are brought back to him.

lines.title: Shawn

lines.index: #section:Shawn is one of the children of Lakeshire. He spends his days fishing by the lake with his friend Hilary and her kitten, Effsee. When Hilary's necklace, a gift from her father, fell into the water, Shawn looked for help. His parents forbid him to swim in the lake, for they say there are monsters in it.

lines.index: #section:Morganth. Warlock of the Tower of Ilgalar.
lines.text: Morganth. Warlock of the Tower of Ilgalar.
lines.title: Morganth

lines.index: #section:Morganth is a human warlock who dwells in the Tower of Ilgalar. Long ago he studied in the mage tower of Stormwind, one of three who learned there together. He fell to the dark arts, and when he would not turn back he was banished. He took with him a sealed book of shadow magic. Now he commands the Shadowhide gnolls, speaks to them through enchanted pendants and summons demons to his side.

He fell to the dark arts, and when he would not turn back he was banished. He took with him a sealed book of shadow magic. Now he commands the Shadowhide gnolls, speaks to them through enchanted pendants and summons demons to his side.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Morganth is the hidden author of Redridge's ruin. It was his magic that fed the Blackrock savagery at Stonewatch Keep. He is also the rival of the High Mage Theocritus, who has watched him from Elwynn for a long time.
lines.text: Morganth is the hidden author of Redridge's ruin. It was his magic that fed the Blackrock savagery at Stonewatch Keep. He is also the rival of the High Mage Theocritus, who has watched him from Elwynn for a long time.
lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He made an alliance with Gath'Ilzogg and the Blackrock clan, and helped them take Stonewatch Keep. • He turned on the orcs soon after, raised his own tower and bound the Shadowhide gnolls to his service. • He keeps Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic, although he never broke the seals the mages of Stormwind set on it. • He seeks the Scythe of Elune.

lines.title: Deeds

lines.index: #section:The Broken Alliance. The Eye of Azora showed Theocritus a warlock at war with the orcs he had once helped. Why the two had fallen out, not even Magistrate Solomon could say. To learn more, the High Mage hid a glyph at the top of the watchtower beside Stonewatch Keep, and he began to read the minds of the orcs inside.

lines.index: #section:The Scythe. At last Theocritus learned what Morganth sought: the Scythe of Elune. He feared that the warlock had already found it, and that Stormwind would soon feel his power. The High Mage would not face Morganth himself, so another climbed the Tower of Ilgalar in his stead. Morganth's Pendant of Shadow came back to Elwynn, and Theocritus called the kingdom saved from a grave peril.

lines.index: #section:Tharil'zun leads the Blackrock outrunners and renegades who lay ambushes between Lakeshire and Stonewatch Keep. He is vicious and crafty, and he picks his fights where the roads are narrow. Marshal Marris wants his head more than any other.

lines.text: Bellygrub. The Boar of Lakeshire's Gardens.
lines.title: Bellygrub

lines.index: #section:Bellygrub is a great boar who forages in the fields south-west of Lakeshire. Now and then he wanders into Martie Jainrose's garden and eats or tramples everything in it. Marshal Marris gave him his name, and it has stuck. The fields where he forages lie close to the town, and his tusk is worth a reward from the herbalist.

lines.index: #section:Blackrock Clan.
lines.text: Blackrock Clan.
lines.title: Blackrock Clan

lines.index: #section:The Blackrock are one of the oldest and most warlike clans of the orcs. They were the backbone of the old Horde and gave it two of its Warchiefs. Long after the Horde's defeat, the Blackrock have kept the old ways of war, and they have never made peace with the humans.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:In the First War, the Blackrock chieftain Blackhand led the Horde as its Warchief, though others pulled the strings behind him. He was slain by one of his own, Orgrim Doomhammer, a Blackrock warrior who then led the Horde to the conquest of Stormwind. In the Second War, Doomhammer's Horde was broken at Blackrock Mountain after he had slain Anduin Lothar. Most of the orcs were herded into camps. The Blackrock who escaped took refuge in the mountain that bears their name, and they have held its heights ever since.

lines.title: History

lines.index: #section:Now the Blackrock have come south out of the Burning Steppes. Under the warlord Gath'Ilzogg, and with the dark magic of Morganth, they took Stonewatch Keep and brought down the Everstill Bridge. Their outrunners ambush the roads, their shadowcasters carry orbs tainted by demons, and their champions camp by the northern pass. Another war band has entered the far south-east by Render's Valley. Yet they have pushed so far into the kingdom that they must forage in the hills for food and arms, and Lakeshire hopes to starve them out.

lines.index: #section:The Shadowhide are a clan of gnolls who dwell in Galardell Valley, in the north-east of Redridge. They serve the warlock Morganth. Their leader is Lieutenant Fangore. Their darkweavers practice a shadowy magic, their assassins strike unseen, and their slayers attack orc and human alike.

lines.index: #section:Each Shadowhide wears a pendant through which Morganth speaks to them. The High Mage Theocritus has spent months trying to reach into those pendants. He has managed to send a message through some of them, and he hopes one day to send an attack through them that would freeze every gnoll that wears one.

lines.text: Redridge Gnolls.
lines.title: Redridge Gnolls

lines.index: #section:The Redridge gnolls are the old gnoll pack of the Redridge Mountains, distinct from the Shadowhide who serve Morganth. They serve no warlock and no orc. Their brutes and mystics range the hills north of Lakeshire, and their poachers and mongrels camp along the southern road. Their leader is Yowler, who has his den in the Redridge Canyons, and whose howl carries all the way to Lakeshire.

lines.index: #section:The Redridge gnolls take what the war leaves unguarded. They seized the caravan that carried iron for the Everstill Bridge. They steal horses from the stable of Lakeshire. They have moved into the Rethban Caverns, where their drudgers dig the ore that the town once mined. They are loosely organized, but they respect strength above all else. Deputy Feldon hopes that the death of their fiercest thrashers will teach the rest to stay in the hills. In Rethban, a gnoll named Ardo Dirtpaw leads the pack that holds the caverns.

lines.index: #section:Stormwind City.
lines.text: Stormwind City.
lines.title: Stormwind City

lines.index: #section:Stormwind City is the capital of the Kingdom of Stormwind and the greatest city of humankind still standing in the south. Its white walls rise at the western edge of Elwynn Forest, and blue canals run between its districts. Merchants crowd the Trade District. Pilgrims climb the steps of the Cathedral of Light. Above them all stands Stormwind Keep, where the kings of the realm have ruled for generations. The city is proud, rich and crowded. It is also a city without its king.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records the year Stormwind was founded. Its roots lie with the families of Arathor who travelled south long ago and raised a kingdom they named Azeroth. Stormwind was its heart. For centuries the city grew in peace, and the Church of the Holy Light made it one of the great seats of its faith. Then came the First War. The orcish Horde burned the kingdom and sacked the capital, and King Llane Wrynn died within his own keep. The survivors fled north with Sir Anduin Lothar to Lordaeron.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:Stormwind was raised again after the Second War, stone by stone, by the Stonemasons' Guild. When the House of Nobles refused to pay for that labor, the masons rioted, Queen Tiffin Wrynn was killed, and the masons were driven out. They became the Defias Brotherhood. Now King Varian Wrynn has vanished on a diplomatic journey, and no one at court can say where he is. His young son Anduin holds the title of king. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon rules in his name as regent, and the noblewoman Katrana Prestor is often at his side. The army is far away. The Defias prey on the roads outside the walls. Inside the walls, the prisoners of the Stockade have risen against their guards. The agents of SI:7 suspect that someone at court is helping the Brotherhood.

lines.index: #section:Trade District.
lines.text: Trade District.
lines.title: Trade District

lines.index: #section:The Trade District is the busiest quarter of Stormwind. Its streets hold the bank, the auction house, the inn called the Gilded Rose and shops of every craft. Morgan Pestle sells his potions here, and the Trias family sells cheese. Gryphons land at the district's edge, carrying letters and travellers from across the kingdom. Beneath all the bargaining runs the city's oldest trade of all, which is rumor. What is heard in the Trade District at noon is known in the Keep by evening.

lines.index: #section:Cathedral Square.
lines.text: Cathedral Square.
lines.title: Cathedral Square

lines.index: #section:Cathedral Square is the great open plaza at the heart of Stormwind. At its northern end rises the Cathedral of Light, the largest house of the Holy Light in the south. Around the square stand City Hall, where the architect Baros Alexston keeps his office, and the halls where the city's clergy and paladins train. Soldiers drill on the flagstones. Pilgrims come to pray. The square is the place where Stormwind shows itself as it wishes to be seen: faithful, orderly and strong.

lines.index: #section:Old Town.
lines.text: Old Town.
lines.title: Old Town

lines.index: #section:Old Town lies in the east of Stormwind, where the streets are narrow and the buildings older than elsewhere. It holds the city's barracks and a shop of armor for soldiers. It is also the home of SI:7. Master Mathias Shaw works from the barracks, and his agents come and go through doors that most citizens never notice. In the alleys, folk keep to their own business and ask few questions. Soldiers newly arrived in the capital come here first, to be armed, lodged and sent where the kingdom needs them.

lines.text: Dwarven District.
lines.title: Dwarven District

lines.index: #section:The Dwarven District stands in the north of Stormwind, by the city walls. The dwarves of Ironforge who live in Stormwind keep this quarter as their own. Here are the city's loudest forges, a hall of the Explorers' League, and the entrance to the Deeprun Tram, which runs beneath the mountains to Ironforge. The district is a sign of the old friendship between the two kingdoms. Its smiths say, not quietly, that the best steel in Stormwind is made on their street.

lines.text: Mage Quarter.
lines.title: Mage Quarter

lines.index: #section:The Mage Quarter lies in the south-west of Stormwind, where violet roofs rise above the canals. The Wizard's Sanctum stands at its heart, and there the mages of the city train their students in the arcane. Not all magic here is lawful. Under the tavern called the Slaughtered Lamb, warlocks meet in a cellar and study powers that the Church condemns. Near the quarter, beside the canals, stands the grim gate of the Stockade, where the guards have been pushed back to the door by their own prisoners.

lines.index: #section:The Park.
lines.text: The Park.
lines.title: The Park

lines.index: #section:The Park is a green quarter in the north-west of Stormwind. Old trees stand between quiet paths. It is the calmest place in a crowded city, and it lies close beneath the walls of Stormwind Keep. The townsfolk come here to rest, to walk and to talk. Roy Lewells keeps a book club nearby. Its members meet in a cellar after hours to argue about history and ideas, with books borrowed from the Royal Library, and with refreshments that Roy is happy to share with those who help him.

lines.title: Stormwind Keep

lines.index: #section:Stormwind Keep stands at the northern end of the city, the seat of the kings of the house of Wrynn. Its throne room is guarded day and night. There the young King Anduin sits beside Highlord Bolvar Fordragon, and Lady Katrana Prestor attends upon them both. The Keep also holds the Royal Library, the offices of the city guard and a walled garden where the lords of the court walk. Not every conversation in that garden is meant for loyal ears.

lines.index: #section:Stormwind Harbor.
lines.text: Stormwind Harbor.
lines.title: Stormwind Harbor

lines.index: #section:The harbor of Stormwind has grown busy again. A new vessel now crosses the sea from its southern dock to Auberdine on the shores of Darkshore, and it carries supplies, letters and travellers between the kingdom and the lands of the night elves. Clerks count cargo by the crate, and there are never enough dockhands. Guards and cannoneers watch the water. Merchants of the city have already sent kin across the water to trade in Auberdine, and letters come back the other way asking for help. For the first time in years, the city looks outward across the sea.

lines.index: #section:Valley of Heroes.
lines.text: Valley of Heroes.
lines.title: Valley of Heroes

lines.index: #section:The Valley of Heroes is the grand approach to Stormwind. The road from Elwynn Forest crosses a long bridge and passes between tall statues before it reaches the city's main gate. Every traveller who comes to Stormwind by land walks beneath them. The city guard keeps close watch here, for the gate is the first defense of the capital and the first thing its visitors see. Messengers of the kingdom's far marshals arrive here, and squires carry their news from the gate to the throne room.

lines.text: Cathedral of Light.
lines.title: Cathedral of Light

lines.index: #section:The Cathedral of Light is the greatest house of the Holy Light in the Kingdom of Stormwind. It rises above Cathedral Square in the heart of the city. Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church from its halls. Priests teach the faithful there, and in its side chambers Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker trains the paladins of the realm.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The Cathedral does more than pray. Holy things are brought here to be kept safe, and cursed things are brought here to be cleansed. When the cursed Eye of Paleth was recovered, it was carried to the Archbishop. When a small statue of King Terenas Menethil was found in the Wetlands, the Light seemed to gather about it, and it too was sent to the Cathedral for safekeeping. The faithful of Stormwind trust that what enters the Cathedral will be guarded well.

lines.index: #section:Varian Wrynn. The Missing King of Stormwind.
lines.text: Varian Wrynn. The Missing King of Stormwind.
lines.title: Varian Wrynn

lines.index: #section:Varian Wrynn is the King of Stormwind, son of King Llane Wrynn and father of the young Anduin. He saw his father's kingdom burn when he was a boy, grew to manhood in exile, and came home to rule a city rebuilt from its ashes. Now he is gone. He set out on a diplomatic journey and never returned, and no word of him has reached his court.
lines.text: Varian Wrynn is the King of Stormwind, son of King Llane Wrynn and father of the young Anduin. He saw his father's kingdom burn when he was a boy, grew to manhood in exile, and came home to rule a city rebuilt from its ashes. Now he is gone. He set out on a diplomatic journey and never returned, and no word of him has reached his court.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Varian's absence shapes all of Stormwind. A child holds his title. A regent governs in his name. His army is far away, his roads are unsafe, and his nobles quarrel in the halls of the Keep. Every loyal subject of the kingdom asks the same question, and no one at court can answer it: where is the king? Until he returns, Stormwind must be held by those who stood beside his throne.

lines.index: #section:Anduin Wrynn is the only son of King Varian and Queen Tiffin. He is still a child, yet with his father gone he holds the title of King of Stormwind. He stands in the throne room of the Keep among grown men in armor and ladies of the court, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs in his name.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Anduin is the future of the house of Wrynn and the living hope of his kingdom. As long as he stands in the throne room, the people of Stormwind can believe that their line of kings is unbroken. He was named for Sir Anduin Lothar, the champion who saved his father as a boy and carried him out of the burning city. The boy's place is a strange one. He holds the highest title in the realm, yet the decisions of the realm are made by others. Every petitioner who enters the throne room bows before him. Few of them speak to him. They speak to the regent at his side, and to the lady of the court who stands near them both. Anduin sees and hears all of it.

Among them, none is heard more often than Lady Katrana Prestor.

Windsor fell, and the dragon fled. What she left behind was a shaken regent and a court that could no longer trust its own.

lines.index: #section:In a court without a king, the counsel of a trusted advisor carries the weight of law. Lady Prestor's voice is heard on every great question of the realm: what the kingdom can spare, whom it should believe, and which of its troubles can safely be ignored. Some in the kingdom admire her wisdom. Others, far from the capital, have begun to wonder why their pleas so rarely find an answer. She is always present. When the regent receives a petition, she is at his side. When a report comes for the absent king, it is she who takes it. When the regent must decide, he asks for her counsel first. No lord of the House of Nobles has so close a place at the heart of the kingdom.

Onyxia fled, and she left Bolvar to learn how long he had been her puppet.

lines.index: #section:Ironforge.
lines.text: Ironforge.
lines.title: Ironforge

lines.index: #section:Ironforge is the capital of the Kingdom of Ironforge and the oldest city of the dwarves. It is carved into the heart of a mountain in Dun Morogh, and even the Horde at the height of its power could not take it. At its center the fires of the Great Forge burn day and night, and the rivers of molten metal that feed them light the whole city in red and gold. Around the forge lie the halls of commerce, scholarship, magic and war, and beneath the throne lie older halls still.

Around the forge lie the halls of commerce, scholarship, magic and war, and beneath the throne lie older halls still.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The dwarves hold that Ironforge is their first home, and that their people were shaped from the stone of these mountains in ages past. No chronicle records the year when its first halls were hewn. For long ages all dwarves were ruled from Ironforge by a single high king. When he died, the Bronzebeard, Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans fought for his throne. The Bronzebeards held the city, and when the Dark Irons came back to take it, they were broken before its gates.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:King Magni Bronzebeard rules from the High Seat, with the Senate of Ironforge beside him and not always in agreement with him. Much of his army is far away, serving the Alliance. His brother Muradin Bronzebeard was lost in the north, and his brother Brann Bronzebeard roams the world. His daughter Moira is gone, and he believes the Dark Iron emperor took her. The gnomes of Gnomeregan have lived in Tinker Town since their city fell, and their tinkers fill the halls with noise. Now the old sealed ways beneath the High Seat have been opened. Something has been disturbing the tombs of the thanes, and the Dark Irons have been found digging toward them.

lines.index: #section:• The Three Hammers. The Bronzebeards held Ironforge against their kin. A treaty tablet kept in the royal vaults records the peace that followed: signed by the Bronzebeards and the Wildhammers, and never by the Dark Irons. • The Second War. The Horde overran Khaz Modan, but Ironforge held out. The dwarves joined the Alliance of Lordaeron and fought until the Horde was broken. • The Third War. Muradin went to Northrend and did not return. The dwarves count him among the dead. • The Fall of Gnomeregan. When the gnomes lost their city, Magni opened Ironforge to them. • The Present Day. The halls beneath the High Seat stand open again, and the kingdom learns that its oldest enemy has been digging toward its oldest dead.

lines.index: #section:The Great Forge.
lines.text: The Great Forge.
lines.title: The Great Forge

lines.index: #section:The Great Forge fills the central hall of Ironforge. Molten metal pours from the heights into great basins, and around them the smiths of the city work at anvils that never grow cold. The heat and the light of the forge reach every ward, and its hammering is the sound that dwarves call home. Traders, trainers and messengers crowd its ring, and the gryphons of the city come and go from the terrace nearby. No other place in the city is so busy, and none is so loved.

Here stand the Vault of Ironforge, where the city's wealth and that of its visitors is kept under guard, the great auction hall and the inn of Innkeeper Firebrew. Merchants of every people of the Alliance come here, and the ward is loud with bargaining from the first hour to the last. Travelers who have been long on the road come to the inn for a warm hearth and a strong ale before they go on.

lines.text: Hall of Explorers.
lines.title: Hall of Explorers

lines.index: #section:The Hall of Explorers is the home of the Explorers' League. Its galleries hold relics carried back from ruins across the world, its library keeps the League's books and maps, and its scholars argue over the true origins of the dwarven people. High Explorer Magellas presides here. Advisor Belgrum, Historian Karnik and Prospector Stormpike keep their business in the hall, and news from the dig sites of the Badlands and Loch Modan arrives here first.

lines.index: #section:Tinker Town.
lines.text: Tinker Town.
lines.title: Tinker Town

lines.index: #section:Tinker Town is the ward that King Magni gave to the gnomes after the fall of Gnomeregan. It clatters with gears and hisses with steam, and its workshops are crammed with half-built devices. High Tinker Mekkatorque holds his court here in exile. From Tinker Town the Deeprun Tram runs deep beneath the earth to Stormwind, and the tinkers of Gnomeregan send volunteers back into their lost city to save what they can.
