It is a quieter place than the rest of Ironforge, far from the roar of the forge, and those who seek the higher arts find their teachers here.

lines.index: #section:The High Seat is the throne room of Ironforge, raised above the western halls of the city. Here King Magni Bronzebeard holds court, guarded by the Iron Kingsguard. Senators of Ironforge come and go on the business of the realm, and the Royal Historian keeps the memory of the kingdom close to the throne. A door at the side of the hall, long sealed, now stands open. Beyond it a path leads down into Old Ironforge.

lines.index: #section:Old Ironforge.
lines.text: Old Ironforge.
lines.title: Old Ironforge

lines.index: #section:Old Ironforge lies beneath the High Seat, the most ancient part of the city. For generations its gates were shut, and few living dwarves had walked there. Now the way stands open. A long path winds down through old halls to the caverns below, where the Hall of Thanes holds the tombs of the great dwarves of the past. The keepers of those tombs have heard strange noises from the vaults, and the dead within have begun to stir.

lines.index: #section:Magni Bronzebeard. King of Ironforge.
lines.text: Magni Bronzebeard. King of Ironforge.
lines.title: Magni Bronzebeard

lines.index: #section:Magni Bronzebeard is King of Ironforge and lord of the Bronzebeard dwarves. He is the eldest of three brothers, and the heaviest crown in Khaz Modan rests on his head. From the High Seat he rules a proud and stubborn people, bargains with a Senate that does not always share his mind, and keeps faith with an Alliance that has cost him dearly.
lines.text: Magni Bronzebeard is King of Ironforge and lord of the Bronzebeard dwarves. He is the eldest of three brothers, and the heaviest crown in Khaz Modan rests on his head. From the High Seat he rules a proud and stubborn people, bargains with a Senate that does not always share his mind, and keeps faith with an Alliance that has cost him dearly.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Magni is one of the pillars of the Alliance. When the Horde overran Khaz Modan in the Second War, his people did not forget who stood with them, and Ironforge has kept its word to humankind ever since. When the gnomes lost their city, he took them in. When the Alliance calls, his soldiers go. It is Magni's burden that each of those choices has been paid for by his own people.

lines.index: #section:• He leads the Kingdom of Ironforge and holds its seat in the Alliance. • He sends his army abroad to fight beside the Alliance, though it leaves his own lands thinly guarded. • He gave the exiles of Gnomeregan a home in his city. • He mourns his brother Muradin, lost in Northrend. His brother Brann is far away on the League's business. • He seeks his daughter Moira, who vanished in the Burning Steppes, and he holds the Dark Iron emperor to blame.

lines.index: #section:A King's Tribute. When the widow of Sully Balloo wrote to him, Magni did not pretend that her husband's death had been anything but a loss. He said that every dwarf who falls for the Alliance weighs on his soul. He could not bring Sully back, so he had the Grand Mason carve him a memorial of Lordaeron granite, in the hope that those who come after would remember for whom such soldiers died.

lines.index: #section:The Treaty of Understanding. From the Reliquary of Kings beneath Ironforge came a tablet of stone. Magni knew it at once. It was the peace drawn up after the war of the three clans, in the days of his ancestor Madoran, the first Bronzebeard to rule Ironforge. The Bronzebeards had signed it, and the Wildhammers had signed it. The Dark Irons had not.

He was glad to hear that its commander was dead, and gave orders at once for the breaches to be sealed and the lower halls strengthened. He also sent his warm regards to an old Wildhammer friend, Earthseer Farsen, and a demand that Farsen come and visit properly.

lines.index: #section:The Lost Princess. Magni wept when he spoke of Moira. He had sent his men to search the Burning Steppes, and the only clue they found pointed into the depths of Blackrock. He believed her the captive of the Dark Iron emperor, Dagran Thaurissan, bound by his spells, and he wanted the emperor dead. When the truth came back to him, it was worse than he had feared. Moira carried Thaurissan's child, and she sent word that the heir of Ironforge would be a Dark Iron. Magni could only say that even in death, Thaurissan had won.

lines.index: #section:Muradin Bronzebeard. Brother of the King.
lines.text: Muradin Bronzebeard. Brother of the King.
lines.title: Muradin Bronzebeard

lines.index: #section:Muradin Bronzebeard is the brother of King Magni. He was one of the mightiest warriors of Ironforge, a dwarf of great strength, blunt speech and a warm heart. In the Third War he went to the frozen continent of Northrend, and he did not come home. Ironforge counts him among its dead.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Muradin was bound to the house of Lordaeron by more than alliance. He had been a teacher in arms to the young Prince Arthas Menethil, and the two were friends. That bond made Muradin a witness to the prince's first steps toward ruin. It also cost him his life, or so it is believed in Ironforge.

lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He served the Alliance and was known in the courts of the human kingdoms. • He taught the prince of Lordaeron the craft of the sword and the hammer. • He led an expedition of dwarves to Northrend in search of a legendary runeblade called Frostmourne. • He fought beside Arthas against the undead in the frozen wastes.

lines.title: Deeds

lines.index: #section:Muradin's company had searched Northrend for Frostmourne for a long time before they met Arthas, who had followed a dreadlord across the sea. The dwarves and the prince joined forces against the undead. Muradin grew uneasy as he watched his old pupil. Arthas had burned his own ships so that his men could not go home, and his hatred of the enemy had become the only thing he seemed to live for. At last they found the blade in a frozen cavern, sealed in ice and guarded. Muradin read the warning carved there and begged Arthas to leave it. The prince would not. When Arthas freed the sword, the ice burst apart, and a shard of it struck Muradin down. Arthas took Frostmourne and went on without him.

In the halls of Ironforge his name is spoken with sorrow, and with the stubborn pride that dwarves keep for those who fell doing what they thought was right.

lines.text: Brann Bronzebeard. Explorer of the Explorers' League.
lines.title: Brann Bronzebeard

lines.index: #section:Brann Bronzebeard is the youngest brother of King Magni. Where Magni took up the crown and Muradin the hammer, Brann took up the map and the lantern. He is the most famous explorer of the Explorers' League, a dwarf who would rather sleep in a titan ruin than in a royal bed.
lines.text: Brann Bronzebeard is the youngest brother of King Magni. Where Magni took up the crown and Muradin the hammer, Brann took up the map and the lantern. He is the most famous explorer of the Explorers' League, a dwarf who would rather sleep in a titan ruin than in a royal bed.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Brann is the living spirit of the League's great question: where did the dwarves come from? He has spent his life searching the ancient places of the world for the answer, and his name opens doors that closed to lesser delvers. The League's scholars in the Hall of Explorers carry on his work while he roams.

lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He has explored ruins across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond in search of the dwarves' origins. • He is counted among the leading members of the Explorers' League.
lines.text: • He has explored ruins across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond in search of the dwarves' origins. • He is counted among the leading members of the Explorers' League.
lines.title: Deeds

lines.index: #section:The question that drives Brann is the one the whole League asks: were the dwarves truly shaped from stone by the titans? In his absence, his colleagues have come closer to an answer than ever before. From the depths of Uldaman they have brought back records of the titans' works, and those records point to still greater vaults in the deserts of the south. It is the kind of discovery to which Brann has given his life.

lines.text: Gelbin Mekkatorque. High Tinker, King of Gnomes.
lines.title: Gelbin Mekkatorque

lines.index: #section:Gelbin Mekkatorque is the High Tinker of the gnomes, the king of a people who have lost their kingdom. He ruled in Gnomeregan when the city was great. He rules now from a workshop in Tinker Town, a guest of the dwarves, with most of his people dead, poisoned or scattered. He has not lost his wits or his will. He means to go home.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Mekkatorque holds the gnomes together. Without him, the exiles would be a crowd of refugees. With him, they remain a nation, with a seat among the peoples of the Alliance and a claim to their city that they have never given up.

lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:• He led the gnomes of Gnomeregan as High Tinker. • When the troggs rose beneath the city, he turned the gnomes' own arts against them in a desperate purge, and the city was poisoned. • He led the survivors to Ironforge and made Tinker Town their home. • He sends volunteers back into Gnomeregan to recover what was left behind, and to strike at the traitor who holds it.

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records the year when the troggs came up from the depths beneath Gnomeregan. They came in great numbers, and the city could not hold them back. Mekkatorque chose to purge them with a weapon of the gnomes' own making. It killed troggs, but it also killed a great many gnomes, and it left the city soaked in poison. Many of those who lived were changed into sick and witless lepers. The rest fled into the snows of Dun Morogh.

lines.index: #section:In Tinker Town, the High Tinker's people have not stopped working. Tinkmaster Overspark hopes to repair his poor Techbot, whose mind was reversed in the fall. Master Mechanic Castpipe organizes parties to recover vital records from the city's terminals. Klockmort Spannerspan needs the parts that no one remembered to take in the flight. Every such mission is a small step back into Gnomeregan, and Mekkatorque encourages them all.

lines.index: #section:The Grand Betrayal. Mekkatorque had trusted Sicco Thermaplugg. He had never imagined that Thermaplugg would betray him and the whole gnomish people, and he still does not understand why, for power and wealth would have come to Thermaplugg in time. Now the traitor sits in the ruins, the king of nothing. When word came that Thermaplugg had fallen, Mekkatorque allowed himself a grim joke, and then turned his mind to the day the gnomes would take their city back.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Archesonus is the voice of Ironforge's past. The dwarves are a people of long memory, and in the High Seat that memory has a keeper. Her knowledge of the Dark Irons has become urgent, for the kingdom's old enemy is on the move again.

lines.index: #section:• She teaches the history of Ironforge to those who come to the High Seat. • She sends searchers to the ruins of Thaurissan in the Burning Steppes to read the relics left there.

lines.title: Deeds

lines.index: #section:The Story of Thaurissan. Archesonus begins far back, when the Dark Irons had a city of their own. Thaurissan stood in a green country that is now the Burning Steppes, and in those days the dwarven clans were at war with one another. Then a terrible blast destroyed it, and the land for miles around was burned to cinders. What caused the blast, she admits, no historian can say. The Dark Irons who lived went into the mountain and began again. From the ashes rose Blackrock Spire, and the Cauldron of the Searing Gorge was fortified. Soon there were whispers of an ancient evil that ruled the Dark Iron kingdom from within. Her tale ends in the present. The Dark Irons are seen more often on the surface every year. They have raised forts in the Badlands, sent great parties into Uldaman and even attacked the dam of Loch Modan.

Soon there were whispers of an ancient evil that ruled the Dark Iron kingdom from within. Her tale ends in the present. The Dark Irons are seen more often on the surface every year. They have raised forts in the Badlands, sent great parties into Uldaman and even attacked the dam of Loch Modan.
lines.title: The Story of Thaurissan

One of them alone at the end, kneeling amid seven dead before a pillar of fire. Archesonus heard these memories and said that they explained a great deal, and that there was much more to learn.

lines.index: #section:Undercity.
lines.text: Undercity.
lines.title: Undercity

lines.index: #section:The Undercity lies beneath the ruins of Lordaeron's Capital City, in the east of Tirisfal Glades. It is the capital of the Forsaken and the seat of their queen, Sylvanas Windrunner. Its halls were carved from the sewers, crypts and catacombs of the old city. Green slime flows through its canals, bats circle its vaults, and its four great quarters ring a central court where the Forsaken trade, scheme and brew their poisons. No city in the world is stranger, and few are better defended.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:The first tunnels were not dug by the Forsaken. After Prince Arthas Menethil slew his father and sacked the capital, he meant to rule the north from its ruins, and he set the Scourge to deepen the crypts beneath the city. Then the Lich King called him to Northrend, and the work was left unfinished. When the Lich King's hold weakened, Sylvanas broke free. With the dreadlord Varimathras bound to her service, she overthrew the demons who sought to rule the ruined kingdom, and she claimed the fallen capital for her people. The Forsaken went below. They gathered the free-willed dead from the ruins above and brought them down to join their ranks. A stonemason named Bernd, rescued from the ruins, led the laborers who shaped the new halls. Goblin traders followed, and opened the first shops of the Trade Quarter. The dead of Lordaeron had a home again.

lines.index: #section:The Undercity is complete, or nearly so, and it is full. From the Royal Quarter, Sylvanas wages war against the Scourge and against the Scarlet Crusade. Varimathras commands the city's defense. In the Apothecarium, the Royal Apothecary Society labors on a new plague that the Dark Lady has ordered. The city has joined the Horde and receives its orcs, trolls and tauren, who find it unsettling. Its people also remember a recent terror. Not long ago the necropolis Naxxramas came against the city, and the Forsaken fought it on the surface of the ruins. Many fell there, among them the captain of the Deathguard.

lines.index: #section:Trade Quarter.
lines.text: Trade Quarter.
lines.title: Trade Quarter

lines.index: #section:The Trade Quarter is the heart of the Undercity, a great ring of halls at the bottom of the lifts that come down from the ruins above. Here stand the bank, the auction house, the inn and the stalls of a hundred merchants. The Royal Overseer keeps the census of the city here. A goblin cuts the hair of the dead. Beggars wait in the corners for scraps, and apothecaries hurry past them on the Dark Lady's business. Every visitor to the Undercity passes through the Trade Quarter first.

lines.index: #section:The Apothecarium.
lines.text: The Apothecarium.
lines.title: The Apothecarium

lines.index: #section:The Apothecarium is the domain of the Royal Apothecary Society. Its chemists call it the most vital organ of the Undercity. Across a canal of green slime, in vaults full of bubbling vats and caged prisoners, they study the poisons of every land and brew the new plague that the Dark Lady has demanded. Master Apothecary Faranell rules here. His assistants stitch abominations together from whatever bodies can be found, and one of them turns captives into beasts. The city's alchemists also teach their craft in these halls, and potions that cannot survive a long journey are carried here at a run.

lines.index: #section:The Magic Quarter is the hall of the mages and warlocks of the Undercity. Some of them studied the arcane in Dalaran before the plague and lost none of their learning in death. The most powerful of these is the mage Bethor Iceshard. Here too are the portal masters of the city and a banshee who teaches the arts of the mage. The Forsaken of this quarter are shrewd and patient, and they seek out every scholar who has broken free of the Lich King.

lines.title: War Quarter

lines.index: #section:The War Quarter lies in the north-west of the Undercity. It is the base of the Forsaken military and the home of the city's priests, who serve the shadow now. Here the Undercity trains its fighters. Its halls ring with the clash of practice blades and the hammers of the smiths. Warriors learn their craft here, a weapon master teaches every kind of arms, and the smiths of the city work their forges. In these days even a trainer of paladins can be found in its halls, a sight that many Forsaken would once have thought impossible.

lines.title: Royal Quarter

lines.index: #section:The Royal Quarter lies at the deepest part of the Undercity, below the ruined throne room where Arthas murdered his father. Here Sylvanas Windrunner holds her court. Her dreadguards line the chamber, and Varimathras stands at her side. Her champions come here to receive her orders, and here the captains of the Horde gather fighters for the distant battlefields of Alterac, Arathi and Ashenvale. The banshee Sharlindra drifts in the chamber too. The Forsaken paladin Morbin Lightbane waits nearby, gathering what his people need to mend their dead.

lines.index: #section:Sylvanas Windrunner. The Banshee Queen.
lines.text: Sylvanas Windrunner. The Banshee Queen.
lines.title: Sylvanas Windrunner

lines.index: #section:Sylvanas Windrunner is the queen of the Forsaken. In life she was the Ranger-General of Quel'Thalas, the commander of its rangers. She died defending her homeland against the Scourge, and Arthas raised her as a banshee to serve him. She broke free, and she led the undead of Lordaeron out of the Lich King's grip. Her people call her the Dark Lady. They obey her, and many of them love her.

lines.index: #section:No one did more to give the dead of Lordaeron a future. Sylvanas made them a people, gave them a name and a city, and brought them into the Horde. She has also made them feared. Her war against Arthas is personal. Her war against the living is harder to explain, and she does not try to explain it.

She simply expected more such madness, and she warned the order that she might one day decide it was not worth keeping.

lines.title: Varimathras

lines.index: #section:Varimathras is a dreadlord, one of the nathrezim of the Burning Legion. After the fall of Archimonde, he and his kin tried to seize the ruined kingdom of Lordaeron for themselves. Sylvanas Windrunner took him captive and gave him a choice: serve her, or die. He chose to serve. He helped her cast down his own brethren, and he has stood at her side ever since, in the deepest hall of her city.

lines.index: #section:Varimathras is the Dark Lady's lieutenant and the master of the Undercity's defense. His agents and soldiers range across Tirisfal, and he sees to the enemies nearest home while his queen watches the north. That a demon of the Legion serves the Forsaken is a strange fact. Many of the Forsaken choose not to think about it. Those who do think about it know only what they have seen: that he has served his queen without fail since the day she spared him, and that he despises humankind as much as she does. His soldiers are told that he himself sees to it that the human race is wiped from Lordaeron.

lines.index: #section:Master Apothecary Faranell rules the Apothecarium. He oversees the most ambitious work of the Royal Apothecary Society: the new plague that the Dark Lady has ordered, a disease to bring ruin to the Scourge and, in time, to the living. His colleagues send him their findings from Silverpine, Hillsbrad and beyond. He is cheerful about his work in a way that frightens those who understand it.

Faranell had the head fixed to a new body, and when it refused to serve, he fed it a serum of his own making. He has many plans for Othmar's future.

lines.index: #section:Bethor Iceshard is a high-ranking and powerful mage of the Undercity. Before the plague he studied with the Kirin Tor of Dalaran, beside two friends, Gunther Arcanus and Thule Ravenclaw. Thule sold himself to the Lich King. Gunther and Bethor died of the plague. Bethor rose free, and he thought his friend had not.

lines.index: #section:Glix Xizzix is a goblin trader who came to the Undercity when it was young. His caravan was robbed by gnolls in Tirisfal, and the Forsaken won back his wares. In return he set up shop among the dead and brought them a line of supply. Now he runs a barbershop in the Trade Quarter. He calls it diversification.

lines.title: Morbin Lightbane

lines.index: #section:Morbin Lightbane is a Forsaken paladin. He believes that his duty is twofold: to carry out the Dark Lady's will and to tend his people's needs. Above the Undercity the Scourge still roam the ruins in great numbers, and the Forsaken who fight them are falling. Decaying flesh does not heal on its own. Morbin gathers whole limbs from the fallen dead, so that his brothers and sisters can be mended.

lines.index: #section:Darnassus.
lines.text: Darnassus.
lines.title: Darnassus

lines.index: #section:Darnassus is the capital of the night elves, a city of living wood and moonlit water in the high boughs of Teldrassil. Its halls are grown rather than built. Its terraces open onto gardens and quiet pools, and the Temple of the Moon shines at its heart. It is a young city of an ancient people. The kaldorei raised it after the Third War, when they had lost their immortality and their old home on Mount Hyjal lay scarred, and they meant it to be a new beginning.

The priestesses of Elune took up their temple there, the druids their enclave, and the Sentinels their barracks. From Rut'theran Village far below, a portal carries travellers up to the city.

lines.index: #section:Two leaders sit in Darnassus. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind rules the city and its people as Elune wills. Fandral Staghelm leads the druids in the long absence of Malfurion Stormrage, who has not returned from the Emerald Dream. Tyrande asks her people to respect his station, but she reminds them that the affairs of Darnassus are hers alone. Fandral, for his part, trusts no one outside his enclave. He and Keeper Remulos of Moonglade suspect each other of trickery, and the troubles of the World Tree go on unhealed. The Sentinels keep a sharp watch within the city itself, for something is amiss on Teldrassil.

lines.index: #section:Temple of the Moon.
lines.text: Temple of the Moon.
lines.title: Temple of the Moon

lines.index: #section:The Temple of the Moon stands among the Temple Gardens in the south of Darnassus. It is the house of Elune and the seat of the High Priestess. Tyrande Whisperwind holds court in its upper hall. Below, the priestesses teach the young and heal the wounded, and a fountain of holy water rises at its centre. Offerings laid in that fountain are given to the goddess. Sentinels guard its doors and pray there daily, for a huntress of Elune must wield her goddess's gifts as well as her blade.

lines.index: #section:The Cenarion Enclave is the quarter of the druids, in the north of Darnassus. Here grows the great tree of Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, where he studies the troubles of Teldrassil with his second, Mathrengyl Bearwalker, on the floor below. Druids like Rellian Greenspyre walk its paths. Hunters and rogues keep halls here too. Behind the Arch Druid's tree, piles of strange soil from distant lands wait to be sorted, and tunnels lead down into the depths beneath the Enclave.

lines.index: #section:The Warrior's Terrace lies in the east of Darnassus. Here the warriors of the kaldorei train under teachers such as Elanaria and Arias'ta Bladesinger, and here the commander Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps the affairs of the Sentinels. The belongings of Sentinels who have gone missing are stored in their bunkhouse until they return. A warrior who would learn more must first prove her resolve against the enemies of the tree.

lines.index: #section:The Craftsmen's Terrace lies in the north-east of Darnassus. lines.index: #section:The Tradesmen's Terrace lies in the east of Darnassus, between the gardens and the Warrior's Terrace. It is the market of the city. Merchants of food, cloth, arms and general goods keep their stalls along its winding paths, and news from the forest below travels quickly among them. It is the busiest place in Darnassus, and still quieter than any market of the human lands.

lines.index: #section:Tyrande Whisperwind. High Priestess of Elune.
lines.text: Tyrande Whisperwind. High Priestess of Elune.
lines.title: Tyrande Whisperwind

lines.index: #section:Tyrande Whisperwind is the High Priestess of Elune and the leader of the night elves. For ten thousand years she has guarded her people, first in the ruins of their ancient empire and now in the boughs of Teldrassil. She is the beloved of Malfurion Stormrage, and she waits for his return. She rules Darnassus firmly, and she is known to be kind.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Tyrande is the living bond between the kaldorei of old and the kaldorei of today. She fought in the War of the Ancients and in the Third War. Under her the Sentinels became the shield of their people, and under her the night elves have joined the Alliance.

lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:Tyrande was a novice of the Sisterhood of Elune in the days of Queen Azshara. The twin brothers Malfurion and Illidan Stormrage both loved her, and she chose Malfurion. When the Burning Legion came, she fought beside them, and she rose to lead the Sisterhood in that war. After the Great Sundering, while the druids slept in the Emerald Dream, she and her priestesses kept watch over the forests through long centuries. When the Legion returned and the humans and orcs came to Kalimdor, Tyrande woke the sleeping druids from their barrow dens. She freed Illidan from his prison, against her beloved's wishes. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, her Sentinels fought alongside humans and orcs until Archimonde fell.

lines.title: History

lines.index: #section:Malfurion has gone into the Dream again, and no one knows what has become of him. Tyrande leads the kaldorei alone. She respects Fandral Staghelm as Arch Druid, but she does not let him forget that his domain is druidism, while hers is the whole of her people. Her priestesses and Sentinels bring her news from every forest of Kalimdor, and she hears it herself. Those who come to her temple with deeds done for her people find her grateful and generous, and quick to ask them to share their tales with the young.

lines.index: #section:Fandral Staghelm. Arch Druid of Darnassus.
lines.text: Fandral Staghelm. Arch Druid of Darnassus.
lines.title: Fandral Staghelm

lines.index: #section:Fandral Staghelm is the Arch Druid of the night elves. When Malfurion Stormrage vanished after the Third War, Fandral took up the leadership of the druids and resolved that his people would rebuild. He grew Teldrassil, the new World Tree, and he labours still to make it whole. He is proud, impatient and tireless, and he trusts no one but himself to finish the work.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Few kaldorei have shaped the present age more than Fandral. Darnassus stands in the tree he raised. Yet the tree is flawed, the immortality he sought has not returned, and his quarrel with Moonglade divides the Cenarion Circle.
lines.text: Few kaldorei have shaped the present age more than Fandral. Darnassus stands in the tree he raised. Yet the tree is flawed, the immortality he sought has not returned, and his quarrel with Moonglade divides the Cenarion Circle.
lines.title: Significance

lines.index: #section:After the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Nordrassil lay smoking and the druids were without a leader. Fandral persuaded the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore that the kaldorei must rebuild and win back their immortality. With the Circle's approval, he and the mightiest druids grew Teldrassil off the northern coast. He then asked the dragons for their blessing. Nozdormu refused him and rebuked his arrogance, and Alexstrasza also refused. Without their gifts, the tree has grown flawed and unpredictable.

He hoped to grow a timberling from a seed to help his friend's work, but he found that the corruption passes from parent to seed. Until a cure is found, he says, the most tainted timberlings must be cut down and their tumors burned.

lines.title: Sentinels

lines.index: #section:The Sentinels are the warriors of the night elves. For thousands of years they have guarded the forests of Kalimdor, and they answer to the High Priestess of Elune. Most are women, huntresses who wield the gifts of the goddess as well as the glaive and the bow.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:After the Great Sundering, while the druids slept in the Emerald Dream, the priestesses of Elune and their warriors kept watch over the kaldorei. Through those long ages the Sentinels became the shield of their people.

lines.index: #section:Sentinels keep watch in every village of Teldrassil and on every road. They guard the Oracle Tree, carry its messages to Darnassus, and fight the Gnarlpine and the harpies. Beyond the tree they hold posts in Darkshore, Ashenvale and Feralas. General Feathermoon sees that each of them has time to pray, and in Darnassus they watch the city itself, for they fear that something is amiss.

lines.index: #section:Orgrimmar.
lines.text: Orgrimmar.
lines.title: Orgrimmar

lines.index: #section:Orgrimmar is the capital of the Horde, a fortress city in the mountains of northern Durotar. Its walls are of timber, stone and iron, and much of it is carved into the red rock of the canyons. Through its great gate pass orc warriors, troll hunters, tauren elders and the pale envoys of the Forsaken. At its heart sits the hall of the Warchief. The city bears the name of Orgrim Doomhammer, who died so that his people might be free, and it is meant to show the world what the orcs have become: not a war machine of demons, but a nation.

lines.index: #section:When the war against the Burning Legion was won, Thrall brought his people to the eastern coast of Kalimdor and set about building a home for them. He chose a site where the northern mountains would guard the city's back, and he named it for Doomhammer, his friend and teacher. The orcs did not raise it alone. The tauren, the Darkspear and the goblins lent their hands, and the city rose quickly, valley by valley. Even as it was built, the humans of Kul Tiras came to tear it down. They failed, and Orgrimmar stood.

lines.index: #section:Orgrimmar is the greatest city of the Horde, and its heart. Thrall rules from Grommash Hold, with the chieftain of the Darkspear and his old counselors at his side. Its markets are loud, its training halls are full, and its young warriors hunger for their first battle. But the city has enemies within its walls. The cultists of the Burning Blade whisper in the Cleft of Shadow, and beneath the city, in the burning caves of Ragefire Chasm, a sect of the Shadow Council gathers its strength. Thrall knows more of them than they believe.

lines.index: #section:Valley of Strength.
lines.text: Valley of Strength.
lines.title: Valley of Strength

lines.index: #section:The Valley of Strength lies just inside the great gate of Orgrimmar. It is the busiest place in the city. Here are the bank, the auction house and the tavern, and above them the tower where the wind riders land. Grunts watch every road. Travellers from every people of the Horde crowd its paths, and news from all Kalimdor passes through it. It is here, too, that the Horde celebrates its victories. The heads of fallen enemies are raised above the valley, and the overlords of the city call on the people to honor the heroes who took them.

lines.text: The Drag.
lines.title: The Drag

lines.index: #section:The Drag is a long and shadowed street that winds from the Valley of Strength deeper into the city. Its walls are lined with shops. Leatherworkers, tailors, alchemists and engineers work in its stalls, and the smoke of cookfires drifts between the awnings. It is a crowded and noisy place, and not every trader in it is honest. Those who seek a craft come here to learn it. From the Drag, paths lead to the Valley of Honor and down into the Cleft of Shadow.

lines.index: #section:The Cleft of Shadow is a dark gorge in the heart of Orgrimmar, where the sun rarely reaches. It is the quarter of rogues, warlocks and poisoners. The warlock Neeru Fireblade keeps his tent here, and here the Shattered Hand gathers in secret. At the bottom of the cleft, a passage leads down into Ragefire Chasm. The honest folk of the city avoid the Cleft, and those who live there prefer it that way. Many of the Warchief's secrets are kept here, and so are some of his enemies'.

lines.index: #section:The Valley of Honor lies in the northeast of Orgrimmar and belongs to the warriors of the Horde. In the Hall of the Brave, old veterans teach the young the ways of the axe and the shield. Hunters keep their lodges here, and the forges of the city's smiths burn day and night. The valley is loud with the ring of hammers and the shouts of those who spar. An orc who wishes to be known as a warrior comes here to prove it.

lines.index: #section:The Valley of Spirits runs along the southwest of Orgrimmar. It is the quarter of the Darkspear. Their huts stand among the orcish buildings, and their witch doctors, priests and mages practice the old ways of the tribe here. Young troll priests are brought into the circle of their elders in this valley. Its still pool reflects the red walls above. Of all the city's valleys, it is the quietest, and the trolls keep it so. Here the Darkspear remember the isles they have lost.

lines.index: #section:The Valley of Wisdom lies in the northwest of Orgrimmar, far from the noise of the gate. It is the seat of the Warchief. At its head rises Grommash Hold, and around it gather the shaman of the Horde, who teach the young to speak with the elements as their ancestors did on Draenor. The elders of the city come here to counsel and be counseled. It is a place of learning, and of power. Many who seek the Warchief's favor walk its road.

lines.index: #section:Grommash Hold is the fortress of the Warchief, built into the cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom. It is named for Grom Hellscream, whose sacrifice freed the orcs from the demon's blood. Its hall is vast and dim, lit by fire. At its far end, Thrall holds court from his throne. Vol'jin of the Darkspear stands at his side, with the old warrior Eitrigg and the far seer Zor Lonetree. The elite guards of the Kor'kron keep its doors, and none come before the Warchief without their leave.

lines.text: Thrall. Warchief of the Horde.
lines.title: Thrall

lines.index: #section:Thrall is the Warchief of the Horde. He was born the son of Durotan, chieftain of the Frostwolf clan, and raised a slave among humans. He broke his chains, freed his people from the internment camps and brought them back to the old ways of the shaman. He led them across the sea to Kalimdor and gave them a homeland. Even his enemies grant him honor.

lines.index: #section:Thrall made a new Horde from the ashes of the old one. Under him, the orcs are no longer the servants of demons, and the Horde is no longer only a horde of orcs.

lines.index: #section:Durotan and his mate, Draka, were murdered in the wilderness when their son was an infant. A human officer named Aedelas Blackmoore found the child and took him to Durnholde Keep. He named him Thrall, a word for a slave, and raised him to fight in the arena and perhaps one day to lead an army for him. A human girl, Taretha Foxton, showed him kindness, and with her help he escaped.

lines.title: The Slave

lines.index: #section:In the wilds, Thrall found Grom Hellscream and the last free clans. Among the Frostwolves in the Alterac Mountains, the old shaman Drek'Thar taught him to speak with the elements. Then he met Orgrim Doomhammer, and together they struck at the internment camps. Doomhammer fell in battle, and before he died he gave Thrall his hammer, his armor and his title. Thrall freed the orcs and broke the power of Blackmoore at Durnholde.

lines.index: #section:A prophet came to Thrall in dreams and told him to lead his people west. He did. A storm cast his fleet upon the isles of the Darkspear, and he saved the trolls from their enemies. In Kalimdor he won the friendship of Cairne Bloodhoof and the tauren. He saw Grom fall again under the demon's blood, and freed him, and watched him die slaying Mannoroth. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, he fought beside humans and night elves against Archimonde. Afterward he founded Durotar and Orgrimmar, and he made peace with Jaina Proudmoore of Theramore.

lines.index: #section:Hidden Enemies. Thrall will not tolerate traitors, but he will not strike at them too soon. A blow struck early would only drive the rot deeper. He needed someone young and unknown, who could go where his own agents could not. The insignia of a Burning Blade lieutenant, taken from Skull Rock, was the key to the enemy's door.

Thrall has long known it, and he lets Neeru believe he is trusted. The warlock is more useful free than dead, for through him Thrall means to find the Shadow Council and destroy it at last.

At Thrall's command both were slain, and none could say it was his doing. Neeru raged, and in his anger he told his false lieutenant of new plans in Ashenvale and the Barrens.

lines.text: Vol'jin. Chieftain of the Darkspear.
lines.title: Vol'jin

lines.index: #section:Vol'jin is the chieftain of the Darkspear and a shadow hunter of great skill. He is the son of Sen'jin, who gave his life so that the tribe might follow the orcs to a new world. Vol'jin keeps his father's oath. He stands at Thrall's side in Grommash Hold, counseling the Warchief and speaking for his people, while the Darkspear wait in their village by the sea for the day they can reclaim their isles.

lines.index: #section:The Darkspear were outcasts, driven from the jungles and scattered across the islands of the southern seas. When a storm cast Thrall's fleet upon their shores, the tribe was fighting for its life against humans and the murlocs of the deep. Thrall fought beside the trolls. Their chieftain, Sen'jin, was taken by the murlocs and did not return, but he had foreseen that the orcish warchief would lead his people to a new home. Sen'jin's son swore the tribe to the Horde.

lines.index: #section:After the war against the Legion, the Darkspear settled the Echo Isles off the coast of Durotar. Their peace was short. The fleet of Kul Tiras fell upon the isles, and Vol'jin had to see his people evacuated while the Horde struck back at the human ships. Then came a worse blow: Zalazane, a witch doctor of their own tribe, turned his magic against them. The free Darkspear fled to the mainland and built a village there, which they named for Sen'jin.

lines.title: Eitrigg

lines.index: #section:Eitrigg is an old orc warrior of the Blackrock clan who serves Thrall as counselor and overseer of the Horde's recruits. He fought in the wars of the old Horde under Blackhand and Doomhammer. He came to hate the demon worshippers who led his people astray, and for a time he left the Horde altogether. He returned when he heard Thrall's vision of a Horde guided by shaman instead of demons.

lines.index: #section:Neeru Fireblade is a warlock who lives in the Cleft of Shadow. Few orcs trust his kind, for it was warlocks who first bound the orcs to demons. Neeru claims to use his arts only against the demons. Since the last war, he says, he has searched out every trace of demonic corruption in orcish society, and he serves the Warchief in rooting out the cults that hide in his city.

lines.index: #section:Thunder Bluff.
lines.text: Thunder Bluff.
lines.title: Thunder Bluff

lines.index: #section:Thunder Bluff is the capital of the tauren, raised on a cluster of windswept mesas that tower hundreds of feet above the plains of Mulgore. Bridges of wood and rope swing between the heights, and every mesa is crowned with tents, longhouses, painted totems and spirit lodges. Great lifts of rope and timber carry travellers up from the grass below, and wind riders circle the central tower. It is a city of many tribes and a refuge for hunters, traders and artisans of every kind. From his lodge on the central mesa, the High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof watches over all of them.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:For countless generations the tauren had no city. They were nomads, and the centaur hunted them across the plains until their tribes were few and scattered. Cairne of the Bloodhoof dreamed of a land where his people could live in peace. With the help of Thrall and the orcs of the Horde, the tauren drove the centaur out of Mulgore. On the mesas at its northern end Cairne built a refuge where tauren of every tribe would be welcome. No chronicle records the year it was finished. Over time the scattered tribes came to it and united under his rule.

lines.index: #section:Cairne is old, but his strength and wisdom still hold the tribes together. Not every tribe agrees with the path he has chosen. On Elder Rise, Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone of the Grimtotem, keeps her own counsel and her own guards, and she believes that she, not Cairne, should lead the tauren. Beside her the druids of the Cenarion Circle tend their lodges under Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem. Emissaries of the Forsaken dwell in the Pools of Vision and teach on Spirit Rise, a sign of the pact that brought them into the Horde. The sages of the city are known across the Horde as historians. In these days new faces have come as well: priests of An'she, the sun, and Skyborne elves who pass through on their way from the camp of the Earthen Ring to Orgrimmar.

lines.index: #section:Elder Rise.
lines.text: Elder Rise.
lines.title: Elder Rise

lines.index: #section:Elder Rise is the north-eastern bluff of Thunder Bluff, the home of the city's wise ones. The druids of the Cenarion Circle keep their lodges here under Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem, with his daughter Bashana, the young druid Nara Wildmane and the teachers of the druidic arts beside them. In a lodge of her own, guarded by two warriors of her clan, lives Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone. The two elders share the same rise and seldom the same mind. Those who seek counsel on the troubles of the land, whether of spirits, dreams or the earth itself, are sent here.

lines.text: Spirit Rise.
lines.title: Spirit Rise

lines.index: #section:Spirit Rise is the western bluff of Thunder Bluff, where the shamans of the Skychaser family teach the young to speak with the spirits of the elements. It is also the rise of strangers. Priests and mages of the Forsaken have taken up teaching here, and a hidden path winds from the rise down into the cave of the Pools of Vision, where the apothecaries of the Undercity keep their work. In these days a paladin trainer has come to the rise as well. For many tauren, Spirit Rise is where they first meet the dead who are now their allies.

lines.title: Hunter Rise

lines.index: #section:Hunter Rise is the southern bluff of Thunder Bluff, the rise of those who live by the hunt and the spear. The hunters of the Thunderhorn family train the young to track and to tame, and the warriors of the Ragetotem teach them to fight. The great hunter Melor Stonehoof sets his hardest hunts from here, against beasts that live outside the Earthmother's blessing. From the rise's southern cliff the tauren scatter incense to the winds, as their tradition asks, and look out over the whole of Mulgore.

lines.index: #section:The Pools of Vision lie in a cave beneath Spirit Rise, reached by a hidden path. Still water fills the cavern, and the tauren hold it sacred. In these days the pools have become the home of the Forsaken emissaries in Thunder Bluff. Apothecary Zamah of the Royal Apothecary Society works here, receiving strange shipments and sending out others. It was to her that Magatha Grimtotem turned when she sought a cure for the sickness of Stonetalon, and the cure the Forsaken offered was a poison.

lines.text: Cairne Bloodhoof. High Chieftain of the Tauren.
lines.title: Cairne Bloodhoof

lines.index: #section:Cairne Bloodhoof is the High Chieftain of the tauren and the founder of Thunder Bluff. He was once the chief of a single tribe, the Bloodhoof, who wandered the plains near the Great Sea and lived in fear of the centaur. He is now the lord of all the tauren tribes and one of the great pillars of the Horde. Age has slowed him, but it has not bent him. He is a peerless warrior, a patient judge and a friend to those who honor the land.

Through him the Horde gained more than warriors: it gained a people of deep wisdom and old faith. In these days the High Chieftain still holds the tribes together, though not all of them agree with where he leads.

lines.index: #section:The Long March. Before the tauren had a home, the centaur hunted Cairne's people from one camp to the next. When the young warchief Thrall came upon them in battle, Cairne saw in the orcs a people as savage as they were noble. He told Thrall of the Oracle in the north. Thrall in turn swore to guard the tauren caravans across the Barrens, and the orcs fought off wave after wave of centaur until the tauren reached Mulgore. Cairne did not forget the debt. He followed Thrall to Stonetalon, and from that day the tauren marched with the Horde.

lines.index: #section:The Horn of Arra'chea. To Cairne, a place in Thunder Bluff is not earned once. It must be kept. He reminds each young tauren who reaches his lodge that their people are hunters, and he sends them down to the plains to track and slay the great kodo Arra'chea. When the horn is brought back, he sends a party to gather the hide and meat, so that nothing of the beast is wasted.

lines.index: #section:The Longwalkers. Cairne sent the Longwalker Perith Stormhoof to speak with the Palemane gnolls, and the gnolls took him captive. When the news came that Perith was safe, Cairne was relieved. He named Perith his most trusted scout and his mission one of the utmost importance, and he said no more of what that mission was.

He had driven the centaur from these plains beside Thrall, and he honored those who drove them out again, so that the centaur would remember the pain that awaits them if they return.

lines.index: #section:Magatha Grimtotem is the Elder Crone of the Grimtotem, a shaman whom many count the most powerful of the tauren, and one of the oldest of their elders. She dwells in a lodge on Elder Rise, attended by two warriors of her clan and by her servant Rahauro. Many come to her for counsel, and she gives it gladly. What she wants in return, few can say.

lines.index: #section:Magatha is the great rival of Cairne Bloodhoof. She has sought power and standing nearly all her life, and she believes that she alone is fit to lead the tauren. The warriors of her clan follow her, and they dream of driving the lesser races from Kalimdor. Yet she lives in the High Chieftain's city, sits among his elders and speaks for the Forsaken, whom she has helped more than any other tauren has.

lines.index: #section:• She was blessed with the gifts of a shaman when still a girl. • She became matriarch of the Grimtotem by an arranged marriage. Many suspect she arranged it herself. lines.index: #section:The Disease upon the Land. When word came to her of the troubled spirits of Stonetalon, Magatha said that the land could not be healed until the disease upon it was removed. The disease was the Venture Company. She turned to the Forsaken, saying that their knowledge of sickness would strengthen the trust between the two peoples. The apothecaries answered with a toxin, meant to spread among the goblins like a plague.

Magatha claimed it might show her how the tauren could help the Forsaken become human again. She was pleased with the work, and she promised Jediga her payment.

lines.index: #section:The Serpent of Vengeance. Magatha enchanted a powder that would summon Arikara, a serpent of vengeance, from the sacred fire of the Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. She warned that the serpent might be stalking Cairne Bloodhoof, angered because too much of tauren lore had changed. The tauren of Freewind Post could not understand why Arikara would hunt the High Chieftain. They did not doubt Magatha. She was, they said, their most powerful shaman.

One of her servants, Maur Grimtotem, died in Ragefire Chasm clutching a satchel. Magatha wanted it back, and she declared the troggs a threat to all the Horde.

lines.index: #section:Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem is the first tauren druid in many generations and the leader of the druids of Thunder Bluff. He was stirred by the druids who fought at Mount Hyjal, and after the war he sought out Malfurion Stormrage and asked to be taught. He is a member of the Cenarion Circle and a friend of Cairne since their childhood.

lines.index: #section:Hamuul opened the old ways of the night elves to the tauren. Because of him, druids of both peoples now work side by side, and his lodge on Elder Rise is where the tauren turn when the land itself falls sick.

lines.index: #section:The Druids of the Fang. The taint in the oases of the Barrens led to the Wailing Caverns. Hamuul entered the land of dreams and saw a cult of druids there, once noble, who had lost their way and now served the taint. He was old, and he could not stay long in the dream. Young Nara Wildmane stayed when he fled.

lines.index: #section:The Sage speaks for the tauren who doubt the pact with the dead. He believes that the Earthen Ring meant well when it urged the Horde to help them, but he wonders who was whispering in the ears of its Elder Council. He also stands at the edge of a deeper mystery, one that reaches back to the makers of the world.

lines.index: #section:Compendium of the Fallen. The Forsaken have a history full of deceit, the Sage says, and the pact was made too quickly. Perhaps Cairne should have heeded the warnings from Orgrimmar. The zealots of the Scarlet Crusade are mad, but they have studied the undead, and Truthseeker wanted to know what they had learned. He had begun to wonder if their book existed at all.

She has travelled far, and has stood before the sealed gates of Uldum in the south.

lines.index: #section:The Grimtotem are a tauren clan unlike the others. Where most tauren seek harmony with the land, the Grimtotem seek to master it. They believe that the lesser races should be driven from Kalimdor and that the tauren should take back the lands of their ancestors. Their matriarch is Magatha, the Elder Crone, and their warriors follow her.

lines.index: #section:The Deadmines.
lines.text: The Deadmines.
lines.title: The Deadmines

lines.index: #section:The Deadmines lie beneath the village of Moonbrook in Westfall. Once they were the richest gold works in the human lands. Now they are the secret heart of the Defias Brotherhood. In their depths, the stonemasons of Edwin VanCleef and the goblins they have hired are building something that no one in Stormwind has yet seen: a great warship, hidden in a sea cave at the bottom of the mines.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:For generations the mines beneath Moonbrook sent gold to the treasury of the Kingdom of Stormwind. When the Horde razed Stormwind in the First War, the miners fled and the works fell silent. The tunnels were left to the dark, and folk began to call them the Deadmines. They remained empty through the years of exile and rebuilding. When the betrayed masons came west, they found a fortress already dug for them.

lines.index: #section:The Brotherhood has made the old mine its sanctum. Defias miners dig in its shafts, and wizards and evokers of the Brotherhood guard its halls. Goblin craftsmen and engineers of the Brotherhood's hire cut timber, smelt metal and assemble machines. An ogre keeps the first gate. Far below, where the tunnels open onto the sea, the ship is nearly ready, and its captain and crew wait for their master's command. What VanCleef means to do with it, only the Brotherhood knows. Many fear that it is meant for Stormwind.

lines.index: #section:Ironclad Cove is a vast sea cave at the bottom of the Deadmines, where the tunnels of the old gold works break through to the Great Sea. Here the Defias Brotherhood keeps its greatest secret. A warship rides at anchor on the dark water, built from timber cut in the Mast Room and metal smelted in the Foundry. Pirates of the Brotherhood crew her. From her upper deck Edwin VanCleef commands his whole Brotherhood, and it is here that he has made his stand.

lines.index: #section:Edwin VanCleef. Kingpin of the Defias Brotherhood.
lines.text: Edwin VanCleef. Kingpin of the Defias Brotherhood.
lines.title: Edwin VanCleef

lines.index: #section:Edwin VanCleef was the master of the Stonemasons' Guild of Stormwind. It was his guild that raised the capital again from the ashes of the First War. When the work was done, the House of Nobles refused to pay the masons what they were owed. VanCleef led them in revolt and left the city, swearing revenge. Now he is the kingpin of the Defias Brotherhood, master of Westfall, and from a hidden cove beneath the earth he prepares his blow against the kingdom that betrayed him.

When the work was done, the House of Nobles refused to pay the masons what they were owed. VanCleef led them in revolt and left the city, swearing revenge. Now he is the kingpin of the Defias Brotherhood, master of Westfall, and from a hidden cove beneath the earth he prepares his blow against the kingdom that betrayed him.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:VanCleef is the wound that Stormwind gave itself. He was a builder, not a bandit, and those who knew him remember a talented and industrious man. His Brotherhood was born of a real injustice. Yet his revenge has fallen hardest on the common people of Westfall, not on the nobles who cheated him, and it has driven the kingdom's own breadbasket to ruin.

lines.index: #section:• He led the Stonemasons' Guild in the rebuilding of Stormwind after the wars. • When some senior masons were offered posts in the government, he refused his own out of loyalty to all the guild. • He led the masons' riot, and fled the city at its end. Queen Tiffin Wrynn was killed in the chaos. • He gathered the exiled masons in Westfall and founded the Defias Brotherhood. • He took the Deadmines for his stronghold and hired goblins to build a warship in its depths. • His lieutenant, Bazil Thredd, was taken and imprisoned in The Stockade of Stormwind.

He called his guards to his side and fought, as Baros Alexston remembered him fighting in his younger years, without peer. When he fell, his head was carried back to Sentinel Hill.

lines.text: Wailing Caverns.
lines.title: Wailing Caverns

lines.index: #section:The Wailing Caverns are a maze of caves beneath the heart of The Barrens. Their mouth opens in a rocky hill beside the Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. Steam bursts from cracks in their stone with a long and mournful cry, and from that cry they take their name. Underground rivers run through them for miles, and from their hidden springs rise the waters of the new oases. Something has gone wrong in the deep. The beasts of the caverns have turned savage and strange, the water carries a taint that spreads across the plains, and the druids who came here to heal the land now serve the sickness.

lines.index: #section:Naralex still sleeps in the depths of the caverns, tossing in troubled sleep. Most of his disciples have been twisted into the Druids of the Fang, who wear the shapes of serpents and guard their master's slumber against all who would end it. Their four leaders, the Fanglords, each hold a gem of the dream. Deviate raptors, serpents and faerie dragons have risen from the nightmare to haunt the tunnels, and shapeless ectoplasms drift through the dark. The world above has begun to notice. The tauren druid Tonga Runetotem traced the taint of the oases to the caverns, and Hamuul Runetotem saw the Druids of the Fang in his own dreams. Nara Wildmane learned their faces and wants their gems. The Forsaken apothecary Apothecary Zamah seeks the serpentbloom that grows in the depths. The goblins of Ratchet want the essence of the ectoplasms for their drinks, and a thief called Mad Magglish has fled inside with a stolen bottle of old port. A few disciples of Naralex remain true. One waits within the caverns for anyone strong enough to help him wake his master.

lines.title: Naralex

lines.index: #section:Naralex is a night elf druid who came to the Wailing Caverns with a noble purpose. He believed that through the Emerald Dream and the hidden springs of the caverns, he could make the Barrens bloom again. He entered the dream and did not return. His vision of regrowth became a nightmare, and he lies in the depths of the caverns still, lost between sleep and madness. The nightmare flows out of him into the waters and the beasts.

From the body of the beast came a green shard in which smoke seemed to swirl, a fragment of the Dream that showed a nightmare.

But the Disciple cannot perform the rite of awakening while his corrupted brethren live. The four Fanglords must die first.

lines.index: #section:Ragefire Chasm.
lines.text: Ragefire Chasm.
lines.title: Ragefire Chasm

lines.index: #section:Ragefire Chasm is a network of burning caves beneath Orgrimmar. Rivers of lava light its tunnels, and the heat of the deep rises through its stone. It is reached by a passage at the bottom of the Cleft of Shadow. Few citizens of the capital know what lies beneath their feet. Those who do have reason to fear it, for the chasm is home to savage troggs and to a secret cult that plots the fall of the Horde.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:No chronicle records who first found the chasm, or how deep its tunnels run. The troggs came first. They climbed from the lava-filled depths and claimed the upper caves as their own. Then the Searing Blade came down from the city above, a sect of the Shadow Council and a sister to the Burning Blade. The troggs were too weak to drive them out, and the two now share the dark in uneasy hostility.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:The Searing Blade has made the chasm its sanctum. Its cultists believe themselves the rising generation of the warlocks' art, and they work to turn the loyal folk of Orgrimmar to demon worship. Three leaders command them: a felguard, Taragaman the Hungerer, a warlock, Jergosh the Invoker, and a satyr, Bazzalan. The troggs of the Ragefire clan still hold the caves near the entrance under their chieftain, Oggleflint. The chasm draws the eyes of the whole Horde. The tauren seer Magatha Grimtotem sent envoys to make peace with the troggs, and they were slain. One of her servants, Maur Grimtotem, went down to speak with them and never returned. Envoys of the Forsaken want two books of dark spells held by the cultists. Above all, the Warchief Thrall watches. The warlock Neeru Fireblade sends heroes down into the chasm, and Thrall knows exactly why.

To the cultists of the Searing Blade he is their master, and to the few in Orgrimmar who know of the chasm he is the head of the sect. lines.text: Shadowfang Keep.
lines.title: Shadowfang Keep

lines.index: #section:Shadowfang Keep stands on a dark hill in southern Silverpine Forest, above the hamlet of Pyrewood. It was once the seat of the noble Baron Silverlaine. Now it is the lair of Archmage Arugal and of the worgen he calls his children. Wolf-men prowl its halls, worgs howl in its courtyards, and the dead of the baron's household still walk the rooms where they were slain.
lines.text: Shadowfang Keep stands on a dark hill in southern Silverpine Forest, above the hamlet of Pyrewood. It was once the seat of the noble Baron Silverlaine. Now it is the lair of Archmage Arugal and of the worgen he calls his children. Wolf-men prowl its halls, worgs howl in its courtyards, and the dead of the baron's household still walk the rooms where they were slain.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:In the Third War, the wizards of the Kirin Tor fought the Scourge in the north. Every wizard who fell soon rose again to fight for the enemy, and the Scourge only grew. Arugal would not accept it. Against the counsel of his peers, he called upon beings from beyond the world to fill the thinning ranks of Dalaran. What answered his summons were the worgen. The ravenous wolf-men tore through the undead, then turned upon the wizards themselves. They laid siege to the keep of Baron Silverlaine, and it fell into shadow and ruin. Maddened by guilt, Arugal took the worgen for his own children. He withdrew into the fallen keep and gave it a new name: Shadowfang.

lines.title: Origins

lines.index: #section:The Forsaken cannot hold Silverpine while Arugal lives, and they have sworn to see him dead. High Executor Hadrec sent two Deathstalkers into the keep to learn its secrets. They did not return. The Kirin Tor have sent their own agent as well, and he fared no better. Both now wait in cells near the gate. Keeper Bel'dugur of the Undercity wants a book that lies somewhere in the keep, the work of a mage of Dalaran named Ur, who studied other worlds. At the Sepulcher, a dead archmage now claims that Arugal never made the worgen at all.

lines.title: Archmage Arugal

lines.index: #section:Arugal was an archmage of the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. In the Third War, when the wizards of his order died and rose again for the Scourge, he summoned the worgen to fight for them. The worgen slaughtered the dead, then turned on the living. Driven mad by guilt, Arugal took the beasts as his sons, seized the keep of Baron Silverlaine and named it Shadowfang Keep. From there his curse has spread across Silverpine Forest.

Every worgen of the Moonrage wore his shackle, and so did every villager of Pyrewood, who were human by day and beasts by night. From those shackles Dalar drew the power he needed to understand the curse.

He did not rest. His ghost walks the dining hall where he once feasted, among the dead servants of his household, and he turns his wrath on everyone who trespasses there.

lines.index: #section:Springvale was a servant of the Holy Light in life, and the Light has not wholly left him. He still heals his wounds with it, shields himself with it and strikes his foes down with the hammer of justice. It is a bitter sight: a defender of the keep, turned by death into one more guardian of Arugal's lair. He is not alone in that fate. Tormented officers stand beside him, wailing guardsmen walk the halls, and haunted servitors still keep the rooms of a lord who is gone.

lines.index: #section:Fenrus the Devourer. The Great Beast of Arugal.
lines.text: Fenrus the Devourer. The Great Beast of Arugal.
lines.title: Fenrus the Devourer

lines.index: #section:Fenrus the Devourer is the pet of Archmage Arugal, a worg of enormous size. He prowls the chambers of his master and guards them against every intruder. His bite drips with a poison that sickens those who survive it.
lines.text: Fenrus the Devourer is the pet of Archmage Arugal, a worg of enormous size. He prowls the chambers of his master and guards them against every intruder. His bite drips with a poison that sickens those who survive it.
lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Fenrus is Arugal's shield. Those who would reach the archmage must first get past his beast. When Fenrus falls, it is said, Arugal sends servants of shadow to take his place.

lines.index: #section:Wolf Master Nandos. Master of the Pack.
lines.text: Wolf Master Nandos. Master of the Pack.
lines.title: Wolf Master Nandos

lines.index: #section:Wolf Master Nandos is a worgen who commands the wolf packs of Shadowfang. His worgs and lupine horrors roam the upper courtyard, and he can call more of them with a howl. He loves his pack. When it is destroyed, his grief becomes fury.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Nandos is the last of Arugal's guardians before the archmage himself. Of all the Sons of Arugal, he is the one who keeps beasts of his own.

lines.index: #section:Deathstalker Adamant. Prisoner of Shadowfang.
lines.text: Deathstalker Adamant. Prisoner of Shadowfang.
lines.title: Deathstalker Adamant

lines.index: #section:Deathstalker Adamant was one of two agents that High Executor Hadrec sent into Shadowfang Keep to gather news before an assault. He was caught and thrown into a cell. His partner, Deathstalker Vincent, was not so lucky. Vincent's broken body lies in the keep, and whatever he learned died with him.

lines.title: Summary

lines.index: #section:Adamant is the Forsaken's key to the keep. Freed, he leads his rescuers to the courtyard and opens its door. Then he hurries back to Hadrec with his report.

lines.index: #section:Sorcerer Ashcrombe. Prisoner of Shadowfang.
lines.text: Sorcerer Ashcrombe. Prisoner of Shadowfang.
lines.title: Sorcerer Ashcrombe

lines.index: #section:Sorcerer Ashcrombe is a mage who answers to the Kirin Tor. He came to Shadowfang Keep and was caught, and now he waits in a cell beside a Deathstalker whom he calls scum. He scorns the worgen's locks almost as much as his neighbor.
